en: The *Sāmavedārṣeyadīpa*, composed by Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara, the Lord of Sacrificers:
[herein are contained] the seers (*ṛṣi*), meters (*chandas*), and deities (*devatā*) of the Vedic Sāmans.
For the prosperity of the Bhāskarayajvans, according to their lineage and other traditional criteria. ||1||
The calculation of the asterisms (bhagaṇa) of those [planets] observed by many sages is proclaimed by the sacrificer named Bhāskara, born in the lineage of Kāśyapa. 2.
Even when seen in the Pratihāra, the Ārṣeya, and the Kalpasūtras, as well as in the Śruti, the seer, metre, and deity of the original Ṛks and Sāmans [are to be known]. (3)
The notion of "this-ness" (idantā) and its quantitative measure (iyattā) are now investigated, in accordance with the Sāman of the Bharatas, the descendants of the Ṛṣis. 4.

"Remembering the names and lineages of the sages leads to heaven, fame, wealth, merit, progeny, cattle, Vedic splendor, and longevity according to the Smṛti"—thus it is said. Whoever remembers this becomes a guest for a thousand divine years with each individual sage.

"Being welcomed, greeted in return, honored, and worshipped, one then lives upon the fruit of one's study," and so forth. "Indeed, he who officiates at a sacrifice or teaches with a mantra whose *ṛṣi*, meter, deity, and *brāhmaṇa* [explanation] are unknown, either strikes a stump, falls into a pit, or perishes; he becomes worse off. His meters become exhausted in power (*yātayāman*). But he who knows [these] for every mantra reaches a full lifespan and becomes superior."

His meters become fresh and unexhausted; therefore, one should know these [names] in every mantra. He becomes a member of the assembly of the seers (*ṛṣis*); he becomes a member of the assembly of Brahman. He is glorified in the heavenly world; remembering, he is born again. Thus it is for him who knows this. Furthermore, by means of positive and negative concomitance (*anvaya-vyatireka*), as established in such passages as, "He who studies those [names] belonging to the seers becomes a purifier of the row for Brahman," the necessity of knowing the seers and others is demonstrated; thus, they are set forth in order within the *Ṛgveda* and *Sāmaveda*.

Regarding this, the author of the Nidāna first states: "Does the metre and deity of the *sāmans* exist? Or does it not exist? Gautama replied: "That which is sung upon a particular *ṛc* is its metre; that which belongs to that [verse] is its deity. Thus he answered. (1)
The seers (ṛṣis), however, differ for the Ṛgveda and Sāmaveda; there is no difference regarding the meters (chandas) and deities (daivata). ||2||

There are three sections: the Āgneya, the Aindra, and the Pāvamāna. For the Sāmans dedicated to Agni, Agni is the deity; this is the general rule. For those dedicated to Indra, Indra is the deity; for those dedicated to Soma, Soma is the deity. In specific instances, exceptions will be stated here and there. ||3||

Now follows the Āgneya section. Regarding the meters (*chandāṃsi*): for the first three sections beginning with "O Agni, come hither" (*agna āyāhi*), the meter is *gāyatrī*. For the next three sections beginning from the fourth, the meter is *bṛhatī*. For the seventh [section] beginning with "He offers" (*ājuhotā*), the meter is *jagatī*. For the eighth [section] beginning with "Agni has been awakened" (*abodhyagniḥ*), the meter is *triṣṭubh*. For the ninth and tenth [sections] beginning with "O Agni, most powerful one" (*agna ojiṣṭha*), the meter is *anuṣṭubh*. For the eleventh [section] beginning with "Many times you" (*purutvā da*), the meter is *uṣṇih*. For the twelfth [section] beginning with "Most generous one" (*pramaṃhiṣṭhīya*), the meter is *kakubh*. ||1||
Thus ends the Āgneya Parva.

Now, regarding the Indra-section: for the first twelve *anuvākas* beginning with "tad vo gāya," the meter is *gāyatrī*. For the eight *anuvākas* beginning with "abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ," the meter is *bṛhatī*. For the three [sections] beginning with "asāvi devaṃ goṛjīvamandhaḥ," the meter is *triṣṭubh*. For the three *anuvākas* beginning with "gāyanti tvā," the meter is *anuṣṭubh*. For "viśvāḥ pṛtanā," the meter is *ati-jagatī*. For "śrat te dadhāmi," the subsequent verses are *jagatīs*.

The two sections beginning with "indra suteṣu" consist of two *uṣṇih* verses; the section beginning with "abhrātṛvya" consists of *kakubh* verses; the two sections beginning with "svādorittha" consist of *pāṅkta* verses; the three sections beginning with "pari pra dhanva" consist of two-footed verses (*dvipadarcam*); and the section beginning with "trikadrukeṣu" consists of *aticchandas* verses. ||1||
Thus ends the Indra-parvan.

Now, regarding the Pāvamāna section: the four *anuvākas* beginning with "uccā te jātam" have the *gāyatrī* metre; the fifth, "punānaḥ soma dhārayā," has the *bṛhatī* metre; the two *anuvākas* beginning with "pra tu drava" have the *triṣṭubh* metre; the *anuvāka* beginning with "purojitī" has the *anuṣṭubh* metre; [the *anuvāka*] beginning with "abhi priyāṇi" has the *jagatī* metre; the [hymn] beginning with "indramaccha" has the *uṣṇih* metre; and the [hymn] beginning with "pavasva madhumattama" has the *kakubh* metre. ||1||
Thus ends the Pāvamāna Parvan.

Regarding the five Āraṇyaka sections beginning with "indra jyeṣṭham," they do not have fixed meters nor do they have fixed deities; the specific meters and deities for each will be stated in the section on the seers (ṛṣiprakaraṇa).
Now, regarding the Āgneya Parvan, the seers (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc*s and *sāman*s are stated in order:
for the *ṛc* beginning with "agna ā yāhi," Bharadvāja is the seer; for the first *parva* of its *sāman*s, Gautama; for the second, the *barhiṣya*, Kaśyapa; and for the third *parva*, Gautama. ||1||
The seer of "tvam agne yajñānām" is Bharadvāja; the seer of the Sāman is Sauparṇa. ||2||
For this verse beginning with "Agniṃ dūtam," Medhātithi is the seer; for the Sāman known as Bṛhadbhāradvāja, Bharadvāja is the seer. ||3||
For the [hymn] beginning with "agnir vṛtrāṇi," Bharadvāja is the seer; for the three Śrautarṣi Sāmans, Śrutarṣi is the seer. ||4||

Uśanas is the seer of the ṛc beginning with "preṣṭham vaḥ. Of the Sāmans, Uśanas is the seer of the first and third, which belong to Uśanas; Śirīṣa is the seer of the middle one, which belongs to Śirīṣa. ||5||
For the verse "tvaṃ no agne mahobhiḥ," the seer is Sudīti; for the two Sāmans, the Sāṃvarga and the Vārtraghna, the deity is Indra. ||6||
"Bharadvāja is the seer of the ṛc beginning with *ehy ū ṣu*; Śunaḥśepa Sākamaśva is the seer of those two sāmans, the Sākamaśvas. ||7||
Regarding the verse beginning with "ā te vatsa," Vatsa is the seer; and for those two Sāmans belonging to the Vatsas, Vatsa Kāṇva is likewise the seer. ||8||
The seer of the verse beginning with "tvāmagre puṣkarāt" is Bharadvāja; the seer of that Āgneya Sāman is Agni. ||9||
For the *ṛc* beginning with "agre vivasvad ā bhara," Vāmadeva is the *ṛṣi*. For that *sāman* belonging to Vādhrayaśva, Vaghyaśva Anūpa is the *ṛṣi*. |||10||
Thus ends the first section in the Āgneya [section].
The second section:
For the mantra "namaste agne ojase," Viśvarūpa Āṅgirasa is the seer (ṛṣi). For that Sāman, the Sāṃvarga, Agni is the deity. 11.
Vāmadeva is the seer of the Ṛgvedic verse beginning with "dūtaṃ vo," and Viśvamanas is the seer of the Sāman belonging to Viśvamanas. ||12||
The Ṛg verse beginning with "upa tvā jāmayaḥ" belongs to Bhārgava; Agni is the deity for the Sāmans Śvābhra and Auṣṭīya. (13)
The ṛc beginning with "upa tvāgre" belongs to Madhucchandas, the son of Viśvāmitra; the Sāman belonging to that [ṛc] belongs to Viśvāmitra.
(14) The ṛc beginning with "jarābodha" belongs to Śunaḥśepa; for the two Sāmans based on that [ṛc], Agni is the seer. (15)

The ṛc "prati tyam cārum" was [revealed] by Śunaḥśepa; of the *vārayantīya* sāmans, [the seer is] Bhṛgu or Śunaḥśepa. (16) The ṛc "aśvam na tvā" was [revealed] by Śunaḥśepa; of the *vārayantīya* sāmans, [the seer is] Bhṛgu or Śunaḥśepa. (17)
The seer for the application of the verse beginning with "aurvabhṛguvat" is Aurva Vaidhāraya; he is the seer of those two Sāmans as well.
The seer of the verse beginning with "agnimindhāna" is [its own] seer; for the seer of that sāman is Atri. ||19||
The seer of the ṛc "ādit pratnasya" is Vatsa Kāṇva; that of the sāman for one desiring the nidhana is Prajāpati. |||20||
Thus ends the second section in the Āgneya-purāṇa.
The third section: The application of the Ṛg-verses begins with "agnim vo vṛdhantam. The Sāmans for these are the Saindhukṣitas; Sindhuksit is the seer of all three. ||| 21 ||
The ṛc "agnis tigmena" is by Bharadvāja; Agni is the deity of that and its sāman. The third [sāman] is the Vāmadevya, for which Vāmadeva is the seer. ||22||
The Ṛg verse beginning with "agne mṛḍa" has Vāmadeva as its seer; for the Yāma Sāmans, Yama is the seer. ||23||
The ṛc "agne rakṣā ṇaḥ" has Bharadvāja as its seer; Agni is the deity of that sāman. ||24||
The ṛc "agne yuṅkṣva" is by Bharadvāja; its sāman is Agni. ||25||
Vasiṣṭha [saw] the ṛc beginning with "ni tvā nakṣya"; Viśvamanas [saw] that sāman of the Vaiśvamanasa family. ||26||
The verse "Agnirmūrdhā" belongs to Viśvarūpa (or Virūpa); and of the Sāman dedicated to Agni, [the deity] is Agni. |||27||
The seer of this ṛc, "imāmu ṣu tvam," is Śunaḥśepa; the seer of that sāman, the Somasāman, is Soma. ||28||
The Ṛg verse "taṃ tvā gopavana" was [seen] by Ātreya; the Sāman of that [verse] was [seen] by Gopavana.
The seer of the verse beginning with "parivāja pati" is Vāmadeva; the seer of that Sāman, the Sūryasāman, is Sūrya. ||30||
"udu ityā" is the Ṛc; Meghātithi is its seer. "tat sāmnaḥ" is the Kāva Sāman; Kavi is its seer. ||31||
Meghātithi [composed] the Ṛgvedic verses beginning with "kavim agnim"; Kavi [composed] that Sāman belonging to the Kavas. ||32||
The seer of the verse beginning with "śaṃ no devīḥ" is Sindhudvīpa; the seers of those two Sāmans, the Kāśītas, are Kāśīta. ||33||
For the verse beginning with "kasya nūnam," Uśanas is the seer; for the two Sāmans belonging to Gaurāṅgirasa, Gau, who is of the lineage of Aṅgiras, is the seer. ||34||
The verses in the three sections of the Gāyatrī.
Thus ends the third section in the Āgneya; now begins the fourth section:
the Bṛhatī verses.

The ṛc beginning with *yajñāyajñā* has Śaṃyu Bārhaspatya as its seer (*ṛṣi*). Of the four Sāmans, in the first two—the *aupāhana* and the *hava*—Bharadvāja is the seer. The third is the *śnauṣṭīgava*; Śnuṣṭīgu is its seer. The fourth is the *yajñāyajñīya*; its seer is Agni Vaiśvānara. ||35||

"Protect us, O Agni"—this verse has Bharga as its seer; among the Sāmans, the first is Kārtayaśa, whose seer is Kṛtayaśas. The second is Nārmedha, whose seer is Nṛmedha Aṅgiras. The third is Kārtaveśa, whose seer is Kṛtaveṣa. |||36||
The Ṛṣi of the verse beginning with "bṛhadbhir agne" is Śaṃyu; the Ṛṣis of the two Sāmans [beginning with] "pṛśninī" are Bharadvāja and Pṛśni-bharadvāja. |||37||
The seer of the verse beginning "tve agne svāhuta" is Vasiṣṭha; the seer of the Sāman of Uru Āṅgirasa is Uru Āṅgirasa. ||38||
For this verse, "agne jaritar viśpatiḥ," the seer is Bharga; for the two Sāmans, Paurumudgaya and Gautama, the seer is Purumudga. ||39||
The seer of the verse beginning with "agne vivasvad uṣasaḥ" is Praskaṇva; the seers of the two Sāmans belonging to the Māṇḍavayas are Maṇḍu and Jamadagni. ||40||
The seer of this verse, "tvaṃ naścitra ūtyā," is Śaṃyu; the seer of the Sāman, Gādha, is Bharadvāja. ||41||
The seer of the verse beginning with "tvamitsaprathāḥ" is Śaṃyu Bhārgava; the seer of the two Sāmans is Gautama of the Gautamas. ||42||
The seer of this verse, "O Agni, [grant] us life-increasing [strength]," is Śaṃyu Bharga; the seer of the Sāman, "O Agni, [grant] us long life," is Agni. ||43||

The seer of the *ṛc* "yo viśvā dayate vasu" is Saubhari; for the first two of the four *sāmans*, the seer is Agni Harasvant; for the latter two, which belong to Dīrghaśravas, the seer is Dīrghaśravas. ||44||
Thus ends the fourth section in the first chapter of the Āgneya Purāṇa.
The fifth section:

For this verse, "enā vo agniṃ namasā," Vasiṣṭha is the seer (ṛṣi). Of the four Sāmans, for the first two which are addressed to Agni, Agni is the seer; for the latter two, Gautama is the seer. Of the first two [of these latter], Gautama is the seer. ||45||
For the verse beginning with "śeṣe vaneṣu," Bharga is the seer; for the Sāman of Devarāja, Devarāja is the seer. ||46||
For the Ṛgvedic verse beginning with "adarśi gatuvittamaḥ," the seer is Saubhari; for the Sāman of Kauśika, the seer is Gādhi Kauśika. ||47||
For the verse beginning "Agni is placed in front at the hymn," the seer is Manu Vaivasvata; for the two Sāmans of Bṛhaduktha, the seer is Bṛhaduktha. ||48||
The seer of the ṛc "agnim īḷe" is Suditi or Purumīḍha; and the seer of the Paurumīḍha sāman is Purumīḍha. ||49||
Praskaṇva is the seer (ṛṣi) of this verse beginning with "śrudhi śrutkarṇa vahnibhiḥ," and Praskaṇva is also the seer of the Sāman belonging to Praskaṇva. ||50||
For this verse beginning with "pra daivodāso'gniḥ," Saubhari is the seer; for the Sāman known as Daivodāsa, Divodāsa is the seer. ||51||
The Ṛṣi of the Ṛc beginning with "adha jmo adha vā" is Medhātithi; the Ṛṣi of the Sāman belonging to Sukratu is Sukratu. This [verse] is addressed to Indra; its deity is Indra. 52.
For the verse beginning "kāyamāno vanā tvam," Viśvāmitra is the seer (ṛṣi) and Vaidyuta Agni is the deity; for the two Sāmans of the Kaṇvas, Kaṇva is the seer. ||53||
For the verse beginning with "ni tvāmagre manurdadhe," Kaṇva is the seer; for the two Sāmans [beginning] with "mānavayoḥ," Manu is the seer. ||54||
Thus ends the fifth section in the first chapter of the Āgneya Purāṇa.
The sixth section:
For the *ṛc* "devo vo draviṇodā," Vasiṣṭha is the seer; for the *sāman* "draviṇasya," Agni is the seer. || 55 ||
"May Brahmanaspati go forth"—of this Ṛc, Kaṇva is the seer; of the Sāman dedicated to Bṛhaspati, Bṛhaspati is the seer; Brahmanaspati is the deity. |||56||
For this verse beginning with "ūrdhva ū ṣu naḥ," Kaṇva is the seer; the deity is the sacrificial post being erected; and for the Sāman of Vasiṣṭha-vīṅka, Vasiṣṭha is the seer. ||57||
Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi) of this verse beginning with "pra yo rāye ninīṣati"; Aṅgiras is the seer of the Sāman belonging to Viṣpardhas Āṅgirasa. ||58||
For the verse beginning "pra vo yahvam puruṇām," Kaṇva is the seer; for the Sāman beginning with "aitavarddhi," Aitavarddhi is the seer. ||59||
Regarding the verse "ayam agniḥ suvīryasya," Kātyotkīla is the seer; regarding the Sāman, Neḍaścamana is the seer. 60.

For the verse beginning "tvam agne gṛhapatiḥ," Vasiṣṭha is the seer. Regarding the three *sāmans* [beginning with] *samanta*, Agni is the seer of the first, and Varuṇa is the seer of the latter two. ||61||
For the verse beginning "sakhāyastvā vavṛmahe," Viśvāmitra is the seer; for the Sāman, Āñjīgavi Dānava is the seer. ||62||
Thus ends the sixth section in the first chapter of the Āgneya-purāṇa.
Thus ends the three sections (anuvākas) in the Bṛhatī meter.
The seventh section: the verse beginning with "ā juhūta" is in the Bṛhatī meter; its seer is Vāmadeva. Of the Sāman, the seer is Śyāvāśva. 63.
For the verse beginning with "citra icchiśoḥ," Tvaṣṭṛhavya is the seer; the metre is Jagatī. For the two Sāmans, the Ṛtusāman and the Ṛtavaḥ, the Ṛtus are the seers. ||64||
"idaṃ ta ekam" is the Ṛṣi Bṛhadaktha for the Ṛgveda verses; the metre is Triṣṭubh. For the Sāman, "yāma," the Ṛṣi is Yama; for the Yajus, Agni. ||65||
For this verse beginning with "imaṃ stomaṃ," Kutsa is the seer; Jagatī is the meter. For the Sāman known as Yajñasārathi, Kutsa alone is the seer. ||66||
The seer of the verse "mūrdhānaṃ divo aratim" is Bharadvāja; the meter is Triṣṭubh. For the two Sāmans, Vaiśvānara and [the other], the seer is Agni Vaiśvānara. ||67||

For the verse beginning with "vitvadāvo na parvatasya," Bharadvāja is the seer (ṛṣi), Triṣṭubh is the metre (chandaḥ), and for the two Sāmans [named] Rāśvaya, Aśva is the seer. (Grāmageya 111–112) ||68||

Regarding the verse beginning with "ā vo rājānam adhvarasya," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi) and Triṣṭubh is the meter. Some say Rudra is the deity; others say Agni alone. Regarding the Sāman of Vāmadeva, Vāmadeva or Rudra is the seer. ||69||
"Indhe rājā samaryaḥ"—this *ṛc* has Vasiṣṭha as its seer (*ṛṣi*). The metre (*chandas*) is *triṣṭubh*. For the two *sāmans*, the Vaiśvajyotiṣas, the seer is Viśvajyotis. 70.
The seer of the verse beginning with "pra ketunā bṛhatā" is Triśiras Tvaṣṭra; the metre is Triṣṭubh. For the two Sāmans [of the] Yāma [type], the seer is Yama. |||71||
For the verse beginning with "agnim naro," Vasiṣṭha is the seer; the metre is the three-footed Virāṭ. For the two Sāmans, Rāśimara and Ayāsya, Vasiṣṭha is the seer. ||72||
Thus ends the seventh section in the first chapter of the Āgneya Purāṇa.
The eighth section:
"Agni has been awakened"—of this verse, Budha and Gaviṣṭhira are the seers; Triṣṭubh is the meter; for the Sāman, Prajāpati is the seer of the Śyena. ||73||
The Lord [is the deity] of the Ṛg verse beginning with "jayaṃtam"; Vatsa is the seer; Triṣṭubh is the meter. Of the Śukra Sāman, Śukra is the seer. ||74||
The seer of the verse beginning with "śukraṃ te anyat" is Bharadvāja; its metre is Triṣṭubh. The seer of the Sāman of Pūṣan is Pūṣan. ||75||
For the verse beginning with "iḍāmagre," Viśvāmitra is the seer; the metre is Triṣṭubh. For the Sāman of Kautsa, Kutsa is the seer. ||76||
The *ṛc* beginning with "pra hotā jāta" has Vatsapri as its seer (*ṛṣi*) and Triṣṭubh as its meter. For the two *sāmans*, Kaśyapa is the seer of the two Kāśyapas. 77.
For the verse beginning with "pra samrājam asurasya," Vasiṣṭha is the seer; Triṣṭubh is the meter. For the Sāman of Ghṛtāci Āṅgirasa, Ghṛtāci Āṅgirasa is the seer. ||78||
For this verse, "araṇyornihito jātavedāḥ," Viśvāmitra is the seer; the metre is Triṣṭubh. For the Sāman [of] Bharadvāja, [and] Prāsāha, Bharadvāja is the seer. ||79||
For this verse beginning with "sanādagre mṛṇasi," Pāyu Bhāradvāja is the seer; the metre is Triṣṭubh. For the Sāman that destroys demons, Vaiśvānara Agni or Atri is the seer. ||80||
Thus ends the eighth section in the first chapter of the Āgneya Purāṇa.
The Ninth Section.
The seers of the verse beginning with "agra ojiṣṭham" are the Ātreyas; the seer of the two Sāmans is Pantha Pāthya. || 81 ||
If the verse "yadi vīro anu ṣyāt" has Vāmadeva as its seer; for the Sāman "bṛhat" dedicated to Agni, Agni is the seer. || 82 ||
The seer of this verse, "tveṣaste dhūma ṛṇvati," is Bharadvāja; the seer of the Sāman, Yāma, is Yama. ||83||
For the verse beginning with "tvaṃ hi kṣaitavat," the seer is Bharadvāja; for the Sāman "Bṛhat" dedicated to Agni, the seer is Agni. ||84||
The seer of the *ṛc* beginning with "prātar agniḥ puruhūta" is Muktavāha; the seer of the *sāman* Bṛhat Kaumuda is Kumuda. ||85||
Regarding the verse *yad vāhiṣṭhaṃ tad agnaye*, the seer is Vasūyava, the son of Atri; for the two Sāmans beginning with *yad vāhiṣṭham*, Agni is the seer. || 86 ||
The seer of the verse beginning with "viśo viśo vo atithim" is Gopavana; the seer of the Sāman known as Viśoviśīya is Agni. ||89||
For the verse beginning with "jātaḥ pareṇa," Vāmadeva is the seer; for the Sāman of its own origin, Kaśyapa is the seer. ||90||
Thus ends the ninth section in the first chapter of the Āgneya Purāṇa.
The tenth section: "Somaṃ rājānam" (King Soma). Agni Tāpasa is the seer; Anuṣṭubh is the meter; the Viśvedevas are the deity. For the Bārhaspatya Sāman, Bṛhaspati is the seer. ||91||
Furthermore, for the verse beginning "uta eta udāruhan," Vāmadeva is the seer; for the Sāman "āruḍhavat" of Aṅgiras, Aṅgiras is the seer. ||92||
The seer of the verse beginning with "rāye agne" is Vāmadeva; the seer of the two Sāmans [beginning with] "asita" is Asita. ||93||
The seer of the verse beginning with "dadhanve" is Bhārgava; however, for the Sāman known as the Tvāṣṭrīsāman, the seer is Tvaṣṭṛ. ||94||
The seer of the verse beginning with "pratyagne harasā" is Vāyu; the seer of the Rākṣoghna Sāman is Agastya. ||95||
"O Agni, you [bring] the Vasus"—this verse has Praskaṇva Kāṇva as its seer; for the Sāman of Manu, Manu is the seer. ||96||
Thus [end] the Anuṣṭubh verses.
Thus ends the tenth section in the first chapter of the Āgneya Purāṇa.
The first section consists of eleven verses; the second, known as Purutva, consists of ten verses in the Uṣṇih meter.

The seer of the *ṛc* beginning with "purutvā" is Aucathya; he is the seer of the first two of the five *sāmans*, while Dīrghatamas is the seer of the three subsequent ones belonging to Dairghatamasa. ||97||
For the *hotṛ* [invocation] "pra hotre pūrvyam," Viśvāmitra is the seer; for the two *sāman*s "prahita," Śyāvāśva is the seer. ||98||
For the verse beginning with "agne vājasya," Gautama is the seer; for the two Sāmans, Śruddhaya, Prajāpati is the seer. ||99||

For the verse beginning "O Agni, most skilled in sacrifice at the rite," Viśvāmitra is the seer. For the first *sāman*, Prajāpati is the seer; for the two subsequent ones, [Prajāpati is the seer] of the *sadas* and the two *havirdhāna* sheds. 100.
The seven verses beginning with "jajñānaḥ" have Trita as their seer; for the Sāman of Tvaṣṭṛ’s hospitality, Tvaṣṭṛ is the seer. This verse has been extracted from the Pavamāna [laud]. ||101||
Furthermore, for the verse beginning with "uta syā no divā," the seer is Vainya; for the Sāman known as Ārka-jambha, the seer is Vṛka-jambha. ||102||
For the Ṛg verse beginning with "īḍiṣva hi," the seer is Vainya; for the Sāman, the seer is Agastya's Vṛkajambha. || 103 ||

For the *ṛc* "na tasya māyayā," the seer is Vaiyaśva; for the *sāman* "agastyasya rākṣoghnasya," the seer is Agastya, the descendant of Agastya; for the *ṛc* "vṛjinam," the seer is Ṛjiśvan Bhāradvāja; and for the *sāman* "rākṣoghnasya," the seer is Agastya. || 105 ||
The seer of the verse beginning with "śruṣṭyagre navasya me" is Viśvamanas; the seer of the Sāman known as Rokṣoghnya is Agastya. ||106||
Thus [end] the uṣṇihs.
Thus ends the eleventh section in the first chapter of the Āgneya [Purāṇa].
The Twelfth Section.
Now follow eight verses in the Kakubh metre.
The seer of the *ṛc* beginning with "pra maṃhiṣṭhāya" is Pra-maṃhiṣṭhīya; for the four *sāmans* beginning with "pra maṃhiṣṭhāya," Indra is the seer. ||107||
The seer of the verse beginning with "pra so agre" is Sobhari; the seer of the Sāman "vājabhṛtaḥ" is Bharadvāja. ||108||
For the verse beginning "taṃ gūrdhaya svarṇaram," the seer is Saubhari; for the three Saubhara Sāmans, the seer is Saubhari. ||109||
The seer of the verse "mā no hṛṇīthāḥ" is [the sage] Prayoga; the seer of the two *sāmans*, Pārthya and Saubhara, is Saubhari, the descendant of Subhara. ||110||
The seer of the three [verses] beginning with "bhadro no agnirāhutaḥ" is Saubhari alone; the seer of the Sāman "daivānīka" is Daivānīka. ||111||
Regarding the verse "yajiṣṭhaṃ tvā," Sādhi is the seer of the Sādhya Sāman. || 112 ||
"tadagre dyumnam" belongs to Jamadagni Sāṃvarga; Jamadagni Saṃvaga is the seer. |||113||
Alternatively, for the verse beginning with "yadvā u viśvapatiḥ," Viśvamanas is the seer; for the Rākṣoghna Sāman, Agastya is the seer.
Thus are the eight directions.
Thus ends the twelfth section in the first chapter of the Āgneya Purāṇa.
Thus, one hundred and fourteen ṛcas are in the Āgneyaparvan;
one hundred and eighty sāmans are proclaimed in the Āgneya;
and the seers, meters, and deities of all of them have been fully demonstrated.
The Āgneya Parvan is completed.
Thus ends the first chapter. 1.
The Second Chapter: The Indra Section.
First Section.

Now, in the section dedicated to Indra (aindra-parvan), there are three chapters (adhyāyas) and twelve sections (anuvākas). In the first chapter, there are eighteen verses in the Gāyatrī meter; Indra is the deity for all of them. Specific deities for particular rites of release (utsarga) will be mentioned in their respective places.
Regarding the verse beginning with "tad vo gāya," the seer is Śaṃyu Bārhaspatya; for the Sāmans, the seer is Rudra or Mṛgayu. ||115||
"O Śatakratu, he who is yours now"—this *ṛc* has Śrutakakṣa as its seer; for the *sāman* Āśvya, Aśva is the seer. ||116||
The *ṛc* "gāva upa vadāvaṭe" has the seer Haryata as its *pragātha*; the two *sāmans*, *raiṭa* and *iṭanvān*, have the seer Bhārgava as their seer. || 117 ||
For the verse "aramaśvāya gāyata," Śrutakakṣa is the seer; for the two Sāmans, Śrautakakṣya and Śrutakakṣya, Śrutakakṣa is the seer. |||118||

For the *ṛc* beginning with "tam indraṃ vājayāmasi," Śrutakakṣa is the seer (*ṛṣi*). For the two *sāmans* belonging to Tanva Pārtha, Tanva Pārtha is the seer. For the second [verse] of Dāvasu Vāṅgirasa—[his seer is Dāvasu]. For the two [verses] in the *niveṣṭau* of Vasiṣṭha, Vasiṣṭha is the seer. Or, the fourth *sāman* is the *saṃkṣāra* of the *iḍās*. 119.
"O Indra, from strength..."—this is the *ṛc*. The seers are the mothers of Indra, born of the gods. Of the three types of *sāmans* that are recited, the seer is the one who lies upon the bed. 120.

The hymn "The sacrifice magnified Indra" (*yajña indram avardhayat*) has Gauṣūkti and Aśvasūkti as its seers. The Sāman "The sacrifice magnified Indra" belongs to Indrāṇī; its seer is Indrīṇī. Regarding the two verses beginning "O Indra, if I were as you are" (*yad indrāham yathā tvam*), Gauṣūkti and Aśvasūkti are the seers of the *Gauṣūkta* and *Aśvasūkta*. (121–122)
For the verse beginning with "panyaṃ-panyam-it," the seers are Medhātithi Āṅgirasa, Priyamedha Kāṇva, and for the Sāman of Gaurīvita, the seer is Gaurīviti. || 123 ||
For the ṛc beginning with "idaṃ vaso sutamandhaḥ," the seers are Medhātithi Āṅgirasa and Priyamedha Kāṇva; for the three gāras of the sāmans, the seer is Gāra. ||124||
Thus ends the first section in the second chapter dedicated to Indra.
The second section:
for the *ṛc* "uddhedabhi śrutāmagham," Śrutakakṣa is the seer (*ṛṣi*). For the three *sāmans* belonging to Suparṇa, Suparṇa is the seer. 125.

Regarding the verse beginning with "yadadya kacca," Śrutakakṣa is the seer; regarding the Sāman of Śākala, Śākala is the seer. By means of these two verses, Indra is praised in the form of the Sun. (Grhya Pariśiṣṭa 207, 126)
The seer of the verse beginning with "ya ānayat parāvataḥ" is Bharadvāja; the seers of the two Sāmans, "ābharadvasu," are Ābharadvasu. ||127||
"O Indra, do not point [us] toward calamities"—this verse has Śrutakakṣa as its seer; for the two Sāmans, "tanva," the seer is Tanu. ||128||
Madhucchandas is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of this verse beginning with "endraṃ sānasim. For the two Sāmans, the Rohitakūlīyas, Indra is the seer, or alternatively Viśvāmitra. ||129||
For the ṛc beginning with "indraṃ vayaṃ mahādhane," Madhucchandas is the seer; for the two sāmans concerning Indrāṇī, Indrāṇī is the seer. |||130||
The seer of the *Ṛgveda* hymn beginning with "apibat kadruvaḥ" was Triśoka; the seer of the *Sāmaveda* hymn beginning with "sahasrabāhu" was Indra. ||131||
"O Indra, we [invoke] you with barley"—this verse has Vasiṣṭha as its seer; "of the bold Marut [hymn]"—the seer of this bold Sāman is Dhṛṣanmarut.

The seer of the second [hymn], *Ādarsṛt*, son of Bharadvāja, is Bharadvāja; the seer of the third, *Dhṛṣat*, son of Marut, is Dhṛṣanmarut; the seers of the fourth and fifth are Bharadvāja and Ādarsṛt, both sons of Bharadvāja. || 132 ||
The seer of the *ṛc* beginning with "ā ghā ye" is Triśoka; the seer of the three *sāmans* belonging to the Idhmavāhas is Idhmavāha. ||133||
"Bhindhi viśvā apa dviṣaḥ" (Pierce all our enemies)—this is the Ṛṣi Triśoka for the Ṛc; "Aheḥ paiḍvasya" (Of the serpent Paiḍva)—this is the Ṛṣi Ahi Paiḍva for the Sāman. ||134||
Thus ends the second section of the second chapter dedicated to Indra.

The third section: For this verse beginning with "I hear them even here" (*iheva śṛṇva eṣām*), Triśoka is the seer; for the Sāman (*aiṣa*), Iṣa is the seer; the Maruts are the deity; the Gāyatrī is the metre. ||135||
The seer of the verse beginning "ima u tvā vi cakṣate" is Triśoka; the seer of the Sāman (Pauṣa) is Pūṣan, and the deity is the Maruts. ||136||
For the verse beginning with "samasya manyave viśaḥ," Vatsa is the seer; for the Sāman known as the Marutāṃ Saṃveśīya, the Maruts are [the deities]. ||137||

For the verses beginning with "devānām id vaḥ mahat," the seer is Kusīdin Kāṇva. Regarding the four Sāmans, for the first two it is Haviṣmān, and for the latter two it is Haviṣkṛt. The Viśvedevas are the deities. ||138||
For the verse beginning with "somānāṃ svaraṇaḥ," Medhātithi is the seer; for the Sāman, Kakṣīvat Auśija is the seer; Brahmaṇaspati is the deity. ||139||
For the *ṛc* beginning with "bodhanmanā," Śrutakakṣa is the seer; for the *sāman* of the dawn, Uṣas is the seer. ||140||
The ṛc beginning with "adyā no deva savitar" has Śyāvāśva as the seer (ṛṣi) and Savitṛ as the deity. For the two sāmans [based on] the Maukṣya verses of Bharadvāja, Bharadvāja is the seer. ||141||
The seer of the *pragātha* verse beginning with "kvasya vṛṣabha" is Kaṇva; the seer of the three *sāmans* belonging to the Bhāradvājas is Bharadvāja. ||142||
For the verse beginning with "upahvare girīṇām," Vatsa is the seer; for the two Sāmans of the Śāktya family, the Śāktya is the seer. ||143||

For the verse beginning with "pra samrājam carṣaṇīnām," the seer is Irimbiḍha; for the Sāman, the seers of the first two [verses] are Vārṣāgira and Vṛṣaṃdhara, while the seers of the latter two are Kutsa and Prastoka. || 144 ||
Thus ends the third section of the second chapter dedicated to Indra.
The fourth section:
for the *ṛc* beginning with "apādu śipre andhasaḥ," the seer is Śrutakakṣa; for the two *sāmans* belonging to the Aupagavas, the seer is Upagu Sauśravasa. || 145 ||
The seer of these verses beginning with "imā u tvā puruvaso" is Bharadvāja; the seer of the Tvaṣṭrī-sāman is Tvaṣṭrī. ||146||
Regarding this, it is said: for the verse beginning with "goramanvata," Gautama is the seer; for the two Sāmans, the Ātithya and the Tvaṣṭṛ-sāman, Tvaṣṭṛ is the seer. || 147 ||
The seer of the ṛc "yad indro anayat" is Bharadvāja; the seers of the two sāmans [beginning with] "śyāvāśva" are Śyāvāśva.
For the *ṛc* "gaur dhayati marutām," the seer is either Bindu or Pūtadakṣa; for the two *sāmans* belonging to Śyāvāśva, the seer is Śyāvāśva. ||149||
The seer of the verse beginning with "upa no haribhiḥ sutam" is Śrutakakṣa; the seers of the two Sāmans, *Sutaṃrayiṣṭhīya*, are Sutaṃrayiṣṭha. ||150||
The seer of the *ṛc* "iṣṭā hotrā" is Vatsa; the seer of the *sāman* for one desiring offspring is Prajāpati. ||151||
The seer of the *ṛc* "Aham iddhi" is Śrutakakṣa; the seer of the *sāman* Raivata is Raivatya; and the seer of the Vājadāvarīs is either Prajāpati or [Raivatya]. || 152 ||
The seer of the verse beginning with "revatīr naḥ sadhamādaḥ" is Vatsa; the seer of the *nidhana* of the Sāman for one desiring progeny is Prajāpati. ||153||
Regarding the verse beginning with "Somaḥ Pūṣā," Pūṣan is the seer (ṛṣi); for the Sāman dedicated to Soma and Pūṣan, both Soma and Pūṣan are the deity (and the seers). ||154||
Thus ends the fourth section in the second chapter dedicated to Indra.
Fifth Section.
"Pāntamā vo andhasaḥ"—this is the Ṛgvedic verse; Śrutakakṣa is the seer. Of the Sāman, Vītahavya is the seer for the Vaitahavyas, or the third Sāman is the Okonidhana. Anuṣṭubh is the metre. ||155||

The seer (*ṛṣi*) of the verse beginning with *pra va indrāya mādanam* is Vasiṣṭha. Of the six *sāmans*, the first two are the *Śāktisāman*s; their seer is Śāktya. The third and fourth are the *Gaurīvitas*; their seer is Gaurīvita. The fifth and sixth have both Śāktya and Gaurīvita as their seers. ||156||
The two seers Medhātithi and Priyamedha are the seers of the ṛc verse beginning with "vayam ut tvā tad id arthāḥ"; for the two Sāmans belonging to Kaṇva, Kaṇva is the seer. ||157||
For the *ṛc* "indrāya madvane sutam," the seer is Śrutakakṣa. For the Sāmans, Gaurīvita is the seer of the first two; for the third, belonging to Śrautakakṣa, Śrutakakṣa is the seer. ||158||
The seer of the *ṛc* "This, O Indra, is your Soma" is Irimbiḍha; of the first two *sāmans*, the Saumitras, the seer is Sumitra; and of the third, the Ihavad-daivodāsa, the seer is Divodāsa. ||159||

For the protection [of the world], the seer of the ṛc beginning with *surūpakṛtnum ūtaye* is Madhucchandas. Of the four Sāmans, the first has Śākvara as its varṇa; its seer is Śākvara. The second is Raiṇava; its seer is Reṇu. The third and fourth belong to Audala; their seer is Udala Vaiśvāmitra. ||160||
The seer of the verse beginning with "abhi tvā vṛṣabhā sute" is Triśoka; the seer of the three Sāmans is Ṛṣabha. || 161 ||
The ṛṣi of the verse beginning with "ya indra camaseṣu" is Kusīti; the ṛṣis of the two Sāmans belonging to the Kautsa family are Kutsa. ||162||
The seer of the verse beginning with "yogeyoge tavastaram" is Śunaḥśepa; the seer of the three Sāmans known as Saumedhas is Sumedhās. ||163||
The seer of the ṛc beginning with "ā tvetā ni ṣīdata" is Madhucchandas; the seer of the sāman of Devātithi is Devātithi Kāṇva. ||164||
Thus ends the fifth section in the second chapter dedicated to Indra.
The Sixth Section.

For this [hymn] beginning with "idaṃ hyanvojasā," Viśvāmitra is the seer (*ṛṣi*). There are three *sāmans* belonging to the Aṅgiras lineage; their seer is Aṅgiras. Alternatively, the first is that of Mādhucchandas, the second is the Krauñca, and the third is the Ghṛtaścunnighana. ||165||
For the verses beginning with "mahām̐ indraḥ puraśca na," Madhucchandas is the seer (*ṛṣi*). The three *sāmans* are either the Vāmrāṇi or the Priyamedhāni; Priyamedha is the seer. ||166||

The seer of the ṛc beginning with "ā tū na indra kṣumantam" is Kusīda; for the first four Sāmans, the seer is Gaurīvita; for those two [first] Gaurīvitas, the seer is Gaurīvita Śāktya; for the third and fourth, which are Ākūpāras, the seer is Ākūpāra Āṅgirasa. ||167||

"Abhi pra gopatim girā"—this is the Ṛk of Priyamedha, the seer who has approached the libation. Of the three Sāmans, there are two Sāmans for the first two *dhurs*; the third is the Gaurīvita. The seer of the first and second *dhurs* is [the same]; the seer of the third, the Gaurīvita, is Śaktya. ||168||

Regarding the verse *kayā naś citra ā bhuvat*: Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*). Among the Sāmans, the first two are *vācaḥ sāmanī*; the third is the *vāmadevya*. For the first two, Vāk is the seer; for the third, Vāmadeva is the seer. |||169||
The seer of the verse beginning "tyamu vaḥ satrāsāham" is Śrutakakṣa; the seer of the two Sāmans known as Satrāsāhīya is Indra. ||171||
The Ṛgvedic verse beginning with "ye te panthā adho divaḥ" has Śrutakakṣa as its seer; the Sāman of Gautama Bhadra has Gautama as its seer. ||173||
For the ṛc "asti somo ayaṃ sutaḥ," the seer is either Bindu or Pūtadakṣa; for the sāman, the seers are the Aśvins. ||174||
Thus ends the sixth section in the second chapter dedicated to Indra.
The Seventh Section.

The verses beginning with "īkṣayantīrapasyuvaḥ" are the mothers of Indra and sisters of the gods; they are the seers of the Sāman, specifically of the Tvaṣṭrīya-sāman; the seer of the Tvaṣṭrīya is [the same]. || 175 ||
For the *ṛc* "nakiḥ devā" the seer is Godhā; for the *sāman* as well, it is Godhā. ||176||
The seer of the verse beginning with "doṣo āgād bṛhatī" is Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa; the seer of the Sāman of Savitṛ is Savitṛ himself; and he is also its deity. || 177 ||
For this verse, "eṣo uṣā apūrvyā," the seer is Praskaṇva; for the Sāman pertaining to the Dawn, the seer is Uṣas; the deity is Savitṛ. |||178||
For the ṛc beginning with "indro dadhīco asthabhiḥ," the seer is Gautama; for the two Sāmans, "tvaṣṭuḥ" and "ātithyayoḥ," the seer is Tvaṣṭṛ. || 179 ||
For the *ṛc* "indrehi matsyandhasaḥ," Madhucchandas is the seer (*ṛṣi*). For the *sāman* of Pūṣan, Pūṣan is the seer. (180)
"Come then to us, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra"—Vatsa is the seer of this Ṛc. For the Sāman "Indrasya māyā," Indra is the seer. 181.

For the verse beginning "ojasastadasya titviṣe," Vatsa is the seer (ṛṣi). For the two verses beginning with "saṃnorindrasya sāṃvartayoḥ," Indra is the seer; [and] Saṃvarta Āṅgirasa is [the seer]. 182.
The seer of this hymn beginning with "ayamu te samatasi" is Śunaḥśepa; the seer of the Sāman known as the Śaunaḥśepa is also Śunaḥśepa. ||183||

The verse beginning with "May Vāta breathe forth healing" has Vātāyana Ula as the seer (*ṛṣi*) and Vāyu as the deity. Of the *sāman* [beginning with] "pratīcīneḍaṃkāśīta," Kāśīta is the seer. || 184 ||
Thus ends the seventh section in the second chapter dedicated to Indra.

Regarding the verse beginning with "yaṃ rakṣanti pracetasaḥ," Kaṇva is the seer (ṛṣi); the Ādityas, headed by Mitra and Varuṇa, are the deities; for the Sāman known as Saumitra, Sumitra is the seer. ||185||
The seer of the *ṛc* "gavyo ṣu no yathā purā" is Vaṃśa; the seers of the two *sāmans* belonging to Śyāvāśva are Śyāvāśva. || 186 ||
These *pṛśni* verses are for you, O Indra; Vatsa is the seer. Of the *sāman* Śaikhāṇḍina, Śikhaṇḍī is the seer. || 187 ||
The seer of the *ṛc* "Ayā dhiyā ca gavyayā" is Śrutakakṣa; the seer of the *sāman* of Vītahavya is Vītahavya. || 188 ||
For the verse beginning "pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī," Madhucchandas is the seer (ṛṣi) and Sarasvatī is the deity; for the Sāman of Bhāradvāja, Bharadvāja is the seer. ||189||
The seer of the verse beginning "Who [is] among the Nahuṣīs? is Vāmadeva; the seer of the Sāman of Āruṇa Vaitahavya is Aruṇa Vītahavya. || 190 ||
"Come hither, for we have pressed [the soma] for you"—this verse has Irimbiḍha as its seer; of the Saubhara Sāman, Subhari is the seer. ||191||
The verse beginning with "mahi trīṇām avaras tu" has Satyadhṛti Vāruṇi as the seer (ṛṣi) and Mitra and Varuṇa as the deities (devatā). For the two *pāṣṭhauhī* sāmans, Paṣṭhavāh is the seer. ||192||
The seer of the verse beginning with "tvāvataḥ puruvaso" is Vaṃśa; the seer of the Sāman "dhurāṃsākamaśvasya" is Sākamaśva. ||193||
Thus ends the eighth section in the second chapter dedicated to Indra.
"Having lifted [the ladle], let the Soma juices exhilarate"—this is the verse; Gādha is its seer. For the *Sāman* known as *Yāma*, Yama is the seer. ||194||
For the *ṛc* "O lover of songs (*girvaṇas*), drink our pressed [soma]," Viśvāmitra is the seer (*ṛṣi*). For the *sāman* of Āṅgirasa with the *nidhana* "hariśrī," Aṅgiras is the seer. || 195 ||
The seer of the verse beginning with "sadā va indra" is Vāmadeva; the seer of the Vairūpa Sāman is Virūpāṅgiras. || 196 ||
For the *ṛc* "ā tvā viśantvindavaḥ," the seer is Śrutakakṣa; for the *sāman*, the seer is Asita Sindhuṣāman. || 197 ||
For this verse beginning with "indramid gāthino bṛhat," Madhucchandas is the seer; for the Sāman, the Ṛk, and the Yama, Yama is the seer. || 198 ||
"May Indra grant us nourishment"—this is the Ṛgvedic verse; its seer is Śrutakakṣa. Of the two Sāmans belonging to Saumitra, the seer is Sumitra. 199.
For the verse beginning with "Indro aṅga mahad bhayam," Gṛtsamada is the seer; for the Sāman that brings fearlessness, Indra is the seer. ||200||
Regarding these verses beginning with "imā u tvā sutesute," Bharadvāja is the seer; regarding the Sāman known as the Tvaṣṭṛ-sāman, Tvaṣṭṛ is the seer. || 201 ||
"Indrā nu pūṣaṇā vayam"—this is the ṛc (Bharadvāja is the seer; Indra and Pūṣan are the deities). Of the Sāman dedicated to Pūṣan, Pūṣan is the seer. || 202 ||
For the ṛc beginning with "na ki indra tvam," Vāmadeva is the seer; for the sāman of Indrāṇī, Indrāṇī is the seer. || 203 ||
Thus ends the ninth section in the second chapter dedicated to Indra.
The tenth section:
for the *ṛc* "taraṇiṃ vo janānām," the seer is Triśoka; for the *sāman* of Śyāvāśva, the seer is Śyāvāśva. 204.
The seer of the *ṛc* "asṛgram indra te giraḥ" is Madhucchandas; the seer of the *sāman* Vairūpa is Sumitra. ||205||
The seer of the verse beginning with "sunītho ghā sa martyo" is Vaṃśa; the seer of the Sāman of Saumitra is Sumitra. ||206||
The seer of the verse "yadvīḍāvindra" is Triśoka; the seer of the *sāman* "taubha" is Tubha. ||207||
"Śrutaṃ vo vṛtrahantamam"—this is the Ṛc; Śrutakakṣa is its seer. For the Sāman, the Śrauta, Śruta is the seer. ||208||
"araṃ ta indra śravase"—this *ṛc* has Śrutakakṣa (or Vāmadeva) as its seer; for the *sāman* Ābhīśava, Abhīśu is the seer. ||209||
The seer of the verse beginning with "dhānāvantaṃ karambhiṇam" is Viśvāmitra; the seer of the Sāman dedicated to Pūṣan is Pūṣan. ||210||
For the verse beginning with "apāṃ phenena," the seers are Gauṣūkta and Aśvasūktin; for the Sāman, the seer is Kṣurapavin Indra. ||211||
The Ṛgvedic verse beginning "These, O Indra, are the Soma-draughts" has Vāmadeva as its seer; the Sāman for Saumitra has Sumitra as its seer. || 212 ||
The seer of the *ṛc* "tubhyaṃ sutāsaḥ somāḥ" is Śrutakakṣa; the seer of the *sāman* Saumitra is Sumitra. ||213||
Thus ends the tenth section in the second chapter dedicated to Indra.
The eleventh section begins:
"Ā vā indraṃ kṛviṃ yathā"—the seer of this *ṛc* is Śunaḥśepa; the seer of the *sāman* of Kautsa is Kutsa. 214.
Therefore, for the *ṛc* "ataścidindra na upā yāhi," the seer is Śrutakakṣa; for the *sāman* of Kautsa, the seer is Kutsa. ||215||
For the Ṛgvedic verse beginning with "ā bundaṃ vṛtrahā," the seer is Triśoka; for the Sāman dedicated to Uṣas, the seer is Uṣas. ||216||
For the ṛc beginning with "bṛhadukthaṃ havāmahe," the seer is Medhātithi; for the sāman of Bhāradvāja, the seer is Bharadvāja. ||217||
The seer of the verse beginning with "ṛjunītī no varuṇaḥ" is Gautama; the seer of the Sāman of Kautsa is Kutsa. ||218||
For the *ṛc* "dūrād ihaiva yat sataḥ," Viśvāmitra Gautama is the seer (*ṛṣi*). For the *sāman* of the Dawn (*auṣasa*), Uṣas is the seer. ||219||

Regarding the verse beginning with "ā no mitrāvaruṇā," the seer is either Viśvāmitra or Jamadagni; for the Sāman concerning the union of Mitra and Varuṇa, the seers are Mitra and Varuṇa themselves. 220.
"udutye sūnavo giraḥ"—this *ṛc* has Praskaṇva Kāṇva as its seer (*ṛṣi*). Of the *sāman* called *Ṛtuṣāman*, the Seasons (*ṛtavaḥ*) are the seers. ||221||
For the ṛc verse beginning "idaṃ viṣṇurvi cakrame," Medhātithi is the seer (ṛṣi). For the sāman, "viṣṇoḥ sāma," Viṣṇu is the seer. And he is also the deity. 222.
Thus ends the eleventh section in the second chapter dedicated to Indra.
The twelfth section:
for the *ṛc* "atīhi manyuṣāviṇam," Medhātithi is the seer (*ṛṣi*); for the *sāman* of Kautsa, Kutsa is the seer. || 223 ||
The seer of the verse beginning with "kadu pracetase" is Vāmadeva; the seer of the Sāman belonging to Kāśyapa is Kaśyapa. || 224 ||
And regarding the verse "The hymn being recited for us," Medhātithi and Priyamedha are the seers; Bṛhaduktha, who belongs to Agni, is the seer of the Sāman known as the Bārhaduktha. ||225||
For the *ṛc* beginning with "indra ukthebhiḥ," Viśvāmitra is the seer; for the *sāman* of Bṛhaduktha, Bṛhaduktha or Agni is the seer. ||226||
The seer of the *ṛc* "ā yāhy upa naḥ" is Medhātithi Āṅgirasa; the seer of the *sāman* of Kautsa is Kutsa. || 227 ||
*Kadā vaso stotram* is by the seer Durmitra; for the two *sāmans*, Kautsa is the seer. (228)
The seer of the verse beginning with "brāhmaṇādindra rādhasaḥ" is Medhātithi; the seer of [the verse] "aurdhvasadmanasya" is Ūrdhvasadman. ||229||
"vayaṃ ghā te api smasi"—this *ṛc* has Medhātithi as its seer (*ṛṣi*). Of the *sāman* called Aurdhvasadmana, Urdhvasadman is the seer. ||230||
"O Indra, in which battles [is there] manly strength?"—this is the Ṛc; its seer is Viśvāmitra. Of the Sāman, the Audala, the seer is Abhīpāda Uḍala. ||231||
"evā hy asi vīrayuḥ"—of this *ṛc*, Madhucchandas is the seer (*ṛṣi*). "āmahīyava"—of this, Āmahīyu is the seer. ||232||
Thus ends the twelfth section in the second chapter on the Aindrīs.
In this manner, there are one hundred and eighteen Gāyatrī verses addressed to Indra;
one hundred and eighty-six Sāmans have been handed down by the great seers.
Thus ends the second chapter.
The Third Chapter:

Now, the Bṛhatī verses dedicated to Indra are recited in groups of eight; those in the Triṣṭubh meter in groups of three, and those in the Anuṣṭubh meter in groups of one, as they are recited in the third chapter.
First Section:

Regarding the verse beginning with *abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ*, Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Indra is the deity (*devatā*), and Bṛhatī is the metre (*chandaḥ*). The same applies hereafter. For these [verses] as well, consisting of sixty-nine verses, the metre is Bṛhatī, the deity is Indra. For the other eleven verses, the specific deities will be stated therein. For the two Sāmans and the two Ārka hymns of Bharadvāja, Bharadvāja is the seer. 233.
For the ṛc beginning with "tvām id dhi havāmahe," Bharadvāja is the seer; for that sāman and for the two bhāradvāja-sāmans as well, Bharadvāja is the seer. || 234 ||

The seers of the *ṛc* verses beginning with "abhi pra vaḥ surādhasam" are the Bālakhilyas; for the first two *sāmans*, the Sāṃnatīs, Saṃnati is the seer; for the third, the Śyaita, Prajāpati is the seer. ||235||

The seer of the verse beginning "taṃ vo dasmamṛtīṣaham" is Nodhas; the seer of the first of the five Sāmans is Nāvika of the Nāka; the seer of the second, the Abhīvarta, is Prajāpati; the seer of the third, the Bhāga, is Bhaga; the seer of the fourth, the Indrasyābhīvarta, is Indra; and the seer of the fifth, the Naudhasa, is Nodhas Kākṣīvata. ||236||

Regarding the verse *tirobhivā vidadvasuṃ*, Kali is the *ṛṣi* of the *pragātha*. Regarding the *sāman*: for the first two of the seven [verses], Luśa is the *ṛṣi* of the two *lauśa* [sāmans]. For the second and third (*third and fourth?*), Dhānaka is the *ṛṣi* of the two *dhānāka* [sāmans]. According to another view, for the fourth, the *kṣullukakāleya*, Kṣullukakali is the *ṛṣi*. For the fifth, sixth, and seventh (*seventh among the...*?), Kali is the *ṛṣi* of the two *kāleya* [sāmans] (*of the kāleyas?*). According to another view, Kali alone is the *ṛṣi* of all seven. 237.

The seer of the ṛc verse beginning with "pibā sutasya rasinaḥ" is Medhātithi; the seer of the first *pṛṣṭha* stotra of the Sāmans is Prajāpati; and the seer of the two subsequent *gauśr̥ṅga* stotras is Gauśr̥ṅga. || 239 ||
For the two [verses] beginning with "tvaṃ hyo hi cerave," Bhaga is the seer; for the two Sāmans of Kaulmalabarhiṣa, Kulmalabarhiṣ is the seer. || 240 ||
For "na hi vaścaramaṃ ca na" (RV 7.58.1), Vasiṣṭha is the seer; the Maruts are the deity. For the two *sāman*s belonging to Vasiṣṭha’s progeny, Vasiṣṭha is the seer. ||241||
"Mā cid anyad vi śaṃsata"—this *ṛc* has Kaṇva as its seer (*ṛṣi*), [forming] a *pragātha*; for the *sāman* of Medhātithi, Medhātithi Kaṇva is the seer. || 242 ||
Thus ends the first section in the third chapter concerning Indra.
The second section:
for the verse beginning "nakiṣṭaṃ karmaṇā naśati," Puruhanman is the seer; for the first Sāman, the Vaikhānasa, Vikhanas is the seer; for the second, the Pauruhanmana, Puruhanman is the seer.
The seer of the verse beginning with "ya ṛte cid abhiśriṣaḥ" is Medhātithi; the seer of the Sāman called Sātya is Satya. ||244||

The ṛc beginning with "ā tvā sahasram ā śatam" has Medhātithi and Medhyātithi as its seers (ṛṣis). For the four Sāmans of the Bhāradvāja family, Bharadvāja is the seer; alternatively, for the second, the Kaṇva-Bṛhat, Kaṇva is the seer. ||246||
For the *ṛc* "tvamaṅga pra śaṃsiṣaḥ," the seer is Gautama, the son of Rahūgaṇa. For the *sāman* "agnergauṅgavasya," the seer is Agni Guṅgu, or Guṅgu himself. ||247||

The Ṛgvedic verse beginning with "tvam indra yaśā asi" has Nṛmedha or Purumedha as its seer (*ṛṣi*). For the two Sāmans [or five] concerning Indra’s glory (*yaśas*), Indra is the seer; or for the second *sādhra*, [Indra is the seer]; or for that *sādhra*, Sādhra is the seer. ||249||
The seer of the verses beginning with "imā u tvā pūruvaso" is Medhātithi; the seer of the three Sāmans is Atri. ||250||
The seer of the Ṛgvedic verses beginning with "udu tye madhumattamāḥ" is Medhyātithi; the seer of the three Vāsiṣṭha Sāmans is Vasiṣṭha. || 251 ||
The seer of the *ṛc* "yathā gauro apākṛtam" is Devātithi Kāṇva; the seer of the two *sāmans*, "manān" and "adya," belonging to Gautama, is Gautama. ||252||
Thus ends the second section in the third chapter concerning Indra. ||2||
The third section:
for the verses beginning with "śagdhy ū ṣu śacīpate," Bharga is the seer; for the three Hārāyaṇa Sāmans, Indra is the seer. ||253||
The seer of the *ṛc* beginning with "yā indra bhuja ābharaḥ" is Rebha Kāśyapa; the seer of the three *sāmans* of the Vāmrās is Vāma. ||254||
For "pra mitrāya prāryamṇe," Jamadagni is the seer (ṛṣi); Āditya is the deity. For the three Varuṇa-sāmans among the Sāmans, Varuṇa is the seer. ||255||
The seer of the verse beginning with "abhitvā pūrvapītaye" is Medhyātithi; the seer of the *sāman* known as Vaṣaṭkāraṇidhana is Prajāpati. || 256 ||
The seers of the Ṛc "pra va indrāya bṛhate" are Nṛmedha and Purumedha; the seer of the Dhṛṣat Māruta Sāman is the Ṛṣi Dhṛṣanmāruta. ||257||

Indra is the seer of the four *sāman*s and their *saṃśāna*s. Now, in this *ṛc*, one should chant with the four *stobha*s: "santvāhinvanti," "santyāṛṇanti," "santvā tatakṣuḥ," and "santvā śiśanti"; and with the four quarters [of the verse] beginning "bṛhadindrāya gāyata," all four should be sung. The first three *stobha*s are at the beginning of the *sāman*s, while the last three are sung; the fourth has its *stobha* at the beginning and end of the *sāman*. This dual *stobha* is also to be sung in the four *sāman*s. ||258||

The *ṛc* beginning with "indra kratuṃ na ābhara" has Vasiṣṭha as its *ṛṣi*. Of the three *sāmans*, the first two belong to the Vāma family, while the third belongs to the Vāsiṣṭha family; thus, the *ṛṣis* are Vāma and Vasiṣṭha. ||259||
The seer of the verse beginning "Do not turn us away, O Indra" is Rebha; the seers of the two Sāmans, Rājiga and Ājiga, are the Dānavas. || 260 ||

The ṛc beginning with *vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvantaḥ* has Medhyātithi as its seer (*ṛṣi*). Of the four *sāmans*, the first is the *āṣkāraṇidhana* of the Kaṇva lineage; its seer is Kaṇva of the Kaṇva lineage. The second is the *mahāvaiṣṭambha*; its seer is Viṣṭambha. The third is the *abhinidhana* of the Kaṇva lineage; its seer is Kaṇva. The fourth is the *diṅnidhana* *mahāvaiṣṭambha*; its seer is Viṣṭambha. ||261||
Regarding the verse beginning with "yad indra nāhuṣīṣv ā," Bharadvāja is the seer; for the Sāman, Śnuṣṭigu is the seer of the Śnauṣṭīgava. ||262||
Thus ends the third section in the third chapter concerning Indra. ||3||
The fourth section:
for the *ṛc* "satyam itthā vṛṣed asi," Medhātithi is the seer (*ṛṣi*). For the *sāman* of Indra Vṛṣaka, Indra is the seer. ||263||
The seer Rebha is the seer of the ṛc beginning with "yacchākāsi parāvati"; for the two *dvaigata* sāmans, Dviga Bhārbhava is the seer. || 264 ||
"Abhi vo vīram andhasaḥ"—this *ṛc* has Vaiśa as its seer; "Kārtayaśasa" of the *sāman* has Kṛtayaśas as its seer. ||265||
For the verse beginning "O Indra, the threefold refuge," Bharadvāja is the seer; for the verse concerning Indra's refuge, Indra is the seer. ||266||
The seer of the verse beginning with "śrāyanta iva sūryam" is Nṛmedha; the seer of the Sāman known as Śrāyantīya is Prajāpati. ||267||
Sīmadeva Āpa is the seer of those *ṛc* verses; Puruhanman is the seer of the *sāman*; Vāma is the seer of the [hymn] of Vāma. || 268 ||
The seers of the *ṛc* "ā no viśvāsu havyam" are Nṛmedha and Purumedha; the seer of the three *sāmans* of the Vaiyyāśvas is Vyaśva Āṅgirasa. ||269||
"tavedindrāvamaṃ vasu"—this *ṛc* has Vasiṣṭha as its *ṛṣi*; for the *sāman* desiring the *nidhana*, Prajāpati is the *ṛṣi*. ||270||
Where do the two sages Medhātithi and Medhyātithi stand regarding the Ṛg-verses? Regarding the three Sāmans dear to Indra, Indra himself is the seer. || 271 ||
For the *ṛc* "vayamenamidā hyaḥ," Kali is the seer; for the three *sāmans* of Indra belonging to the Vairūpa group, Indra is the seer, or alternatively Vasiṣṭha. || 272 ||
Thus ends the fourth section in the third chapter dedicated to Indra. ||4||

Regarding the verse beginning with "yo rājā carṣaṇīnām," Puruhanman is the seer (ṛṣi). Of the two Sāmans, for the first, the Pauruhanmana, Puruhanman Vaikhānasa is the seer; for the second, the Prākarṣa, Prakarṣa is the seer. ||273||
For the verse beginning with "yata indra bhayāmahe," Bharga is the seer; for the Sāman known as Abhayamkara, Indra is the seer. || 274 ||
For the verse beginning with "vāstoṣpate," the seer is Irimbiḍha; for the two Sāmans belonging to Kavaṣa, the seer is Kavaṣa. ||275||
For the verse beginning with "baṇ mahām̐ asi," Jamadagni is the seer (ṛṣi) and Sūrya is the deity; for the Sāman of Sūrya, Sūrya is the seer. ||276||
The seer of the verse beginning with "aśvī rathī surūpaḥ" is Devātithi; the seers of the two Sāmans beginning with "rānūpayaḥ" are Vadhrīyaśva Ānūpa. ||277||
The verses beginning with "yaddyāva indra te śatam" have Puruhanman as their seer; for the Vairūpa Sāman, Virūpa is the seer. ||278||
"O Indra, [whatever is] in the east, west, or north"—this is the *ṛc* of the seer Devātithi; "of the two *sāmans*, Naipātitha"—this is the *ṛc* of the seer Nipātithi. || 279 ||
The seer of the verse beginning with "kastamidva" is Vasiṣṭha; the seers of the two Bṛhat-sāmans, namely the Kaumuda and the Bṛhatkumuda, are Bṛhatkumuda. || 280 ||
For the verse beginning with "indrāgnī apāt," Bharadvāja is the seer (ṛṣi). For the Sāman, Vāc is the seer; for the Sāman, Vāc is the seer. Indra and Agni are the deities. ||281||
The seers of the *ṛc* "O Indra, come nearer" are the Bālakhilyas; the seer of the two *sāmans* [beginning with] "vāmram" is Vāmra. || 282 ||
Thus ends the fifth section in the third chapter concerning Indra.
The sixth section:
for the verse beginning "ita ūtī vo ajaram," the seer is Nṛmedha; for the two Bārhata Sāmans (the Gaurīvitas), the seer is Gaurīviti. || 283 ||
For the verse beginning "mo ṣu tvā vāghataś ca na," Vasiṣṭha is the seer; for the two Sāmans [beginning with] "rātreyayoḥ," Atri is the seer. || 284 ||
The seer of the verse "sunota soma" is Vasiṣṭha; the seers of the two Sāmans of Gaurīviti are Gaurīviti. ||285||
Regarding the verse beginning with "yaḥ satrāhā vicarṣaṇiḥ," Parucchepa is the seer (ṛṣi) and the Aśvins are the deities (devatā). For the Sāman [of] the Aśvins, the Aśvins are the seers. || 287 ||
Regarding the verse beginning with "yadā kadā ca mīḍhuṣe": Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi) and Varuṇa is the deity. Regarding the three Sāmans of Vasiṣṭha and the Pajras, Vasiṣṭha is the seer. ||288||
The seer of the verse beginning with "pāhi gā andhasaḥ" is Medhyātithi; the seers of the two Sāmans belonging to the Saubhara collection are Saubhari. || 289 ||
"May he hear both of us"—this [verse] has Bharga as its seer; for the Sāman, Vyaśva, the son of Viyaśva, is the seer. ||290||
For the verse beginning "mahe ca na tvādrivo," the seers are Medhātithi and Medhyātithi; for the two Sāmans, Indra's Sahasrāyutīya, the seer is either Indra or Prajāpati. ||291||
For the Ṛgvedic verse beginning "vasyām indrāsi me pituḥ," Medhātithi and Medhyātithi are the seers; for the Sāmavedic chant "indrāṇyāḥ," Indrāṇī is the female seer. ||292||
Thus ends the sixth section in the third chapter dedicated to Indra.
The seventh section:
"These [somas] are pressed for Indra"—of this *ṛc*, Vasiṣṭha is the seer; of the *sāman* Saubhara, Subhari is the seer. || 293 ||
"ima indra madāya te"—these verses have Vāmadeva as the seer (*ṛṣi*), though some say Viśvāmitra; for the *sāman*, Gṛtsamada is the seer of the Gārtsamada [hymn]. ||294||
The seers of the verse "Come to me today with the cow that yields nectar" are Medhātithi and Medhyātithi; the seer of the Sāman is Vāc. ||295||
The seer of the verse beginning with "na tvā bṛhantaḥ" is Nodhas; the seer of the Bṛhaduktha Sāman is Bṛhaduktha Vāmadevya. ||296||
"Who knows him when the Soma is pressed?"—this [verse] has Medhātithi as its seer; for the Sāman, Vārṣa is the seer of the Vārṣa [tune]. ||297||
Regarding the verse "yad indra śāso avratam," Vāmadeva is the seer; for the Sāman, Turaśravas is the seer of the Tauraśravasa [hymn]. ||298||

For the verse beginning with "tvaṣṭā no daivyam," Vāmadeva is the seer; according to some, it has many deities as its divinity. For the Sāman known as the Tvāṣṭrīya-sāman, the Tvāṣṭrī is the seer. ||299||
The seers of the *ṛc* "kadā cana starīr asi" are the Bālakhilyas; for the *sāman*, Aditi is the seer of the *sāman*, and Aditi is the seer of the *sāman*. ||300||
The seer of the ṛc "yuṅkṣvā hi vṛtrahantama" is Nṛmedhas; the seer of the Mādhucchandasa sāman is Madhucchandas. ||301||
Regarding the verse "tvām idā hyo naraḥ," the seer is Nṛmedha; regarding the Sāman of Mādhucchandasa, the seer is Madhucchandas. ||302||
Thus ends the seventh section in the third chapter concerning Indra.
The eighth section:
"She has been seen approaching"—this is the verse. Vasiṣṭha is the seer; Uṣas is the deity. For the Sāman, Uṣas is the seer of both the Sāman and the verse. ||303||

The Ṛgvedic verses beginning with "imā u vām" have Vasiṣṭha as the seer (ṛṣi), the Aśvins as the deity, and for both the Aśvin Sāman and the Aśvin [hymns], the Aśvins themselves are the seers. ||304||
The seers of the verse beginning with "kuṣṭhaḥ ko vām" are the Aśvins; the deities are the Aśvins. For the Sāman of the conjunction of the Aśvins, the seers are also the Aśvins. ||305||
Regarding the verse "ayaṃ vāṃ madhumattamaḥ," Praskaṇva Kāṇva is the seer (ṛṣi); for both the Aśvin Sāman and the Aśvin [verse], the Aśvins themselves are the seers. ||306||
The seer of the *ṛc* "ā tvā somasya galdayā" is Devātithi; the seer of the *sāman* "ājamāyava" is Ajamāyu. || 307 ||
For the *ṛc* "O Adhvaryu, cause it to flow," the seer is Devātithi; for the *sāman* of Ajamīḍha, the seer is Ajamīḍha. ||308||
"Abhīṣataḥ tat" is the Ṛgvedic verse; its seer is Vasiṣṭha. "Sāma" belongs to Praiyamedha; its seer is Priyamedha. ||309||
For the verse beginning "yad indra yāvatas tvam," the seer is Vasiṣṭha; for the two Sāmans of Indra belonging to the Vairūpa group, the seer is Virūpa. ||310||
The seer of the ṛc verse beginning with "tvam indra pratūrtiṣu" is Nṛmedhas; the seers of the Vaiśvadeva Sāman are the Viśvedevas. ||311||
"Nodhas is the seer of the Ṛgvedic verse beginning with *pra yo ririkṣa ojasā*; Atharvan is the seer of the Sāman belonging to the Atharvans. || 312 ||
Thus ends the eighth section in the third chapter concerning Indra.
Thus [end] the eighty Bṛhatī verses.
The Ninth Section.
Now follows the *traiṣṭubha* [section].
The seer of the ṛc beginning with "asāvi deva" is Vasiṣṭha; the seer of the first sāman, Prākarṣa, is Pṛkṣa (or Prakarṣa?); [the seer] of the second, Nihava, is Vasiṣṭha. ||313||
The seer of the verse beginning "yoniṣṭa indra sadane" is Vasiṣṭha; the seers of the two Sāmans [beginning with] "yoninoh" are Gṛtsamada. ||314||
For the *ṛc* "adardar utsamasṛjaḥ," the seer is Gātu Ātreya; for the two *sāmans* "aurukṣaya" and "urukṣaya," the seer is Urukṣaya. ||315||
For the verse beginning with "suṣvāṇāsaḥ," Pṛthu Vainya is the seer; for the two Sāmans [Pāksya and Arthya], Pṛthu Vainya is the seer. ||316||

The seer (*ṛṣi*) of the seven *ṛc*s beginning with "jagṛhyā te dakṣiṇam" is Saptagu; these are the first five *sāmans* of the Suparṇa group, and for those two, Suparṇa is the seer. There are three Vātsapras; for those, Vatsapra is the seer. The third is the Kṣullakavātsapra, and the fifth is the Mahāvātsapra. ||317||
The seer of the verse beginning with "indraṃ naro nemadhitā" is Vasiṣṭha; the seer of the Sāman belonging to Gaurīvita is Gaurīviti. ||318||
The seer of the verse beginning with "vayaḥ suparṇā" is Gaurīviti; the seer of the Sāman known as Vaidanvata is Vidanvān Bhārgava. ||319||
For the verse beginning with "nāke suparṇam," the seer is Vena Bhārgava; for the Sāman known as Mahāyāma, the seer is Yama. ||320||
For the verse beginning with "brahma jajñānam," Vāmadeva is the seer; for the two Sāmans of the Seasons, the Season is the seer. ||321||
"Apūrvyā purutamāni"—this is the Ṛc; Suhotra Bharadvāja is the seer (ṛṣi). Of the Sāman, the Vāravantīya belonging to Indra, Indra is the seer (ṛṣi). ||322||
Thus ends the ninth section in the third chapter concerning Indra.

The tenth section: For the *ṛc* beginning with "ava drapsaḥ," the seer is Dyutāna. Of the four *sāmans*, for the first two, [the deity is] Indra's Kṣurapavī; for those two, Indra is the seer. For the two [sāmans] of Saumaraśmi, Indra is the seer. For the *ṛc* beginning with "vṛtrasya tvā śvasathaḥ," the seer is Dyutāna. Of the two *sāmans*—[the one] of Dyutāna and [the one] of the Maruts—the seer is Dyutāna.
The seer of the verse beginning with "vidhuṃ dadrāṇam" is Bṛhaduktha; the seers of the two Sāmans, namely the Somasāman, are Soma. || 325 ||
For the verses beginning with "tvaṃ ha tyad," the seer is Dyutāna; for the two Sāmans, "Indravajra," the seer is Indra. ||326||
The seer of the verse beginning with "moḍiṃ na tvā" is Vāmadeva; for the two Sāmans, Bhṛṣṭimat and Sūryavarcas, the seers are Bhṛṣṭimat and Sūryavarcas respectively. ||327||
Vasiṣṭha is the seer of the ṛc beginning with "pra vo mahe"; for the two sāmans [beginning with] "vasiṣṭhasya" and "aṅkuśayoḥ," Vasiṣṭha is the seer. (Gṛhyagrantha 5.58–9) ||328||
The seer of the verse beginning with "śunaṃ huvema" is Viśvāmitra; the seer of the Sāman belonging to Bhāradvāja is Bhāradvāja. ||329||
For the *udu* [hymn], Viśvāmitra is the seer; for the *vaiśvadeva* sāman, the Viśvedevas are the seers. || 330 ||
For the verse beginning with "cakraṃ yadasya," the seer is Gaurīviti; for the Sāman of Atharvan, the seer is Atharvan. ||331||
Thus ends the tenth section of the third chapter.
The Eleventh Section.
The seer of the verse beginning with "tyamūṣu vājinam" is Ariṣṭanemi, the son of Tārkṣya; the seer of the two Sāmans, the Tārkṣya-sāmans, is Tārkṣya. ||332||
For the ṛc beginning with "trātāram indram," Bharadvāja is the seer; for the sāman of Indra Trāda, Indra is the seer. ||333||
The seer of the *ṛc* "yajāmahe" is Vasukṛt, or the seer is Vimada; the seer of the *sāman* Vārtratura is Vṛtratṛt, or Yajñatṛt. ||334||
For the verse beginning with "satrāhaṇam," Vāmadeva is the seer; for the two Sāmans, "dhṛṣataḥ" and "mārutasya," Dhṛṣanmāruta is the seer. ||335||
The seer of the *ṛc* "yo no vanuṣyan" is Vāmadeva; the seer of the *sāman* "ātreya" is Atri. ||336||
The seer of the verse beginning with "yaṃ vṛtreṣu" is Vāmadeva; the seers of the two Sāmans beginning with "gāt" and "samada" are Gṛtsamada. || 337 ||
For the *ṛc* "indrāparvatā" the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Viśvāmitra; for the Sāman belonging to Viśvāmitra, the seer is Viśvāmitra. ||338||

For the *ṛc* "indrāya giraḥ," Reṇu Vaiśvāmitra is the seer (*ṛṣi*). For the six *sāman*s dedicated to Savitṛ, Savitṛ is the seer. There are five *sāvitra*s accompanied by the four *ārcika*s, each with its respective *stobha*, beginning with the five *stobhas*: "hā hā (i)," and so forth. ||339||
The seer of the ṛc beginning with "ā tvā sakhāyaḥ" is Vāmadeva; the seer of the sāman belonging to Kautsa and the Vairūpa melody is Virūpa. ||340||
The seer of the ṛc "ko adya yuṅkte" is Gautama; the seer of the sāman Āmahīyava is Āmahīyu. ||341||
Thus ends the eleventh section in the third chapter concerning Indra.
(Thus the Triṣṭubhs. || The Twelfth Section ||
The ten verses beginning with "gāyanti tvā" are in the Anuṣṭubh meter; Indra is the deity.

"Gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ" and so forth are the Ṛg verses (Madhucchandas is the seer). Of the two Sāman chants beginning with "Śaukhaṇḍine," Śikhaṇḍin is the seer. The third is the Udvaṃśīya; the Viśvedevas are the seers. ||342||

"Indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan"—this is the *ṛc*. The seer is Madhucchandas, the conqueror. Of the seven *sāmans*, the first three are the Śaikhaṇḍinas; their seer is Śikhaṇḍin. Two have Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra Vairūpa as the seer. There are two Mahāvaiśvāmitras; their seer is Viśvāmitra. ||343||

"O Indra, drink this pressed [soma]"—this [verse] has Gautama as its seer (ṛṣi). Of the four Sāmans dear to Vasiṣṭha, Vasiṣṭha is the seer; or the second [Sāman] has Gautama [as its seer], whose seer is Gautama. ||344||

Regarding the verse *yad indra citra ma iha*, Atri is the seer (*ṛṣi*). There are four *sāman*s, the *vīṅka*s. For two of them, Gṛtsamada is the seer; for the third, it is either Ākūpāra, whose seer is Ākūpārāṅgiras. |||345||
The seer of the *ṛc* "śrudhī havam tiraścyā" is Gautama; the same is the seer of the two *sāmans* belonging to the Kaṇvas. ||346||
The seer of the *ṛc* "asāvi soma indra te" is Gautama; the seer of the *sāman* of Viśvāmitra is Viśvāmitra. ||347||
The seer of the ṛc beginning with "endra yāhi" is Kaṇva Nīpātithi; the seers of the two Sāmans belonging to the Kaṇvas are also he alone. ||348||
The seer of the verse beginning "ā tvā giro rathī" is Tiraścī; the seer of the *sāman* belonging to Viśvāmitra is Viśvāmitra. ||349||
The seer of the ṛc beginning with "eto nvindraṃ stavāma" is Tiraścī; for the two Sāmans, Śuddhāśuddhīya, the seer is Indra, or Vasiṣṭha is the seer. ||350||
The seer of the verse beginning "yo rayiṃ vo rayim" is Śaṃyu Bārhaspatya; the seer of the two Sāmans beginning with "rai" is Gautama. ||351||
Thus ends the twelfth section in the third chapter concerning Indra.
Thus ends the third chapter.
The Fourth Chapter.
First Section.
Now, in the two Anuvākas belonging to Indra, there are verses in the Ānuṣṭubh metre.

The seer of the verse beginning with "pratyasmai pipīṣate" is Bharadvāja. Of the three Sāmans, the first two are the Kaulmalabarhiṣa Sāmans; their seer is Kulmalabarhiṣ. The third is the Nānada; its seer is Nadan Nāṅgirasa. ||352||
The ṛṣi of the verse beginning with "ā no vayo vāyaḥ śayam" is Vāmadeva; the ṛṣi of the Sāman of Śākapiṅga is Śākapiṅga. ||353||
The seer of the *ṛc* "ā tvā rathaṃ yathotaye" is Vāmadeva; the seers of the two *sāmans*, Kaulmala and Barhiṣa, are Kulmalabarhiṣ. ||354||
The seer of the *pragātha* verse beginning with "sa pūrvyo mahonām" is Madhuścyut; the seer of the *sāman* whose *nidhana* is "madhuścyut" is Prajāpati. ||355||
Regarding the verse beginning with "yadī vahantyāśavaḥ," Śyāvāśva Ātreya is the seer; the Maruts are the deity; it is a Sāman of the Dawn (uṣas); Uṣas is its seer. ||356||
The seer of the ṛc verse beginning with "tyamu vo aprahaṇam" is Śaṃyu Vārhaspatya; the seer of the sāman is Bhāradvāja Bharadvāja. ||357||
For the verse beginning "I have performed the praise of Dadhikrāvan," Vāmadeva is the seer; for the Sāman of Dadhikrāvan, Dadhikrā is the seer. ||358||
The seer of the ṛc beginning with "purāṃ bhinduḥ" is Jetṛ Mādhucchandasa; the seer of the sāman belonging to Mādhucchandasa is Madhucchandas. ||359||
Thus ends the first section in the fourth chapter dedicated to Indra.
The Second Section.
The seer of the verse beginning with "prapra vastriṣṭubham iṣam" is Priyamedha; the seer of the Vāmadevya Sāman is Vāmadeva. ||360||
For the *ṛc* "kaśyapasya," Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*) and Indrāṇī is the deity; for the *sāman* "kāśyapasya," Kaśyapa is the seer. ||361||
"Arcata prārcata"—these are the *ṛc*s; Priyamedha is the *ṛṣi*; Mitra and Varuṇa are the deities. Of the *sāman* belonging to Priyamedha, Priyamedha is the *ṛṣi*. || 362 ||

"An uktha is to be recited for Indra"—this is the Ṛgvedic verse; Madhucchandas is the seer (ṛṣi), Mitra and Varuṇa are the deities (devatā). Of the Bārhaduktha Sāman, Bṛhaduktha is the seer (ṛṣi). ||363||
For the ṛc "viśvānarasya vaspate," the seer is Priyamedha; for the sāman of Agni Vaiśvānara, the seer is Agni Vaiśvānara. ||364||
Regarding the verse "sa ghā yas te divo naraḥ," Bharadvāja is the seer; regarding the two Sāmans of Śākapūti, Śākapūti is the seer. ||365||
The seer of the ṛc "vibhūṣṭa indra" is Atri; the seer of the sāman "varuṇānyāḥ" is Varuṇānī. ||366||
For the *ṛc* beginning with "vayaścit te patatriṇaḥ," the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Praskaṇva and the deity is Uṣas; for the *sāman* related to the dawn, the seer is Uṣas. ||367||
The ṛc beginning with "amī ye devā sthana" has Trita Āptya as its seer; the Viśvedevas are the deity. For the sāman "rocanasya ruciḥ," the seer is [Trita] Rocana. ||368||

Regarding "the Ṛc and the Sāman": for the Ṛc, Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi). Of the Sāman, the preceding part is the Ṛc; its seer is the Ṛc itself. The subsequent part is the Sāman of the Sāman; its seer is the Sāman itself. [The subsequent part is] the Sāman of the Sāman; its seer is the Sāman itself. The Ṛc and the Sāman are the two deities. ||369||
Thus end the eighteen verses in the Anuṣṭubh meter.
Thus ends the second section of the fourth chapter dedicated to Indra.
The Third Section.
Now follow the Jagatī verses consisting of eleven ṛcs; some say that the first is an Atijagatī.
The seer of the verse beginning with "viśvāḥ pṛtanāḥ" is Rebha Kāśyapa; the seer of the Sāman known as Traiśoka is Triśoka. ||370||

The Ṛg-verse beginning with "śrat te dadhāmi" has Suvedas Śailūṣī as its seer (ṛṣi). Of the eight Sāmans, the first two belong to Śikhaṇḍin; their seer is Śikhaṇḍin. The third and fourth are the Vivartas of Atri; their seer is Atri. The fifth and sixth belong to Mahāsāvetasa; their seer is Atri. The seventh and eighth are the Mahāśairīṣas; their seer is Mahāśirīṣa. ||371||
Regarding the verse beginning with "sameta viśva ojasā," Gautama Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi). For the three Sāmans dear to Indra, Indra is the seer; or alternatively, Vasiṣṭha. ||372||
"Ime ta indra te" and so forth—these verses have Savya Āṅgirasa as their seer. Regarding the three Vairūpa Sāmans dedicated to Indra, the seers are either Indra or Vasiṣṭha. ||373||
The Ṛṣi of the verse beginning "carṣaṇidhṛtaṃ maghavānam" is Viśvāmitra; the Ṛṣi of the Bṛhaduktha Sāman is Bṛhaduktha. ||374||
The seer of the *ṛc* "Acchā va indraṃ matayaḥ" is Kṛṣṇa; and the seers of the two *sāmans* belonging to Trasadasyu are Trasadasyu and [his son] Trasadasyava. ||375||
The seer of the *ṛc* "abhi tyaṃ meṣam" is Savya; the seer of the *sāman*, the *jāgata* *soma-sāman*, is Soma. ||376||
The seer of the verse beginning "tyaṃ su meṣaṃ mahayā svarvidam" is Bharadvāja; the seer of the Sāman, Saubhara, is Subhari. ||377||
For the verse beginning with "ghṛtavatī bhuvanānām," Bharadvāja is the seer; Heaven and Earth are the deities. For the two Sāmans [beginning with] "sāmnor varuṇasya," Varuṇa is the seer. ||378||

Regarding the verse "ubhe yad indra rodasī," the seer is Marut Yauvanāśva; this [verse] consists of eight-syllable quarters and is in the Mahāpaṅkti meter. For the Sāman, Śyena Indra is the seer. ||379||

"Sing forth a word full of nourishment for the exhilarated one"—this is the *ṛc*; its seer is Kṛtsa. This is the secret doctrine (*upaniṣad*) concerning the miscarriage of the embryo. Its seer is Cyavana, the son of Cyāvana, of the Sāman. ||380||
Thus [end] the Jagatī verses.
Thus ends the third section of the third chapter dedicated to Indra.
The Fourth Section.
Now follows the Indra-puccha:
"Indra" occurs twenty-eight times; there are seventeen principal Uṣṇih verses, ten other Kakubh verses in the middle, and the three-footed Virāj verse beginning with "piba. ||1||
In the *tuca* [of the hymn] beginning with "tunāyāpāmīvam," there is praise of the Ādityas;
other verses are addressed to the Marutīs, the Gāvas, and Indra. 2.

The seer of the *ṛc* beginning with "indra suteṣu" is Nārada. Of the three *sāmans*, the first is Krośa, the second is Anukrośa, and the third is Kautsa. For the *saṃkrośa* and *anukrośa*, Indra is the seer; for the *kautsa*, Kutsa is the seer. ||381||

"Sing forth unto him"—these are the *ṛc*s; "This exhilaration for you"—these are the *ṛc*s of the two seers Gauṣūkti and Aśvasūkti. "Unto him"—this is the first of the four *sāman*s belonging to Divodāsa; in these two, Divodāsa is the seer. There are two [hymns] regarding the sending (*prahita*) and the joining (*saṃyojana*); the former is the *okonidhana*, and Prahiti is its seer. "This exhilaration for you"—this is the first of the four *sāman*s of the Hārivarṇas; Harivarṇa Āṅgirasa is their seer. 381–3.
For the verse beginning with "yat somam indra," the seer is Parvata; for the four *traita* *sāmans*, the seer is Trita. ||384||
The seer of the *ṛc* "adharmadintaram" is Viśvamanas Vaiyāśva; the seers of the two *sāmans*, "Surādhasa" and "Prādhasa," are Surādhas and Vāṅgirasa. ||385||
For the verse beginning "Pour [the soma] for Indra," Viśvamanas Vaiyaśva is the seer; for the Māruta Sāman, the Maruts are the seers. ||386||
"Come now, let us praise Indra"—this *ṛc* has Viśvamanas Vaiyaśva as its seer (*ṛṣi*). Of the *sāman* belonging to Viśvamanas, Viśvamana is the seer. ||387||
For the verse "Sing a Sāman unto Indra," the seer is Nṛmedha; for the three Saumitras among the Sāmans, the seer is Sumitra. ||388||
The seer of the verse beginning with "ya eka idvidayate" is Gautama; the seer of the three Traikakubha Sāmans is Trikakubha. ||389||
The seer of the verse beginning with "sakhāya ā śiṣāmahe" is Viśvamanas; the seer of the *sāmans* known as the Ukṣṇorandhras is Ukṣṇorandhra. ||390||
Thus ends the fourth section of the fourth chapter dedicated to Indra in the Auṣṇiha.
Fifth Section.

The seer of the *ṛc* "I proclaim that power of yours, O Indra" (*gṛṇe tad indra te śavaḥ*) is Pragātha. Of the three *sāmans*, the first is *prayasvat* and belongs to Prajāpati; the second is *ākṣāra*; the third is *prayasvat*. Among these, Prajāpati is the seer. ||391||
The seer of the verse beginning with "yasya tyacchambara" is Bharadvāja; the seer of the four Sāmans [beginning] with "taivo dāsānām" is Divodāsa. ||392||
The seer of the verse beginning with "endra no gahi" is Nṛmedha; the seer of the two Sāmans belonging to the Sāṃvarta cycle is Indra. ||393||
For the *ṛc* beginning with "ya indra soma," Parvata is the seer; for each *sāman*, Akṣāra is the seer of the *akṣāra*. ||394||
For the *tuc* verse beginning with "tunāya tatsu naḥ," the seer is Irimbiḍha and the deity is Āditya. For the *sāman* concerning long life, the seer is Prajāpati. ||394||
The seer of the verse beginning "Do you know the Nirṛtis? is Viśvamanas; the Sāman is Bharadvāja’s Śundhyu, and its seer is Bharadvāja. ||396||
For the verse beginning with "apāmīvām," the seer is Irimīḍha; for the Sāman beginning with "apāmīva," the seer and the deity are both Āditya. ||397||

"Piba somam indra" (Drink the Soma, O Indra)—this is the Ṛgvedic verse; Vasiṣṭha is the seer (ṛṣi), the Virāṭ meter with three feet is the metre (chandas). For the two Sāmans [based on this], Dīrghatamas is the seer for both Dīrghatamas and Sahodīrghatamas. || 398 ||
Thus end the eighteen verses in the auṣṇiha meter.
Thus ends the fifth section in the fourth chapter dedicated to Indra.
The Sixth Chapter.
Now, from the Kakubh meters.
For the ṛc "abhrātṛvyo anā tvam," the seer is Saubhari; for the sāman "abhrātṛvya," the seer is Indra. ||399||
The seer of the ṛc "yo na idam" is Saubhari; the seer of the two sāmans "śārkarayaḥ" is Śarkara. || 400 ||
"Ā gantā mā riṣaṇyata" is the ṛc; its seer is Saubhari. "Bṛhaka" is the seer of the Bṛhaka sāman. ||401||
The seer of the ṛc "ā yāhy ayam" is Saubhari; the seer of the three sāmans beginning with "sūyavasa" is Sūyavāsu. ||402||
For the ṛc beginning with "tvayā ha svid yujā," the seer is Saubhari; for the sāman "marutāṃ dhenūnām," the seer is the Maruts. ||403||
The seer of the ṛc "gāvaścid ghā samanvayaḥ" is Saubhari; the seer of the Sāman for the Maruts' settling, "marutāṃ saṃveśanīya," is the Maruts themselves. ||404||
The seer of the ṛc verse beginning with "tvaṃ na indra" is Nṛmedhas; for the three aiṣirāṇa sāmans dedicated to Vāyu, Vāyu is the seer. ||405||
Now, for the ṛc beginning with "adhā hīndra girvaṇaḥ," the seer is Nṛmedhas; for the three aiṣirāṇa sāmans dedicated to Vāyu, Vāyu is the seer. ||406||
The seer of the *ṛc* "sīdantas te vayaḥ" is Saubhari; the seers of the two *sāmans*, the Sīdantīyas, are Prajāpati. ||407||
For the verse beginning with "vayamu tvāmapūrvya," the seer is Saubhari; for the two Saubhara-sāmans as well, the seer is Saubhari. ||408||
Thus ends the ten verses of the Kakubh meters.
Thus ends the sixth section in the fourth chapter concerning Indra.
The seventh section consists of seventeen verses in the Paṅkti meter.
Gautama is the seer of the verse beginning with "svādoritthā viṣūvataḥ"; Yama is the seer of the Sāman named Yāma. ||409||
For "itthā hi soma inmadaḥ"—here Gautama is the seer of the *ṛc*; for the two *sāmans* [beginning with] "gṛtsa" and "mada," Gṛtsamada is the seer. ||410||

For the verse beginning with "Indro madāya," the seer is Gautama. Of the seven Sāmans, for the first two, the Ābhīkas, the seer is Ābhīka; for the third and fourth, the Ābhīśavas, the seer is Abhīśu; and for the remaining three, the Bārhadgiras, the seer is Bṛhadgiri. ||411||
For the *ṛc* beginning with "indra tubhyam," Gautama is the seer (*ṛṣi*). For the *sāman* "Indrasvārājya," Indra is the seer. ||412||
"Prehy abhīhi"—for this *ṛc*, Gautama is the seer (*ṛṣi*). For the *sāman* of Kaśyapa Dhṛṣṇu, Kaśyapa is the seer. ||413||
Regarding the verse beginning with "yad udīrita ājayaḥ," Gautama is the seer; regarding the Sāman "marutāṃ saṃveśīya," the Maruts are the seers. ||414||

For the *ṛc* "akṣann amīmadanta," Gautama is the seer; for the *sāman* of Yama, Yama is the seer. (415) For the *ṛc* "upo ṣu śrṛṇuhi giraḥ," Gautama is the seer; for the *sāman* of Yama, Yama is the seer. (416)

The ṛṣi of the verse beginning with "candramā apsvantā" is Trita. Of the five Sāmans, the ṛṣi of the first three—the *traitāna*s—is Trita; the ṛṣi of the latter two, which belong to Suparṇa (*sauparṇa*), is Suparṇa. ||417||
The seer of the verse beginning with "prati priyatamaṃ ratham" is Avasyu; the seer of the two Sāmans is Luśa, the son of Lauśa. ||418||
Thus ends the seventh section in the fourth chapter concerning Indra.
The Eighth Section.
For the *ṛc* "ā te agne idhīmahi" (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 3.20), Vasuśruta Ātreya is the seer (*ṛṣi*) and Agni is the deity. For those two *sāmans*, Indra Saṃjaya is the seer. ||419||

Regarding the verse beginning with "agnim na svavṛktibhiḥ," Gautama is the seer (*ṛṣi*), *paṅkti* is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Agni is the deity (*devatā*), and the two *sāmans* are the *utsenidha*. For these two, Aṅgiras is the seer. ||420||
For "mahe no adya bodhaya," the seer is Gautama; the metre is Paṅkti; the deity is Agni; and for the Sāman "vāryasya satyaśravasaḥ," the seer is Vārīya. ||421||
"Bhadraṃ no api vātaya"—this *ṛc* has Gautama as its seer (*ṛṣi*), *paṅkti* as its meter (*chandaḥ*), and Soma as its deity (*devatā*). For the *sāman* Pauṣa, Pūṣan is the seer. |||423||
For the verse beginning with "kratvā mahān," Gautama is the seer; Paṅkti is the meter; Indra is the deity. For the Sāman dedicated to Uṣas, Uṣas is the seer. ||423||
Regarding the verse "sa ghā taṃ vṛṣaṇam," Gautama is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Paṅkti is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). (For the *lauśa* Sāman, Luśa is the seer. ||424||
Regarding the verse "agnim tam manye" (RV 7.15.1): Vasuśruta Ātreya is the seer; Paṅkti is the meter; Agni is the deity. Regarding the Niṣedha-sāman: Aṅgiras is the seer. (425)
"Na tamaṃho na" and "ityṛcaḥ": the seer is Aṃhomug Vāmadevya; the deity is the Viśvedevas; the metre is Upariṣṭād-bṛhatī. For the Sāman, Gaura-āṅgirasa, the seer is Gaura-āṅgirā. ||426||
Thus ends the Paṅkti metre.
Thus ends the eighth section in the fourth chapter concerning Indra.
The Ninth Section.
Now follow thirty two-footed verses.
