The ṛc beginning with "pari pra dhanva" has Agni Dhiṣṇya as the seer; its metre is Akṣarapaṅkti, or alternatively Dvipadāpaṅkti; Soma is the deity. For the five Sāmans of the Suhavir group, Suhavis Āṅgirasa is the seer. ||| 427 ||

"Paryūṣu pra dhanva"—this *ṛc* has Tryaruṇa Trasadasyu as its seer (*ṛṣi*). It is an *anuṣṭubh* with three feet, having the "ant-waist" (*pipīlikāmadhyā*) meter. Soma is the deity. For the three *vākās* of the *sāmans*, Vaka is the seer. ||429||

"Flow on, O Soma, for great skill"—this verse has Dhiṣṇya Agni as its seer; Soma is the deity; Akṣarapaṅkti is the metre, or alternatively, Dvipadāpaṅkti. For the two Sāmans, Vidharmaṇī, Prajāpati is the seer; Soma is the deity. ||430||

The moon has flowed, beautiful for exhilaration—thus [says] the seer Agni, the son of the *ṛc*s, the wise one; Soma is the deity; the meter is the two-footed *paṅkti*; Bhaga is the seer of the portion of the *sāman*. ||431||

"O Soma, they have pressed thee..."—this verse has Dhiṣṇya Agni as its seer (ṛṣi), Soma as its deity, and the Pipīlikāmadhyā Anuṣṭubh as its meter. Vājinaḥ Sāman and Vājinaḥ Sāman are the seers. ||| 432 ||

For the verse *ā ī vyaktā naraḥ*, Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the Maruts are the deity, and the *dvipadā-paṅkti* is the meter. For the three Sāmans—Hika, Nikavi, and Ka—the seer is Prajāpati, and the Maruts are the deity. ||434|| For the verse *agne tam adya*, Agni is the seer, Agni is the deity, and the five-footed *padapaṅkti* is the meter. For the two Sāmans [named] Aśva, Prajāpati in the form of a horse is the seer. ||435||

For the verse beginning with "āvirmaryāḥ," Vājina is the seer (ṛṣi); the Vājins are the deity; Purāuṣṇik is the metre; and for the Sāman of the Vājins, as well as for the Sāman itself, the Vājins alone are the seers. ||435||

"Flow on, O Soma, radiant and with a fine stream"—this verse has Vāmadeva as its seer (ṛṣi), Soma as its deity, and the *dvipadā paṅkti* as its metre. For the *sāman* of the Ādityas' purifier (*pavitra*), the Ādityas are the seers. ||436||
Thus ends the ninth section concerning the *dvipadā* verses in the fourth chapter dedicated to Indra.
The Tenth Section.

Regarding the verse beginning with "viśvato dāvā," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi); Indra is the deity; the metre is Dvipadā Viṣṭārapaṅkti. Regarding the verses beginning with "sammīḷe indrasya" and "abhāyi," Indra is the seer, or alternatively, Vasiṣṭha is the seer. ||437||

Regarding the verse beginning "eṣa brahmā ya ṛtviyaḥ": Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi); Indra is the deity; the metre is Dvipadā Gāyatrī. Of the five Sāmans, the first two are the Vasumandas; for those two, Vasumanda is the seer. For the remaining three, Kavaṣa is the seer. ||438||

For the verse beginning "brahmāṇam indram," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi), Indra is the deity (devatā), and the metre (chandas) is Dvipadā Triṣṭubh. For the three Sāmans, Ślokas, and Anuślokas, Prajāpati is the seer. ||439||

For the verse beginning "anavaste rathaṃ," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi), Indra is the deity (devatā), and the metre (chandaḥ) is Dvipadā Triṣṭubh. For the Sāman Śloka, Prajāpati is the seer (ṛṣi). |||440||
"Śaṃ padaṃ magham"—of this verse, Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi); the metre (chandas) is Dvipadā; Indra is the deity (devatā). Of the Sāman, Speech is the seer. ||441||
"Always the cows": Vāmadeva is the seer; the metre is the two-footed Viṣṭārapaṅkti; Indra is the deity; of the Sāman, Speech is the seer. |||442||
Regarding the verse "ā yāhi vanasā," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi); Uṣas is the deity; the metre is Dvipadā Viṣṭārapaṅkti; and for the Māruta Sāman, the Maruts are the seers. ||443||

For the verse beginning "Upa prekṣa madhumatī," Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*); the metre (*chanda*) is Dvipadā Triṣṭubh; Indra is the deity (*devatā*); and for the *Sāman* belonging to Madhucchandas, Madhucchandas is the seer. ||444||
For the *ṛc* "arcaty arkam marutaḥ," Vāmadeva is the *ṛṣi*, the Maruts are the deity, and the metre is *dvipadā triṣṭubh*. For the *sāman* belonging to the Maruts, the Maruts are the *ṛṣi*. ||445||

"pra va indrāya vṛtrahantamāya"—these are the verses. Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi). The uneven-footed two-line meter (dvipadā) is the metre (chandas). Indra is the deity (devatā). For the Sāman [titled] Udvaṃśaputra, Prajāpati and the Viśvedevas are the seers. ||| 446 || Thus ends the tenth section in the fourth chapter on the hymns dedicated to Indra. ||| 10 ||
Now begins the eleventh section.
For the verse beginning with "acetyagniḥ," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi); Agni is the deity; the metre is Dvipadā Gāyatrī; and for the two Sāmans, the Ūrdhva and the Śāmya, Dhur is the seer. ||447||

Regarding the verse beginning *agne tvam no antamaḥ*: the seer is Vardhu Gopāyana; the deity is Agni; the metre is *dvipadā viṣṭārapaṅkti*. Of the four *sāmans*, the first is *gūrda*; its seer is Prajāpati. The second is *atyarda*; its seer is Viśvāmitra. The third is also *gūrda*; its seer is Prajāpati. The fourth is *atyarda*; its seer is Viśvāmitra. ||448||
"Bhago na citraḥ"—this verse has Vāmadeva as its seer (ṛṣi), Agni as its deity, and the uneven-footed dvipadā as its metre; for the two Sāmans, the Sāntanikas, Prajāpati is the seer. ||449||

For the verse beginning with "viśvasya pra stobha," Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*); Indra is the deity; the meter is *dvipadā gāyatrī*; and for the two *sāman*s, Dhanadharmin, Prajāpati is the seer. ||450||
For the verse beginning "O Dawn, flow forth," Saṃvarta is the seer; the deity is Uṣas; the metre is Dvipadā Viṣṭārapaṅkti. For the Sāman of Uṣas, Uṣas is the seer; the deity is Uṣas. ||451||

Now, for these verses beginning with "imā nu kam," the seer is Bhauvana, the Viśvedevas are the deity, the metre is Dvipadā Viṣṭārapaṅkti, and for the Sāman of Bharadvāja, the seer is Bharadvāja. ||452||

The *vistutis* are as follows: for the *ṛc*, Vāmadeva is the *ṛṣi*; Indra (or the Viśvedevas) is the deity; the *chandas* is the two-footed *gāyatrī*. For the *sāman*, Rāti is the *ṛṣi*; Indra (or the Viśvedevas) is the deity. ||453||
Regarding the verse *ayā vājam*, the seer is Bharadvāja; the deity is Uṣas (or Indra!); and for the Sāman of Bharadvāja, the seer is Bharadvāja. ||454||
For the verse beginning with "ūrjā mitro," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi); the Viśvedevas are the deity; the metre is Dvipadā Triṣṭubh; and for the Sāman, Aiṣa, Iṣa is the seer. ||455||

Regarding the verse "Indra rules over all," Vāmadeva is the seer; the meter is the one-footed Gāyatrī; Indra is the deity. Regarding the two Vairāja verses beginning with "Sam no indra," Indra is the seer. ||456||
Thus there are thirty two-footed [verses].
Thus ends the eleventh section in the fourth chapter dedicated to Indra. 11.
The twelfth section: Now, the *aticchandas* [verses] consist of ten *ṛc*s.

For the verse beginning "triṣkadrukeṣu mahiṣaḥ," Gṛtsamada is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Aṣṭi is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Indra is the deity (*devatā*), and Prajāpati is the seer of the Sāman known as Vājijit. 457.
The verse beginning with "ayaṃ sahasramānavaḥ" has the Jagatī metre; Sūrya is the deity. For the two Sāmans [named] Gaurāṅgirasa, Aṅgiras is the seer. ||458||

Regarding the verse beginning with "endra yāhy upa naḥ," Parucchepa is the seer (ṛṣi); Atyaṣṭi is the metre; Indra is the deity. For the Sāman called *Prayasvat*, belonging to Prajāpati, Prajāpati is the seer. ||459||
"Tam indraṃ johavīmi"—the seer of this *ṛc* is Rebha Kāśyapa; Indra is the deity; the metre is Atijagatī; Prajāpati is the seer of the inexhaustible Sāman. ||| 460 ||
"Let it be; let there be *śrauṣaṭ*": Parucchepa is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of this *ṛc*; Atyaṣṭi is the metre; the Viśvedevas are the deity. For the *Sāman* Yājñatura, Yajñatura is the seer. || 461 ||

"May your thoughts go forth to the great Viṣṇu"—this is the Ṛc. Evayāmarut is the seer; Rudra is the deity; Atijagatī is the metre. Of the Sāman, Evayāmarut is the name; Evayāmarut is the seer of the Sāman. ||462||

For the verse beginning "ayā rucā hiraṇyayī," Parucchepa is the seer (ṛṣi), Pavamāna Soma is the deity, and Atyaṣṭi is the meter. For the three Sāmans of Bharadvāja's uneven [stomas], Bharadvāja is the seer. ||463||

Regarding the verse beginning with "abhi tyaṃ devaṃ savitāram," Nakula is the seer (ṛṣi); the meter (chandaḥ) is Atiśakkarī; and Savitṛ is the deity (devatā). For the Sāman of Savitṛ, Savitṛ is the seer and also the deity. ||464||

For the verse beginning "I meditate upon Agni, the Hotṛ, the bountiful one," Parucchepa is the seer; Agni is the deity; Atyaṣṭi is the metre. Among the four Sāmans, these two belong to the Bhāradvāja and Pārucchepe [sections]. For those two, either Bharadvāja or Parucchepa is the seer. The latter two are the Avabhṛtha-sāman and the Pravargya-sāman; for those two, Bṛhaspati is the seer. ||465||
For the verse beginning with "tuva tyad naryam," Gṛtsamada is the seer; Indra is the deity; Aṣṭi is the meter; and for the Sāman, Īṣa is the seer of the Āiṣa [Sāman]. ||466||
Thus ends the twelfth section in the fourth chapter concerning Indra.
There are three hundred and fifty-two Ṛg-verses addressed to Indra.
Thus ends the triad of chapters concerning Indra.
The Fifth Chapter: The Pāvamāna Section;
First Sub-section.
The verses beginning with "uccā ta" are forty-four Gāyatrīs;
indeed, Soma alone is the deity of all the Pāvamānī hymns.
The specific deity in each respective case will be described there.

"uccā te jātamandhasaḥ"—this *ṛc* has Āmahīyu as its seer (*ṛṣi*), the *gāyatrī* as its meter, and Pavamāna Soma as its deity. There are thirteen *sāmans* here. Among them, the first is the Ājīga; the second is the Ābhīka. Prajāpati is the seer of the Ājīga; the seers of the Ābhīka are the Aṅgirases. The third is the Pāvamāna Ṛṣabha, or the Aukṣṇorandhra; Prajāpati is its seer, or Ukṣṇorandhra Kāpya. The fourth is the Ābhīka; its seers are the Aṅgirases.

The fifth and sixth [Sāmans] belong to Bābhrava; for those two, the seer is Babhru Kaumbhya. The eighth and ninth belong to Śaiśava; for those two, the seer is Prajāpati. The twelfth is the Sāman of Indrāṇī; its seer is Indrāṇī. The thirteenth is the Āmahīyava; its seer is Amahīyu. ||467||

Regarding the verse *svadiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā*: Madhucchandas is the seer (*ṛṣi*); Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*); Soma, being praised, is the deity (*devatā*). There are nine *sāmans* here; among them, two are the *Ājigas*. For those, Āji is the seer. The second and third are the *Surūpas*; for those two, Prajāpati is the seer. The fourth and fifth are the *Jamadagneḥ Śilpe*; for those two, Jamadagni is the seer. The sixth is the *Saṃhitam*; for that, Jamadagni is the seer. The sixth is the *Saṃhitam*.

Its seer is Jamadagni. The seventh [is] the *śakuna* of Vasiṣṭha; its seer is Vasiṣṭha. The eighth [is] the *gambhīra* of Jamadagni; its seer is Jamadagni. The ninth is the *saṃhita*; its seer is Prajāpati. ||468||

"Flow forth, O showerer, in a stream"—this is the verse. Its seer is Bhr̥gu Vāruṇi or Jamadagni. There are nine Sāmans here; of these, the first two are Somasāmans. Their seer is Soma. The third is Āśubhārgava; its seer is Bhr̥gu. The fourth and fifth are Vaiśvadevas; their seers are the Viśvedevas. The sixth and seventh are Indrasāmans; their seer is Indra. The eighth and ninth are Yauktāśvas; their seer is Yukta Āṅgiras. ||469||

The seer of the *ṛc* beginning with "yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" is Āmahīyuḥ. Here there are six *sāmans*. Of these, the first is Bhāsa; its seer is Atri. The second is Somasāman; its seer is Soma. The third is Prājāpatya; its seer is Prajāpati. The fourth is also Somasāman; its seer is Soma. The fifth is also Bhāsa; its seer likewise is Atri. The sixth is Adhyardheḍa Somasāman; its seer also is Soma. ||470||

The ṛc, "tisro vāca udīrate," has Trita as its seer (ṛṣi). Here too there are six sāmans. Of these, the first and second are the Vaiṣṭambhas; their seer is Viṣṭambha. The third and fourth are the Pāṣṭhauhas; their seer is Ṣaṣṭhavāḍ Āṅgirasa. The fifth is the Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha; its seer is also Viṣṭambha. The sixth is also a Pāṣṭhauha; its seer is also Ṣaṣṭhavāḍ Āṅgirasa. ||471||

Regarding the verse beginning with *indrāyendo marutvataḥ*, Kāśyapa is the seer (*ṛṣi*). There are eight Sāmans here. Of these, the first is the *iṣovṛdhīya*; its seer is Prajāpati. The second is the *indrasāman*; its seer is Indra. The third and fourth are dedicated to the Viśvedevas; their seers are the Viśvedevas. The fifth and sixth are dedicated to Agni; their seer is Agni. The seventh is dedicated to the Viśvedevas; its seers are the Viśvedevas. The eighth is dedicated to Agni; its seer is Agni. ||472||

For the *ṛc* beginning with "asāvyaṃśurmadāya," Jamadagni is the seer (*ṛṣi*). There are eight *sāmans*; of these, the first four are the *Śaiśavas*. Their seer is Śiśu Āṅgirasa. The subsequent ones, beginning with the fifth, are the *Cyāvanas*; their seer is Cyavana Bhārgava. ||473||
"Pavasva takṣa sādhanaḥ"—these are the verses; Dṛḍhacyuta Āgastya is the seer. There are two Sāmans belonging to Prajāpati; Prajāpati is their seer. ||474||

The ṛc “pari svāno giriṣṭhāḥ” has Kaśyapa Asita as its seer (ṛṣi). Here there are six sāmans. The first four are Vaidanvatas; their seer is Vidvān Bhārgava. The fifth and sixth are padastobhas; the seer of those two is Raji Āṅgirasa. ||475||
The seer of the verse beginning "pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" is Asita Kāśyapa; the seer of the two Sāmans belonging to the Raurava cycle is the Gandharva Ūrṇāyu. ||476||
Thus ends the first section in the fifth chapter concerning the Pāvamānī verses. ||1||
"pra somāso madacyutaḥ"—Śyāvāśva is the seer of this Ṛc; Subhari is the seer of the Saubhara Sāman. ||477||
The seer of the verse beginning "pra somāso vipaścitaḥ" is Trita; the seer of the Sāman Saubhara is Subhari; and for the two [verses] following, Subhru is the seer. 478.
The seer of the *ṛc* "Flow on, O Indu, as a bull, pressed" is Āmahīyu; the seer of the *sāman* "Indra-vṛṣaka" is Indravṛṣa. ||479||
For the verse beginning with "vṛṣā hyasi bhānunā," the seer is Bhṛgu; for the two Sāmans, Indra and Vṛṣaka, the seer is Indra. ||480||
For the verse beginning with "induḥ pavitre," Kaśyapa is the seer; for the three Sāmans of Babhru Kaumbhya, Babhru Kaumbhya is the seer. ||481||
The seer of the verse beginning with "asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ" is Kaśyapa; the seer of the three Sāmans of Babhru Kārtaveśa is Babhru Kārtaveśa himself. ||482||
The seer of the verse beginning "Pavasva deva āyuṣak" is Nidhruvi Kāśyapa; the seers of the two Sāmans, Śāmmada and [the other], are Āṅgirasa Śāmmada. ||483||
The seer Asita [is the author] of the verses beginning with "pavamāno ajījanat"; Vasiṣṭha is the seer of the two Sāmans that have Janitra as their deity. ||484||
For the verses beginning with "pari svānāsa indavaḥ," the seer is Asita; for the Sāmans concerning the sporting Maruts, the seer is the Maruts themselves. ||485||
"Pari prāsiṣyadat kaviḥ"—this [verse] has Asita as its seer (ṛṣi). Of the Sāman belonging to Uśanas, Uśanas Kāpya is the seer. ||486||
Thus ends the second section in the fifth chapter on the Pāvamānī verses. ||2||
The third section:
the seer of the verse beginning "upo ṣu jātam apturam" is Āmahīyu; the seer of the three *yāma* chants is Yama. ||487||
"Punāno akramīt" is the ṛc; Bṛhanmati is the seer. Of the Vairūpa Sāman, "aṅkateḥ," Aṅkati Virūpa is the seer. ||488||
The seer of the verse beginning with "aviśan kalaśam" is Jamadagni; the seers of the two Sāmans belonging to Uśanas are Uśanas.
The seer of the Ṛgvedic verse beginning with "asarji rathyaḥ" is Prabhūvasu; the seer of the Sāman, specifically the Somasāman, is Soma. |||490||
"Apaghnan pavase mṛdhaḥ"—the seer of this ṛc is Nidhruvi; of the Sāman, namely the Somasāman, the seer is Soma. ||492||
For the ṛc beginning with "ayā pavasva dhārayā," the seer is Nidhruvi; for the Sāman of Indra Vārtraghna, the seer is Indra Vṛtrahan. ||493||
The seer of the *ṛc* "sa pavasva ya āvitha" is Āmahīyu; the seer of the *sāman* "indrasya vārtraghnasya" is Indra Vṛtrahā. ||494||
The seer of the verse beginning with "ayā vīti pari srava" is Āmahīyu; the seer of the three Soma-sāmans is Soma. ||495||
"Pari dyukṣam" is the verse; Ucathya is the seer of the verse. Regarding the Sāman of Bhāradvāja, Bhāradvāja is the seer. ||496||
Thus ends the third section of the fifth chapter in the Pāvamānī hymns. ||3||
The fourth section:
for the *ṛc* "acikradad vṛṣā hariḥ," the seer is Medhātithi; for the *sāman* Vārṣāhara, the seer is Vṛṣāhari. 497.
For the verse beginning "ā te dakṣaṃ mayo bhuvam," the seer is Bhṛgu; for the three Vārśa Sāmans, the seer is Vṛśo Jāna. (Gṛhyasaṃgraha 9.20–22) || 498 ||
For the verse beginning "O Adhvaryu, [the Soma] pressed with stones," the seer is Ucathya; for the two *Sāmans* of Indra belonging to the Vairūpa [tune], the seer is Indravr̥ṣa. 499.
The seer of the *ṛc* "taratsamandī dhāvati" is Avatsāra; the seer of the *sāman* "taranta" is Vitadaśva. ||500||
The seer of the verse beginning "ā pavasva sahasriṇam" is Nidhruvi; the seer of the Sāman, the Somasāman, is Soma. ||501||
The seer of the verse beginning with "anupratnāsa āyavaḥ" is Asita; the seer of the Sāman "sūryasya sāmnaḥ" is Sūrya. ||502||
The seer of the Ṛgvedic verse beginning with "arṣā soma" is Bhṛgu; the seer of the three Sāmans belonging to the Dārḍhacyuta family is Dṛḍhacyuta. ||503||
For the ṛc beginning with "vṛṣā soma dyumān asi," Kaśyapa is the seer; for the sāman of Indra Vṛṣaka, Indra is the seer. ||504||
For the verse beginning with "iṣe pavasva," Kaśyapa is the seer; for the Sāman called Aiṣa, Iṭ is the seer. || 505 ||
For the *ṛc* "mandrayā soma," the seer is Asita; for the *sāman* of Śyāvāśva, the seer is Śyāvāśva. ||506||
The seer of the *ṛc* "ā yāhi soma sukṛtyayā" is Bhārgava; the seer of the *sāman* belonging to Āyāsya is Āyāsyāṅgirasa. ||507||
For the *ṛc* "ayaṃ vicarṣaṇir hitaḥ," Jamadagni is the seer (*ṛṣi*). For the *sāman* addressed to Agni, Agni is the seer. ||508||
"Pro na indro mahe tu na" is the ṛc; Āyāsya Āṅgirasa is the seer. For both the sāman and the two āyāsya [hymns], he alone is the seer. || 509 ||
Striking down the adversaries, he flows; the seer of the *ṛc* is Āmahīyu, and the seer of the *sāman* of Bhāradvāja is Bharadvāja. ||510||
Thus end the forty-four *pāvamānī* verses in the *gāyatrī* meter.
Thus ends the fourth section in the fifth chapter concerning the Pāvamānī verses.
Fifth Section:

Now follow the twelve verses in the Bṛhatī meter. For these verses, the seven seers—Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Gautama, Atri, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, and Vasiṣṭha—are the respective seers for each verse. The meter is Bṛhatī; the deity is Pavamāna Soma.

In the verse "punaḥ soma dhāraya," there are sixteen *sāmans*. Of these, the first is the *Āyāsya* *sāman*; its seer (*ṛṣi*) is Āyāsya Aṅgiras. The second is the *Māṇḍava*; its seer is Maṇḍu. The third and fourth are the *Āpadas* and *Soma-sāman*; their seers are Vasiṣṭha and Soma, respectively. The fifth is the *Āyāsya*; its seer is Āyāsya. The sixth is the *Māṇḍava*; its seer is Maṇḍu. The seventh is the *Udvat-prājāpatya*; its seer is Prajāpati. The eighth is the *Āyāsya*.

The seer of that [ninth sāman] is Āyāsya; the ninth is the Kaṇvarathantara, whose seer is Kaṇva. The tenth is the Tiraścīna-āyāsya, whose seer is Āyāsya. The eleventh is the Prajāpateḥ-sado-viśīya, whose seer is Prajāpati. The twelfth and thirteenth are Jamadagneḥ-svavāsinī; the seer of those two is Jamadagni. The fourteenth is Vasiṣṭhasya-plava, whose seer is Vasiṣṭha. The fifteenth is Agneḥ-raurava, whose seer is Ruru. The sixteenth is Yaudhājaya, whose seer is Yudhājit. |||511||

The verses beginning with *parīto ṣiñcatā sutam* have been stated; they belong to the Seven Seers (*saptarṣayaḥ*). Here, in this *aṣṭādaśasāman*, there are chants. Among them, Indra is the seer for the third and fourth [sections], which belong to Bharadvāja; for those two, Bharadvāja is the seer. For the fifth and sixth, belonging to Ābhīśava, Ābhīśu is the seer. For the seventh and eighth, belonging to Māṇḍava, Maṇḍu is the seer. For the ninth and tenth, belonging to the Aṅgirases, they are the Abhivāsa and Parivāsa; for those two, the Aṅgirases are the seers. For the eleventh and twelfth, belonging to Vaiṇasomakratu.

For those two [the 11th and 12th], the seers are Veṇu and Somakratu; or alternatively, the twelfth is the Māṇḍava, whose seer is Maṇḍu. The thirteenth and fourteenth are the Gūdas of Prajāpati, or alternatively, the Pratodas of Kaśyapa. For those two, if they are the Gūdas, Prajāpati is the seer; if they are the Pratodas, Kaśyapa is the seer. The fifteenth and sixteenth are the Gauṣṭhapuṃstanīyas of the Aṅgirases; for those two, Aṅgiras is the seer. The seventeenth is the Mahāraurava; its seer is Ruru. The eighteenth is the Mahāyaudhājaya.

Yudhājit is the seer of that [hymn]. The verses beginning with "O Soma, you who are pressed" have already had their seers stated. There are four Sāmans here, the Soma-sāmans; Prajāpati in the form of a horse, or Soma, is the seer of the four.

The verses beginning with "pra samaḥ devavītaye" have been stated; the seers are [as follows]. There are five *sāmans*. The first is the *triṇidhana* of Agni; its seer is Agni Tsāya. The second is the *sāman* of Agni Vaiśvānara; its seer is Agni Vaiśvānara. The third is the *dvihiṃkāra* Vāmadevya; its seer is Vāmadeva. The fourth and fifth are the *utsedha* and *niṣedha* of the Aṅgirases; their seer is Aṅgīrasa. ||514||
The Ṛṣis of the verses beginning with "soma uṣvāṇaḥ sotṛbhiḥ" have been stated; there are six Sāmans, and their Ṛṣi is Soma, or alternatively, Aśva. ||515||

The seers of the previously mentioned verses beginning with "tava aham soma raraṇa" [RV 8.48.3] are the same; there are five *sāmans*. Of these, two are dedicated to Viṣṇu, or rather, belong to Viṣṇu; for those two, Viṣṇu is the seer. The final three are the *āṅgirasas*; for them, the Aṅgirases are the seers. ||516||

The verses beginning with *mṛjyamānaḥ sṛhastyā* have been stated; their seers are as follows. There are eight Sāmans. Of these, the first three are the Aukṣṇorandhras. Their seer is Ukṣṇorandhra Kāpya. The fourth, fifth, and sixth are the three Āgneyas; their seer is Agni. The seventh is the Aukṣṇorandhra; its seer is Ukṣṇorandhra Kāpya. The eighth is the Vājijit; its seer is Prajāpati. ||517||

The verses beginning with *abhi sobhāsa āyavaḥ* are said to have the seers (*ṛṣi*) as their subject. There are eight *sāmans*. Among them, the first two belong to the Viśvedevas; the Viśvedevas are the seers of those two. The third and fourth are the *Indrasāmans*; Indra is the seer of those two. The fifth is the *Svapṛṣṭha-Āṅgirasa*; the Āṅgirasas are its seers. There are three *Indrasāmans*; Indra is the seer of them all. ||518||
"O Soma, being purified, thou art watchful"—thus the verses are stated; the seers are [the same]; the *Svara-pṛṣṭha* is the *Āṅgirasa* Sāman; Tsāyaṅgirā is the seer. |||519||
The verses beginning with "For Indra the exhilarating drink flows" have been spoken by the seers. There are three Soma-sāmans; their seer is Soma. ||| 520 ||
The verses beginning with "pavasva vājasātama" have already been mentioned as their seers. (One Soma-sāman. Soma is the deity. ||521||
The seers of the verses beginning with "pavamānā asṛkṣata" have already been stated; the seers of the Sāman for the gods' purifier (pavitra) are the gods. (Gṛhyasūtra 1.4.522)
The Bṛhatīs are completed.
Thus ends the fifth section in the fifth chapter concerning the Pāvamānī verses. ||5||
The Sixth Section.
Now follow the verses in the Triṣṭubh meter; twenty-two verses will be presented in two sections.

*Pra tu drava* is the *ṛc*; the seer is Uśanas. Here there are five *sāmans*. Of these, the first is the Auśana; its seer is Uśanas. The next two are the *Vṛśasya-jāna-abhīvarta*s; their seer is Vṛśo Jāna. The fourth and fifth are the Auśanas; their seer is Uśanas. Or, all five may belong to Uśanas. ||523||
"Proclaiming poetic wisdom like Uśanas"—this is the *ṛc*. Vṛṣagaṇa Vāsiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*). There are four *sāmans* here; all are by Varāha. Varāha is the seer. ||524||

Regarding the verse *tisro vāca īrayati pra vahnir*, Parāśara is the seer (*ṛṣi*). Here there are thirteen *sāmans*. There are ten [sāmans] consisting of the first quarter-verse as its refrain (*pratīka*), distinguished by various *stobhas* such as *hoihā*, *hā hoī*, and so forth. There is one [sāman] consisting of the second quarter-verse as presented with another *stobha*: *ohā ohā*. Then there is one consisting of the third quarter-verse as presented with another *stobha*. Furthermore, there is one consisting of the fourth quarter-verse as presented with another *stobha*. Thus, there are thirteen *sāmans*. Among these, the first three are the *Aṅgirasāṃ Saṃkrośāni*.

For those [two], the seer is Aṅgiras; for the fourth and fifth [verses], which are the Sāmasarasī, Aṅgiras is the seer. For the sixth and seventh, which are the Viśāle of Veṇu, Veṇu is the seer. For the eighth and ninth, which are the Tantrāntatre of Gautama, Gautama is the seer. For the tenth and eleventh, which are the Yamike of Agastya, Agastya is the seer. For the twelfth and thirteenth, which are the Vāravantīye of Indra, Indra is the seer. Or, in the case where the twelfth and thirteenth are the Kālakākranda of the Maruts or the Jyāhnoḍau, in that alternative, the Maruts are the seers. ||525||

The seer of the verse beginning with "asya preṣā" is Vasiṣṭha. Therein are six Sāmans belonging to Vasiṣṭha. Among them, five Vasiṣṭha-sāmans are presented by their initial phrases (*pratīka*) according to their various *stobha* insertions. The sixth here is the *ihavat-vāsiṣṭha*. Thus, there are six Vasiṣṭha-sāmans. ||526||

"Soma flows, the progenitor of hymns"—this is the Ṛg-verse; its seer is Pratardana. Here there are four Sāmans. Of these, the first two belong to Vasiṣṭha; thus, there are eight [Sāmans] belonging to Vasiṣṭha, and their seer is Vasiṣṭha. The latter two are the "progenitors" (janitra) of Vasiṣṭha; their seer is Vasiṣṭha. ||527||

Regarding the verse beginning with "abhi tripṛṣṭham," Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*). The *sāman* is the *vratopoha* of the Aṅgirases; its seer is Aṅgiras, or it is the *saṃpā* of Vasiṣṭha. In that case, Vasiṣṭha is the seer. ||528||
For the verse beginning "akrāntasamudraḥ," Praskaṇva is the seer (ṛṣi). The Sāman there is the Vainyaśva; Vyaśva Āṅgirasa is its seer. ||529||
The seer of the verses beginning with "kanikranti" is Praskaṇva; therein are two Soma-sāmans, the seers of which are Soma. ||530||
"eṣa sya te madhumān"—of this *ṛc*, Uśanas is the seer (*ṛṣi*); the *aiṣam* is the *sāman*; its seer is Iṭ. ||531||
"Pavasva soma madhumān"—the seer of this ṛc is Pratardana; the Sāman there is the Mādhucchandasa, and its seer is Madhucchandas. ||532||
Thus ends the sixth section in the fifth chapter on the Pāvamānī verses.
The seventh section:
for the verse beginning with "pra senānīḥ," Pratardana is the seer; Triṣṭubh is the meter; here there are three Sāmans belonging to Kutsa, Raya, and Adhirathi; their seer is Kutsa. ||533||
The seer of the verse *pra te dhārā madhumatīḥ* is Parāśara; of the Sāman Vaiśvajyotiṣa, the [deity] is Viśvajyotis; its seer is Viśvajyotis. ||534||
"Sing forth! Let us worship!"—thus [begin] the *ṛcas*. The seer (*ṛṣi*) is either Indrapramati or Vasiṣṭha; the *sāman* is the Vaiśvajyotiṣa. Its seer is Viśvajyotis. ||535||
The seer of the *ṛc* "pra hinvāna" is Vasiṣṭha; the *sāman* is Vaiśvajyotiṣa; its seer is Viśvajyotis. ||536||
The seer of the verse beginning with "takṣadyadī" is Dṛḍhīka Vāsiṣṭha; therein are two Vācasāmans, for which Vāk is the seer. ||537||
The verse beginning with "sākamukṣo marjayante" is by the seer Nṛmedha Kākṣīvata; there are two Sāmans upon it, both belonging to Daśaspati, and Daśaspati is the seer of those two. ||538||
For the verse beginning with "adhi yad asmin," Kaṇva is the seer; the Sāman is the beautiful one of Kaśyapa, and Kaśyapa is its seer. ||539||
"Indur vājī pavate" is the Ṛc; Indu Vāsiṣṭha is the seer. Herein are four Sāmans belonging to the descendants of Daśaspati; their seer is Daśaspati. ||540||
"Flow with this flow, O purifier"—this is the ṛc; Kutsa is the seer. Herein are three sāmans, the sāmans of Śnuṣṭi Āṅgirasa; their seer is Śnuṣṭi Āṅgirasa. ||541||
"Mahattat somo mahiṣaścakāra"—for this *ṛc*, Parāśara is the seer; for the *sāman* of Atri, Atri is the seer. ||542||
The seer of the verse beginning with "asarji vakvā" is Kaśyapa; the seer of the Sāman belonging to Vasiṣṭha is Vasiṣṭha. ||543||
The seer of the verse beginning with "apāmīvati" is Praskaṇva; the Sāman is "apāṃ sāma"; its seer is Āpaḥ; for these three, the seer is either Agni Vaiśvānara. ||544||
Thus [end] the Triṣṭubh verses.
Thus ends the seventh section in the fifth chapter concerning the Pāvamānī verses.
The eighth section: Now, concerning the Anuṣṭubh verses.
The hymn beginning with "purojitī" consists of nine verses; among these, the first is a Bṛhatī, while the remaining eight are Anuṣṭubhs. The seers for each verse will be stated separately.

Śyāvāśva is the seer of this hymn beginning with "purojitī. Here there are six *sāmans*: the first two are Nakula’s and Vāmadeva’s *preṅkhas*; the third is Mahākārtayaśa; the fourth is Aurdhvasadmana; the fifth and sixth are Śyāvāśva’s and Āndhīgava’s. For the first two, Vāmadeva is the seer; for Kārtayaśasa, Kṛtayaśas is the seer; for Aurdhvasadmana, Ūrdhvasadman is the seer; for the fifth, Śyāvāśva’s, Arcanānas is the seer; and for Āndhīgava, Andhīgu is the seer. ||545||
The seer of the verse "ayaṃ pūṣā" is Nahuṣa Mānava; there are three *krauñca* sāmans therein, and their seer is Krauñca. ||546||

The Ṛgvedic verse beginning with *sutāso madhumattamāḥ* has Yayāti Nāhuṣa as its seer (*ṛṣi*). Here there are eight Sāmans. The first and second are the two Tvaṣṭrī Sāmans; their seer is Tvaṣṭṛ. The third is the Vāsiṣṭha; its seer is Vasiṣṭha. The fourth is also a Tvaṣṭrī Sāman; its seer is Tvaṣṭṛ. The fifth is the Vāsiṣṭha; its seer is Vasiṣṭha. The sixth and seventh are the two Tvaṣṭrī Sāmans; their seer is Tvaṣṭṛ. The eighth is the Vāsiṣṭha; its seer is Vasiṣṭha. ||547||
Regarding the verse "somāḥ panta indavaḥ," the seer is Manu Sāṃvaraṇa; there are two *sāmans* upon it, both called Krauñca, and Kuñca is the seer of those two. ||548||

The *ṛc* "abhī no vājasātamam" has the seers Ṛjiśvan and Ambarīṣa. Here there are five *sāmans*. The first three are *somasaṃs* (*somasāman*s); Soma is their seer. The fifth is also [a *somasaṃs*]. The fourth is the *Krauñca*; Kuñca is its seer. ||549||
"abhī navante adruhaḥ"—this is the ṛc; Rebha and Sūnu, both sons of Kaśyapa, [are the seers] together. Herein are three sāmans belonging to the Aṅgirasas; their seer is Aṅgiras. ||550||
The seer of the verse beginning with "ā haryatāya" is Rebhasūnu Kāśyapa. Here, there are four *sāmans* belonging to the hymns of Gṛtsamada; their seer is Gṛtsamada, and the meter is *Bṛhatī*. ||551||
"Parityaṃ haryatam"—these two verses have Ṛjiśvan and Ambarīṣa as their seers; the Sāman has Ākūpāra as its seer, and for that [Sāman], Ākūpāra is the seer. ||552||
For the verse beginning with "pra sunvānāyāndhasaḥ," Prajāpati is the seer; the Sāman is Vairūpa, whose seer is Virūpa or Nṛga. ||553||
Thus [end] the Anuṣṭubhs.
Thus ends the eighth section in the fifth chapter on the Pāvamānī verses.
The ninth section: Now follow the Jagatī verses.
The seer Kavi perceived twelve Jagatī verses— the first three and the fifth— while the host of sages proclaimed the fourth and the sixth.
To the west of Nivāra, Reṇu beheld the sands three times;
Vena Bhārgava was then the seer of the verse beginning with "indrāya soma."
Vasu Bhāradvāja spoke this verse, "The Soma has been pressed";
Vatsapri [spoke] "The god"; and [the verses beginning with] "Agni is being anointed" are the ṛcas.
The seer Aṅgiras saw the twelfth verse as a purifier (*pavitra*).

Then there are twelve verses in the *jagatī* meter beginning with "abhi priyāṇi. The seer of these verses is the sage Kavi. Of the six *sāmans*, the first is the *kāva*; its seer is Kavi. The second is also the *kāva*; its seer likewise is Kavi. The third is the *vājasani*; its seer is Vājasani. The fourth and fifth are the *vājajiti*; their seer is Prajāpati. The sixth is the *kāva*; its seer is Kavi. 554.

The seer of the *ṛc* "acodaso naḥ" is Kavi Ṛṣi. Here there are six *sāmans*. The first is the *Udvat* of Bhṛgu; its seer is Bhṛgu. The second is the *Āṅgirasa*; its seer is Aṅgiras. The third *sāman* is the *Rāja*; its seer is Prajāpati. The fourth and fifth are the *Somarāja*; their seer is Prajāpati. The sixth is the *Niṣedha* of the *Simās*; its seer is Prajāpati. ||555||
The seer of the verse beginning with "eṣa pra kośe" is Kavi; the Sāman is Vāsiṣṭha; its seer is Vasiṣṭha. ||556||

The seer of the *ṛc* "pro ayāsi" is the group of seers (*ṛṣigaṇa*). Here there are five *sāmans*. The first two are by Lauśa; for these two, Luśa is the seer. The third is the *pravad-bhārgava*; its seer is Bhṛgu. The fourth is the *virūpa-tantra*; its seer is Virūpa. The fifth is the *yāma*; its seer is Yama. ||557||
"Dhartā divaḥ pavate" is the Ṛc; its seer is Kavi. Herein are two Sāmans, the Dāsaśirasī; Prajāpati is their seer. || 558 ||
"Vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate vicakṣaṇaḥ"—of this ṛc, Raibhya is the seer; the Sāman is the cow of the Maruts; the Maruts are its seers. ||559||
The seer of the verse beginning "trirasmai sapta dhenavaḥ" is the group of seers; the Sāmans are the three Yāmas, and their seer is Yama. ||560||
The ṛc beginning with "indraya soma suṣutaḥ" has Vena Bhārgava as its seer (ṛṣi). There are two sāmans, "indrāya" and "syāpāvamīvanī"; Indra is the seer of these two. ||561||
"asāvi somaḥ vṛṣā hariḥ"—this *ṛc* has Vasu Bhāradvāja as its seer (*ṛṣi*). There are three *sāman*s belonging to the Yama [cycle]; their seer is Yama. ||562||
Vatsapri Jālandana, the seer, approached the god with a Ṛc; the Sāman of the Maruts is the milch-cow. ||563||
"Añjate vy añjate"—these are the *ṛc*s; the seer is Āṅgirasa. There are three *sāman*s belonging to Kakṣīvat; their seer is Kakṣīvān. ||564||
The seer of the verse beginning with "pavitraṃ te vitataṃ" is Pavitra; its two Sāmans are Arkapuṣpa, and their seer is Āditya. ||565||
Thus end the Jagatī verses.
Thus ends the ninth section in the fifth chapter concerning the Pāvamānī verses. ||9||
The tenth section:
for the ten verses of the anuvāka beginning with "indramacchā sutā ime," the meter is uṣṇih.

The *ṛc* "indram accha sutā" has Cākṣuṣa as its seer (*ṛṣi*). Therein are five *sāmans*. In the first two, Vasiṣṭha is the seer. Pauṣkala is the fifth; its seer is Puṣkala, or alternatively Prajāpati. ||566||
The *ṛc* "pra dhanvā soma" has Manu Mānava as its seer (*ṛṣi*). Therein are five *sāmans* belonging to the Aiṣiras; their seer is Iṣira. ||567||
"Sakhāya ā ni ṣīdata"—these verses have Parvata and Nārada as their seers (ṛṣis). Herein are five Sāmans belonging to Śukta; of these, Śukti Āṅgirasa is the seer. ||568||
For the verse "taṃ vaḥ sakhāya," the seers are Parvata and Nārada; here there are three Sāmans belonging to Kārṇaśravas, for which Karṇaśravas Āṅgirasa is the seer. ||569||

The *ṛc* "prāṇā śiśurmahīnām" has Trita as its seer (*ṛṣi*). Herein there are five *sāmans*. The first two are the *Vācasāman*s; for those two, Vāk is the seer. The third and fourth are the *Indrasāman*s; for those two, Indra is the seer. The fifth is the *Preṅkhasāman*; for that, the Maruts are the seer. ||570||
For the verse beginning "pavasva devavītaye," the seer is Manu Āplava; therein are two Prājāpatya-sāmans, for which Prajāpati is the seer. ||571||

The seer of this verse, "Somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇā," is Cākṣuṣa. Here there are six Sāmans. Among them, the first two are Sujñāna; their seer is Indra. The third and fourth are Dyaute; their seer is Dyuta. The fifth and sixth are Atīṣādīya; their seer is Prajāpati. ||572||
For the verse beginning "pra punānāya vedhase," the seer is Dvita; there are two Sāmans belonging to the Soma cycle, and for those two, Soma is the seer. ||573||
For the verse beginning with "gomanna indo," Parvata and Nārada are the seers; the Sāman is the Somasāman; its seer is Soma. ||574||
For the *ṛc* "asmabhyaṃ tvā vasuvidam," the seers are Parvata and Nārada; the *sāman* is the Soma-sāman; its seer is Soma. (Garga-gītā 1182) || 575 ||
"Pavate haryataḥ" is the ṛc; its seer is Cākṣuṣa. Herein are three Sāmans concerning the glories of Soma (of which Soma is the seer). ||||576||
The seer of the twelfth verse, "pari kośaṃ madhuścutam," is Bhāradvāja; the Sāman is Bhāradvāja, and its seer is Bharadvāja. ||577||
Thus ends the section on the Uṣṇih verses.
Thus ends the tenth section in the fifth chapter on the Pāvamānī verses.
The eleventh section: Now, regarding the Kakubh verses.

Regarding the verse *pavasva madhumattama*, the seer is Gaurīvita. There are five Sāmans therein. Of these, the first is Vāsiṣṭha; its seer is Vasiṣṭha. The second and third are Sapha; their seers are the Devas. The fourth is Vāsiṣṭha; its seer is Vasiṣṭha. The fifth is Sapha; its seers are the Devas. ||578||
The Ṛgvedic verse beginning with "abhi dyumnam" has the seer Ūrdhvasadmā; here there are four Sāmans belonging to the Aiṣira group, and their seer is Iṣira. ||579||

"Ā sotā pari ṣiñcata"—this is the *ṛc*. The seer (*ṛṣi*) is Ṛjiśvan Bhāradvāja. Here there are six *sāmans*. The first three are the Kārṇaśravasas; their seer is Karṇaśravas Āṅgirasa. The remaining three are the Vācas; their seer is Vāk. ||580||

"Etam utyam madacyutam"—these are the verses; the seer is Kṛtayaśas. Here there are six Sāmans. Of these, the first two are the Kaulmalabarhiṣas; their seer is Kulmalabarhis. The third is the Śaṅku; its seer is Prajāpati. The last three are the Somasāmans; their seer is Soma. ||592||

The verse "sa sunve yā vasūnām" has Ṛṇañcaya as its seer. Here there are five *sāmans*: the first two are *lomanī*; Bharadvāja is their seer. The three following are the *somasāmans*; Soma is their seer. ||582||
Śakti is the seer of this verse beginning with "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya. Herein are four Sāmans, the Śyaita and the Uṣman; Prajāpati is their seer. ||583||

Regarding the verse *eṣa sya dhārayā*, the seer is Urur Āṅgirasa. There are five Sāmans here. The first is Gāyatrapārśva; its seers are the gods. The second is Santani; its seers are the gods. The remaining three are Somasāmans; their seer is Soma. ||584||
Thus ends the Kakubhas.
It is said that there are one hundred and nineteen Pāvamānī verses;
thus, all the Ṛgvedic hymns amount to eight hundred and fifty-five verses.
Thus ends the eleventh section in the fifth chapter on the Pāvamānī verses.
The Fifth Chapter.
The Forest Book, Sixth Chapter,
First Section.
In these [sections], there are fifty-six verses of the Āraṇyaka Sāmans;
we shall state their meters, deities, and seers in their respective places.

In this context, there are three kinds of *ṛc*s: some are studied solely for the purpose of being sung in the village (*grāmageya*); others are for the purpose of being sung in the forest (*araṇyageya*); and others are for both purposes. Regarding those that serve both purposes as well as those intended exclusively for the forest, the seers (*ṛṣi*), meters (*chandas*), and deities (*devatā*) of all these two types of *sāman*s and *ṛc*s are stated here for the sake of clarity.
The first section (*anu-vāka*) is the *Arka-parvan*.

On the verse beginning "Drink of the pressed, flavorful [juice]," there are two *sāmans* in the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*). Medhātithi is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of both; Indra is the deity of both; the *bṛhatī* is the meter. Prajāpati is the seer of the two *sāmans*, or alternatively, the Viśvedevas. ||2||

For the verse beginning with "pavitraṃ te vitatam," Pavitra is the seer (ṛṣi), Jagatī is the meter (chandas), and Soma is the deity (devatā). There are two *hāhā-hoiyā* [chants], and two *pāvīti* *sāmans* named Ariṣṭanāman; for these, the gods are the seers, and the meter and deity are as in the verse. ||3||

The Ṛgvedic verse beginning with *abhi tvā pūrvapītaye* has Medhātithi as its seer (*ṛṣi*), Bṛhatī as its meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra as its deity (*devatā*). Regarding the two Sāmans, *hāvābhī* and *abhīhā*, they are based on the [verse] beginning with *tvā pūrva*. For these two, Prajāpati is the seer; their meter and deity are the same as those of the original Ṛgvedic verse. ||4||
Thus ends the first section in the Āraṇyaka-gāna, on the festival of the Sun.
The second section:

for this verse beginning with "pibā sutasya," Medhātithi is the seer; Bṛhatī is the meter; Indra is the deity. "Hāu pibā sutā" [is the call]. (This is the divine station of Varuṇa. For that, Varuṇa is the seer; the meter and the deity are as in the preceding Ṛgveda verses. ||5||

The ṛc beginning with *bṛhadindrāya gāyata* has Nṛmedha and Purumedha as its seers (*ṛṣi*), Bṛhatī as its meter (*chandas*), and Indra as its deity (*devatā*). Therein, for the Sāman *kabṛhat*, Prajāpati is the seer of the *Bṛhaddevasthāna*. For the phrase *hāuhāuhāu*, the name is *svaritastobha*; and for *ka*, the name is likewise [stobha] everywhere. The meter and deity are the same as those of the ṛc. ||6||

"O Soma, being purified, flow in a stream"—this is the *ṛc*. The seven sages are Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Gautama, Atri, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, and Vasiṣṭha. The metre is *Bṛhatī*. The deity is Pavamāna Soma. Therein lies the *Airā* chant; (twice) the *Airāyāt*; the *Suvarā*; the *Hāhoi*; "Come again," this is the *Airayaṃ* *Sāman*. Varuṇa is its seer (*ṛṣi*). The *Ṛk* and the *Vacand* are the deities. ||7||

The *ṛc* "tavedindrāvamaṃ vasu" has the seven seers beginning with Bharadvāja as its *ṛṣis*; *bṛhatī* is the meter; Soma is the deity. Therein, the *sāman* "ka hauvā puna" is the Āṅgirasa; its *ṛṣi* is Aṅgiras; the *ṛc*, the meter, and the deity are as before. The *sāman* "auhotava" therein is the Bārhaspatya; Bṛhaspati is the *ṛṣi*; the *ṛc*, the meter, and the deity are as before. ||10||

Regarding the verses beginning with "ā tvā sahasram ā śatam": Medhātithi is the seer (ṛṣi); Bṛhatī is the meter; Indra is the deity. Therein, the Sāman is the Kauhoātva belonging to Bhāradvāja; Bharadvāja is its seer; the Ṛg-verse, the meter, and the deity are as previously stated. ||11||

"śaṃ no dīvīḥ"—Sindhu-dvīpa is the seer (ṛṣi) of this verse; Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas); the Waters (Āpas) are the deity (devatā). In that regard, the Ātharvaṇa Sāman "śannaḥ" is the chant; Atharvāṅgiras is its seer; the Ṛg-verse, the meter, and the deity are as before. ||12||

"O Indra, bring to us that which has you as its chief"—this is the *ṛc*; Bharadvāja is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Bṛhatī is the metre (*chandas*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). Therein, "O Kauha, that which has you as its chief" is the Nārada-vasu *sāman*. Naradvasu is its seer; the *ṛc*, the metre, and the deity are the same [as those of the preceding verse]. ||13||

For the verse beginning "kayā naś citra ā bhuvat," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), and Indra is the deity (devatā). Regarding "kabṛhadvāma" and "bṛhadvāma": the word "kayā" refers to the two Sāmans named Bṛhatī and Vāmadevya. For these two, Vāmadeva is the seer; the Ṛg-verses, the meters, and the deities are as previously stated. ||14||

The seer of the verse beginning with "tvām id dhi havāmahe" is Bharadvāja; the metre is Bṛhatī; the deity is Indra. The Sāman based on "au ho it tvām id dhi" is the Bṛhat; its seer is Bharadvāja; the Ṛg-verse, the metre, and the deity are as stated. ||15||
Thus ends the second section in the Āraṇyaka-gāna, on the solar festival (arkaparvan). ||2||

The third section: For the verse beginning with "indraṃ naraḥ," Vasiṣṭha is the seer; Triṣṭubh is the meter; Indra is the deity. In that regard, there are two Sāmans, *iyā-auha* and *indrannara*, belonging to Vasiṣṭha and Jamadagni respectively. For those two, Vasiṣṭha and Jamadagni are the seers; the meter and the deity are as stated for the Ṛgveda verse. ||16||

Regarding the verse beginning with *svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā*: Madhucchandas is the seer (*ṛṣi*); Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*); Pavamāna Soma is the deity (*devatā*). In that context, concerning the word *ayāma*: *svādiṣṭhayā* refers to the *arka* (the hymn) accompanied by the *svāśiras* (well-mixed soma). The *svāśiras* are the vital breaths (*prāṇa*), which are the seers. The *ṛc*, the speech, the meter, and the deity [are thus unified]. ||17||

"Dhartā divaḥ pavate" (The upholder of heaven flows pure) is a verse; its seer is Kavi, its meter is Jagatī, and its deity is Soma. Regarding this, it is said: "Dhartā" (the upholder) is a hymn (*arka*) of Dīrghatamas; its seer is Dīrghatamas, and its meters and deities are those of the *Ṛgveda* verses. 18.

The verses beginning with "pra va indrāya bṛhatā" have Nṛmedha and Purumedha as their seers (*ṛṣi*). Therein, the two *sāmans* "kapravr̥t" and "kaṣantvāno navuḥ" are the hymns (*arka*) of the Maruts. For these two, the Maruts are the seers; the *bṛhatī* is the meter; Indra is the deity. ||19||

For this verse beginning with "Agnirmūrdhā," Virūpa is the seer, Gāyatrī is the meter, and Agni is the deity. Therein, the single Sāman known as "Hoho vā agnirmūrdhā" is the Arka of Agni; for that, Agni is the seer, and the Ṛg-verse, the meter, and the deity are as stated. ||20||

"May this Pūṣan, Rayi, and Bhaga [grant us wealth]"—this verse has Nahuṣa Mānava as its seer; Anuṣṭubh is the meter; Pavamāna Soma is the deity. Regarding that, "May this Pūṣan" is a single *sāman* belonging to Prajāpati; Prajāpati is its seer; the *ṛk*, the *vac*, the meter, and the deity are the same. ||21||

"Indra is the king of the moving world and of men"—this *ṛc* has Vasiṣṭha as its seer (*ṛṣi*), Triṣṭubh as its meter (*chandas*), and Indra as its deity (*devatā*). Therein, "The two Indras" and "O you two Indras"—these two *sāmans* are the *arkas* of Indra; for these, Indra is the seer, and the *ṛc*, the meter, and the deity are the same [as the preceding]. ||22||

For this verse beginning with "yasyedaṃ ā rajoyujaḥ," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), and Indra is the deity (devatā). Therein, the single Sāman called Arkashiras belongs to Hāuhauha; its seer is Arka, and the meter and deity are those of the Ṛg-verse itself. ||23||

Then follows the *staubhika* hymn beginning with "pātīḥ"; the *arka-grīvā* is one *sāman*. Due to the absence of *ṛc* verses, there is no *chandas* (meter). The seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *sāman* is Arka, and he is also its deity. ||24||

Regarding the verse beginning with "uduttamaṃ varuṇapāśam," Śunaḥśepa is the seer (ṛṣi); Triṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ); Varuṇa is the deity (devatā). In that regard, there is one Sāman called the Varuṇārka; its seer is Varuṇa, and its meter and deity are those of the Ṛg-verse. ||25||

"Indra the men invoke at the sacrifice"—this is the *ṛc*; Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), *triṣṭubh* is the meter, and Agni is the deity. Therein [are] these two *sāmans*, "This Indra the men... and "Up to Indra the men...", which are the *arkapuṣpa* [sāmans]. Of those two, Prajāpati is the seer, *triṣṭubh* is the meter, and Indra is the deity. ||26||
Thus ends the third section in the Āraṇyaka-gāna, on the festival of the Sun. ||3||
The fourth section:

"The head of heaven, the navel of the earth" (*mūrdhānaṃ divo aratim*)—this *ṛc* has Bharadvāja as its seer (*ṛṣi*), Triṣṭubh as its meter (*chandas*), and Agni as its deity (*devatā*). Regarding that, there are three *ājyadoha* chants: *kahim-hum*, *dvidoha*, and *makacyoha*. These are the *ājyadoha* *sāmans* of Agni Vaiśvānara. For them, Agni Vaiśvānara is the seer; the *ṛc*, the meter, and the deity are as [stated] above. ||27||

Regarding the verse *surūpakṛtnumūtaye*: Madhucchandas is the seer (*ṛṣi*); Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*); Indra is the deity (*devatā*). In that context, the *Raivata-ṛṣabha* Sāman is used; its seer is Rudra; the meter and deity are those of the Ṛgveda verse. ||28||

"Drink the Soma, O Indra; let it exhilarate you"—this is the Ṛg-verse. Vasiṣṭha is the seer (ṛṣi); Virāṭ is the meter (chandas); Indra is the deity (devatā). Therein, "O thou who art eager to drink"—this is the Vairāja-Ṛṣabha Sāman. Rudra is its seer; the Ṛg-verse, the meter, and the deity are as before. ||29||

Regarding the verse beginning with "svādor itthā viṣūvataḥ," the seer (ṛṣi) is Gautama, the son of Rāhūgaṇa; the metre (chandaḥ) is Paṅkti; and Indra is the deity (devatā). Therein, the single Sāman is "oṃ svādoḥ" (the Ṛṣabha-śākkara); its seer is Rudra; and the metre and deity are as stated for the Ṛc. ||30||

(5-6) For the two verses beginning with *purojitī vo andhasaḥ* and *uccā te jātamandhasaḥ*, Śyāvāśva Āmahīyu is the seer; Anuṣṭubh and Gāyatrī are the meters; in both cases, Pavamāna Soma is the deity. Regarding these two, the *eka-sāman* is the *atīṣaṅga* of Indra; its seer is either Indra or Rudra; the meter and the deity are those of the Ṛc. ||31||

(7–8) For the two verses beginning with *asarji vakvā* and *asāvyaṃśuḥ*, Kaśyapa and Jamadagni are the seers (*ṛṣi*). Triṣṭubh and Gāyatrī are the meters (*chandas*). In both cases, the deity (*devatā*) is Pavamāna Soma. Regarding these two, the single *sāman* is "Indrasya Vasor Vā. Indra or the Vasus are the seer for those two; the meter and the deity are as stated for the *ṛc*. 32.

(9–10) *Abhī no vājasātamam taratsa mandī dhāvati*: for these two verses, the seers of the first are Ṛjiśvan and Ambarīṣa; the seer of the second is Avatsāra. The meters are Anuṣṭubh and Gāyatrī respectively. For both, the deity is Pavamāna Soma. Regarding these two, the *abhitara* [chant] with the vowel *e* is a single *sāman* belonging either to Indra or Parjanya. Indra or Parjanya is the seer. The meter and deity are those of the *ṛc*. 33.

"Dhartā divaḥ pavate" is the Ṛc; the Seer is Kavi, the Metre is Jagatī, and the Deity is Soma. In that regard, there are four *padastobhas* belonging to Prajāpati: *hāhahauvākahauvā*, *auhauhovā*, *āauhovā*, and *dhartā*. These are the four *sāmans*. For them, Prajāpati is the Seer, and the Ṛg-verses, the metres, and the deities are as [previously] stated. ||34||
Thus ends the fourth section in the Arka-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna. ||4||
The fifth section:

For the verse beginning with *carṣaṇīdhṛtam*, Viśvāmitra is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Jagatī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). Therein are three Sāmans known as the Saṃsarpas or Sarpasāmans: *abhāi*, *abhipra*, and *khacarṣaṇī*. These three are the Saṃsarpas, which are [part of] all the Sāmans. Their seers are the Sarpas; alternatively, Agni, Pṛthivī, and Vāyu are the seers. The Ṛk, the Vac, the Chandas, and the Devatā are [the respective subjects]. ||37||

Regarding the verse "tavedindrāvamaṃ vasu" (O Indra, this wealth is yours): Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Bṛhatī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). Among those [verses], the two beginning with "kha suvaḥ-suvas tava" are the Sarpasāmans; they belong either to the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*) and the sun (*āditya*), or their meters and deities are as stated in the Ṛgveda. ||36||

"Abhi priyāṇi pavate" is the Ṛc; the Seer is Kavi; the metre is Jagatī; Soma is the deity. Therein, the Sarpāya and Prasṛpā [hymns] are the Abhiprīti; the Saṃsarva and Sarpasāman are each a single Sāman. For that, the Seer is either Sarpa or Dyaus; the metre and deity are as stated for the Ṛc. ||37||

Regarding the *ṛc* beginning with "tvayā vayaṃ pavamānena soma," Gṛtsamada is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Triṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Soma is the deity (*devatā*). Therein, the two [verses] beginning with "sṛpāya" and "prasṛpā" are the two *Sarpasāmans*. For those two, the serpents, the waters, or the ocean is the seer; the meter and the deity are as stated for the *ṛc*. ||38||

For the verse beginning with "svādoritthā," the seer is Gautama, the son of Rāhūgaṇa; the metre is Paṅkti; the deity is Indra. The two verses beginning with "svādoritthā" are the Sarpasāmans. Alternatively, they belong to Māṇḍava; for those two, the seers are the Sarpas and Maṇḍu Jāmadagnya. The metre and deity are as stated for the Ṛgveda verse. ||39||
Thus ends the fifth section in the Arka-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna. ||5||

The sixth section: "O Indra, in the onsets..."—this *ṛc* has Nṛmedhas as its seer (*ṛṣi*), Bṛhatī as its meter (*chandas*), and Indra as its deity (*devatā*). Regarding this, there is one *sāman* called *triṣandhi*, namely "tvamindra" (or "auhoitvamindra"). Alternatively, it is a single *sāman* consisting of three parts. Because of the combination here of the three—Rathantara, Bṛhat, and Vāmadevya—it is appropriately named *triṣāma*. Prajāpati is its seer; the *ṛc*, the meter, and the deity are as previously stated. ||40||

Regarding this verse beginning with *baṇ mahām̐ asi*, Jamadagni is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Bṛhatī is the metre (*chandas*), and Sūrya is the deity (*devatā*). Therein, the single syllable *e* in *baṇ mahām̐ asi* constitutes one *sāman* called *yajñasārathī*. For that, Prajāpati is the seer, and the Ṛg-verse itself is both the metre and the deity. ||41||

The verse beginning with "imaṃ vṛṣaṇam" consists of a single line (*ekapadā*). Its seer (*ṛṣi*) is Vāmadeva; its meter (*chandas*) is the one-line *triṣṭubh*; its deity (*devatā*) is the Viśvedevas. In that regard, the Sāman called "Vṛṣa" begins with "imā o vā. Its seer is Prajāpati; its meter and deity are the same as those of the verse. ||42||

Then follows the verse beginning with "He who alone rules" (*ya eka id vidayate*). Gautama is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the *uṣṇih* is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). Therein is the *sāman* called *ekavṛṣa*, beginning with "He who" (*ya eka*). Prajāpati is its seer; the *ṛc*, the meter, and the deity are as previously stated. ||43||

Then, for the verse beginning with "tato yo na idam imam," Saubhari is the seer (*ṛṣi*), *kakup* is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). Therein, the *sāman* called Vidratha begins with "hovā hāi yonaḥ"; Prajāpati is its seer, and the meter and deity are as stated in the verse. ||44||

Then follows the verse beginning with "abhrātṛvyo anā tvam," whose seer is Saubhari, the meter is Kakup, and the deity is Indra. In that context, there is one Sāman called Kāhva, known as Abhrātṛvya; its seer is Prajāpati, and its meter and deity are those of the Ṛg-verse. ||45||

Then follows the verse beginning with *revatīr naḥ sadhamādaḥ*. Śunaḥśepa is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). In that regard, there are two Sāmans based on this verse, namely *hāu revā* and *rāvatā*, which belong to the Revatī [group]. For these two, Prajāpati is the seer; the meter and the deity are as stated for the Ṛgveda verse. ||46||

(8–10) *uccā te jātam andhasaḥ*, *sa na indrāya yajyave*, and *enā viśvāny arya ā it*—this is one triplet (*tṛca*). For this, Amahīyu is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the metre (*chandas*), and Pavamāna Soma is the deity (*devatā*). In that [triplet], *eṣu ucca* is one *Sāman* called Śakkaravarṇa. For this, Śakkaravarṇa is the seer; the Ṛg-verses, the metre, and the deity are as before. 47.

Regarding the verse *ayā rucā hariṇyā*, Parucchepa is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Atyaṣṭi is the metre (*chandas*), and Pavamāna Soma is the deity (*devatā*). In this regard, there is one *sāman* called *nityavat* named *eāyā*; Prajāpati is its seer, and the *ṛk*, the metre, and the deity are as previously stated. ||48||

Then follows the verse beginning with *abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ*. Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Bṛhatī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). Therein, the single Sāman known as Rathantara is based on the verse *abhi tvā śūra nonumo vaḥ*; its seer is Vasiṣṭha, and its meter and deity are those of the Ṛg-verse. ||49||

Regarding the verse *tvām id dhi havāmahe*: Bharadvāja is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Bṛhatī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). Therein, the single Sāman named *ayaṃ vāyā ut tvām id dhi* consists of seven [verses]; Jamadagni is its seer, and the Ṛg-verse, the meter, and the deity are as before. ||50||
Thus ends the sixth section in the Arka-parvan of the Āraṇyagāna.

The Seventh Section. Then: (1–2) *ākrandaya kuru ghoṣam* is one *ṛc*; *prayaccha cakram arāvṇe* is another. Thus there are two *ṛcs* in the *atirahasya*. Among them, the meter (*chandas*) of the first is *triṣṭubh*, and that of the other is *anuṣṭubh*. The deity (*devatā*) of the first is Śarva or Agni; the same for the second. For these two, there are the five-fold *pavi*-mantras and the *mahāsāmans*. For the other [of these two], there is a single *sāman* sung upon the words (*padagīta*). Its seer (*ṛṣi*) is Śarva or Agni. In the first *ṛc*, there is a single *mahāsāman* sung as *ākrandāyova*.

[The first] is *agnerharas* (the heat of Agni). Its seer (*ṛṣi*) is Rudra or Agni; its deity is also [Agni]. Then, regarding the second verse, "prayaccakram" (you have given the wheel), there are three *mahāsāmans*: two *sāmans* on the first [verse], beginning with "kās-abhyābhūḥ kakṣura"—namely, *prayaccakram*; and two *sāmans* on the second [verse], beginning with "kṣuraharasī. The two *sāmans* on the third [verse] are "mṛtyorharasī" (the heat of Death) or [alternatively, "śarvasya harasī"]. Such are their names. The seer of the first is Śarva; the seers of the second and third are Rudra or Kṣura; and the deity of the third is Mṛtyu or Śarva. 51.

"abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ"—this *ṛc* has Vasiṣṭha as its seer (*ṛṣi*), Bṛhatī as its meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra as its deity (*devatā*). Therein, the *sāman* called Śānti belonging to the two sages begins with "abhi tvā. Its seer is Prajāpati; its verse, meter, and deity are identical to those of the *ṛc*. ||52||

The verse beginning with "kayā naś citra ā bhuvat" has Vāmadeva as its seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī as its meter (chandas), and Indra as its deity (devatā). Regarding this, it is said that "kayā na" is a single Sāman called Vāmadevya, which consists of five Nidhanas. Its seer is Vāmadeva; its meters and deities are those of the Ṛg-verse. ||53||

Regarding the verse *pibā somam indra*, Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*). It has three feet and the *virāṭ* meter; Indra is the deity. In it, the single *sāman* called *vairāja* occurs in the phrase *ho i yā piba*. Its seer is Indra, or alternatively Vasiṣṭha; its meter and deity are those of the *ṛc*. ||54||

Regarding the verse *agna āyāhi vītaye*: Bharadvāja is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Agni is the deity (*devatā*). In that context, there is the *kāpriya*; "agna āyāhi" is one *sāman* dear to Agni. For that, Agni is the seer, and the Ṛg-verse, the meter, and the deity are as [previously] stated. ||55||

Regarding the verse *kayā naś citra ā bhuvat*, as before, the seers (*ṛṣi*), meters (*chandas*), and deities (*devatā*) are to be understood. In that context, there is one *sarpasāman* [named] *ekayāna* or *kalmāṣa*. Its seers are the serpents (*sarpāḥ*). The meter and deity are those of the verse itself. 56.

"I am the first-born" is a single *ṛc*. Its metre is *triṣṭubh*; its presiding deity is the one who presides over food (*anna*). In this regard, "I am the bridge" refers to the bridge named Setu, or it signifies the state of the Supreme Person (*puruṣagati*), or the state free from sorrow (*viśoka*). For that [verse], the Seer (*ṛṣi*) is Puruṣa; the metre and the deity are as stated for the *ṛc*. ||57||
Thus ends the seventh section in the Arka-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna. ||7||
The Arkaparvan is completed.
The first section of the Dvandvaparva:

therein, regarding the *dvandva* [duet] chants belonging to a single seer (*ekārṣeya*), for the verse beginning with "indraṃ naro na" (Indra, as men...), Vasiṣṭha is the seer, Triṣṭubh is the metre, and Indra is the deity. Herein are eight *dvandva-sāmans*: *Kaprāṇamāyuḥ* and *Kautabalamanohiya* are two *sāmans* concerning the out-breath and in-breath (*prāṇāpāna*) of Vasiṣṭha; Vasiṣṭha is the seer of these two. *Kenyau* and *Kāhoenyau* are two *sāmans* concerning the *ainya* [steeds] of Indra; Indra is the seer of these two. *Kaham* and *Kaihāham* are two *sāmans* concerning the two wings of the vow (*vratapakṣa*); Indrāṇī is the seer of these two.

The two Sāmans, *hāvīndrāma* and *uvāovā*, are the *ulba* (inner membrane) and *jarāyu* (outer membrane). Indrāṇī is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of these two. Their meters, verses, and deities are as previously stated. ||58||

"Upa tvā jāmayaḥ giraḥ"—this is the ṛc. Bhārgava is the seer (ṛṣi); Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas); Agni is the deity (devatā). Regarding that, there are two Sāmans, Udbhid and Valabhid. For these two, Bṛhaspati is the seer, or Indra; for the Udbhid, the Ṛg-verses, the meters, and the deities are as [previously] stated. ||59||
Thus ends the first section in the Dvandva-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna. ||1||

The second section: For Indra, sing the *Bṛhat*—these are the verses. Nṛmedha and Purumedha are the seers (*ṛṣis*). The *Bṛhatī* is the meter. Indra is the deity. In that regard, there is one *Sāman* called *Bharga*, namely the *Hāu-dhāmayat Bṛhat*.

"This is your lowest wealth, O Indra"—these are the verses. Vasiṣṭha is the seer. In that regard, the *Yaśas* *Sāman* is "How shall we praise thee? Prajāpati is the seer of those two. *Bharga* and *Yaśas* are the two *Sāmans*. Their meter is *Bṛhatī*. Indra is the deity. (60–1)

For this verse beginning with *kāyamāno vanā tvam*, Viśvāmitra is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Bṛhatī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Agni Vaidduta is the deity (*devatā*). In that regard, there are two Sāmans, *Kāyamāna* and *Auhova*; for these two, Yama is the seer, and the Ṛk, the Vāk, the Chandas, and the Devatā are [the same]. ||62||

"pra sāma devavītaye"—these [verses] have the seven sages beginning with Kaśyapa as their seers; Bṛhatī is the meter; Pavamāna Soma is the deity. Therein, "kapra soma auhīva" are two *dharmatan* Sāmans. For those two, Gharma is the seer; the Ṛgveda verses, the meters, and the deities are as [previously] stated. ||63||

"ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ"—this *ṛc* has Nahuṣa Mānava as its seer (*ṛṣi*), *anuṣṭubh* as its meter, and Pavamāna Soma as its deity. Among them, "hāvayaṃ pūṣa" constitutes the first and second [verses], and "e ayaṃ pūṣa" is the third; thus there are three *sāmans*. For these, Prajāpati is the seer, and the *ṛc*, the meter, and the deity are as previously stated. ||64||

"tvam etad adhārayaḥ"—this is the ṛc; Śrutakakṣa is the seer (ṛṣi). Regarding that, there are three Sāmans—*tvam etat āt*, *tvam etad dhau hāi*, and *āitvam etat āt*—which belong to the Varṣāhara [cycle]. Vṛṣāhari is the seer of these three. The metre is Gāyatrī. Indra is the deity. ||65||
Thus ends the second section of the chapter on pairs in the Āraṇyagāna. ||2||
The third section:

Regarding the verse beginning with *yacchakrāsi parāvati*, Rebha is the seer (*ṛṣi*). On that [verse], there are two *dyut* *sāmans*: *hāu* and *yacchakrāsī-iyayeti*. For those two *dyuts*, the seer is [Rebha]; the metre is *bṛhatī*; Indra is the deity. |||66||

The verse beginning with "abhī no vājasātamam" has Ṛjiśvan and Ambarīṣa as its seers (*ṛṣi*). In that [hymn], there are two *sāmans* called "ābhīnava" and "abhīnava"; their seer is Prajāpati; the meter is *anuṣṭubh*; and the deity is Pavamāna Soma. ||67||

Regarding the verse "yadindra śāso avratam," Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*). Therein, for the two *sāmans* beginning with "yadindra" and "śāso avratām," Turaśravas is the seer; the meter is *bṛhatī*; and Indra is the deity. ||68||
The seer of the verse beginning with "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" is Madhucchandas.
The verses beginning with "O Agni, yoke those which are yours" have Bharadvāja as their seer.

The two *sāmans* for these [two verses] are the Cow’s Milk (*dhenupayasī*). For these two, Turaśravas Prajāpati is the seer (*ṛṣi*). Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandaḥ*) for both. The first is dedicated to Pāvamāna; the second is dedicated to Agni. Soma and Agni are the deities (*devate*). (69–70)

"Arūrucad uṣasaḥ" is the seer of this verse; its metre is Jagatī; its deity is Soma. In that [hymn], there are two Sāmans, "Kasvar" and "Viśvaṃ-kajyotirviśvam"; for those two, Prajāpati is the seer, and the Ṛg-verse, the metre, and the deity are as previously stated. ||71||
Thus ends the third section in the Dvandvaparvan of the Āraṇyakaparvan. ||3||

The Fourth Section (1–3): "Indra indeed [is praised] by the Gāthins with the Bṛhat; Indra indeed [is praised] along with the two bay horses; O Indra, protect us in the contests for booty"—in these three verses there is one Sāman, the Yaṇva. The seer of the verses is Madhucchandas; the metre is Gāyatrī; the deity is Indra. For the Sāman, Prajāpati is the seer; the metre and the deity are as stated for the verse. 72.

On the triplet beginning with "uccā te jātamandhasaḥ," there is one Sāman called Kaucca, which has the apatya (descendant) as its deity. For the Ṛks, the seers, meters, and deities are those previously mentioned. For the Sāman, Prajāpati is the seer. ||73||

The verses beginning with *viśvato dāvan* have Vāmadeva as the seer (*ṛṣi*). The metre (*chandas*) is the two-footed *viṣṭārapaṅkti*. Indra is the deity (*devatā*). Regarding this, there are two *sāmans* called *khaviśvatodāvan* and *viśvatodāvan* in the *āyurnavastobha* chant; for these two, Prajāpati is the seer, and the metre and deity are those of the *ṛc* verse itself. ||74||

For the verse beginning "svādoritthā viṣūvataḥ," Gautama is the seer (*ṛṣi*), *paṅkti* is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). In that regard, there is one *sāman* called *rāyovājīya*. Its seer is Rāyovāja; its meter, speech, and deity are the same as those of the *ṛc*. ||75||

The ṛc "indro madāya" has Gautama as its seer (ṛṣi), Paṅkti as its meter (chandas), and Indra as its deity (devatā). In that [hymn], "indro mada" is one Sāman belonging to Bṛhadgiras; its seer is Bṛhadgiras, and its meter and deity are those of the Ṛk. ||76||

The ṛṣis and other details for the verse beginning *svādoritthā viṣūvataḥ* have been stated. In that context, *esvādoḥ* is one *sāman* named *Saṃkṛti*; its ṛṣis are the gods, and its *ṛc*, meter, and deity are as before. Furthermore, regarding *svādoritthā viṣūvataḥ*, *esvādoḥ ovā* is the *pārthuraśma* *sāman*; its ṛṣi is Pṛthuraśmi, and its *ṛc*, meter, and deity are as before. ||77||

Regarding the verse "ubhe yadindra rodasī" (When, O Indra, both worlds...), the seer is Marut Yauvāśva; the metre is the eight-syllable-per-foot, six-footed Mahāpaṅkti; the deity is Indra. In that [verse], there is one Sāman named Śyena; its seer is Prajāpati; and its metre, recitation, and deity are the same as those of the Ṛc. ||78||

Furthermore, regarding the verse "punah svādoḥ itthā viṣūvataḥ," the single *sāman* thereon is the *Vṛṣakama*. Prajāpati is its *ṛṣi*; the *ṛc*, the metre, and the deity are as previously stated. ||79||
Thus ends the fourth section in the Dvandvaparvan of the Āraṇyakagāna.

The fifth section: For this verse beginning with *imā nu kaṃ bhuvanā*, the seer is Bhauvana; the metre is *dvipadā viṣṭārapaṅkti*; the deities are the Viśvedevas or Indra. In that regard, there are two Sāmans, *Bhadra* and *Śreyasī*. Of these, the seer of *Bhadra* is Gautama; the seer of *Śreyasī* is Prajāpati. The metre, the word, and the deity are as previously stated. ||80||

"Acikradad vṛṣā hariḥ"—this *ṛc* has Medhātithi as its seer (*ṛṣi*), Hari as its deity, and the *gāyatrī* as its meter. In this regard, there are two *sāmans*, *hāu* and *tantu*, [derived from] *hāvotu*. For these two, Prajāpati is the seer; the *ṛc*, the word, the meter, and the deity are the same. ||81||

"Drink the Soma, O Indra"—this *ṛc* has Vasiṣṭha as its seer (*ṛṣi*), the three-footed *virāṭ* as its meter (*chandas*), and Indra as its deity (*devatā*). In this [hymn], there are two *sāmans*, "Kakha" and "Piba," which possess both *saha* and *maha*; Prajāpati is their seer, and the *ṛc*, the meter, and the deity are the same as those of the original verse. ||82||

"pra va indrāya bṛhate"—of this *ṛc*, Nṛmedha and Purumedha are the seers (*ṛṣi*); *Bṛhatī* is the meter; Indra is the deity. "Hāu pra va indrāya kaviśveṣām"—these two are the *Vārkajaṃbha* *sāmans*. Of these, Vārkajaṃbha is the seer; the *ṛk*, the meter, and the deity are as [previously] stated. ||83||

"asāvi devaṃ goṛjīkamandhaḥ"—this *ṛc* has Vasiṣṭha as its seer (*ṛṣi*), *triṣṭubh* as its meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra as its deity (*devatā*). In this regard, there are two *sāmans*, "hāhahā" and "īya," based on the words "asāvi" and "iti"; these are the *īṣ* and *viśvajyotis*. For these two, Prajāpati is the seer; the *ṛk*, the meter, and the deity are as previously stated. ||84||
Thus ends the fifth section in the Dvandva-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna.
The sixth section:

The *ṛc* beginning with "mahitrīṇām" has Satyadhṛti Vāruṇi as its seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī as its meter (*chandas*), and Mitra and Varuṇa as its deities (*devatā*). In that [section], there are two *sāmans*, "hāu mahi" and "hāu divi," based on the verse beginning with "mahitrīṇām" for those competing for wealth (*draviṇa-viṣparddhasī*). For these two, Prajāpati is the seer; the *ṛc*, the meter, and the deities are as previously stated. ||91+1||

Regarding the verse *nāke suparṇam eti*: the seer is Vena Bhārgava; the metre is Triṣṭubh; the deity is Indra. In this regard, the *auho* [interjection] is used. The *yāma* Sāman is *iyāhāu nāke suparṇam*. Its seer is Yama; its metre and deity are as those of the Ṛgveda verse. (93–1)

Regarding the verse *surūpakṛtnumūtaye*: Madhucchandas is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the metre (*chandaḥ*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). Therein, *surūpakṛtnumūtaye* is the *mādhucchandasa* Sāman; its seer is Madhucchandas, and its metre and deity are the same as those of the Ṛg-verse. ||93+1||

Now, for the verses from the *Āraṇyaka* beginning with "prathaśca yasya saprathaśca," Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Triṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Vāyu is the deity (*devatā*). For the verse beginning with "ātrāha goramanvata," Gautama is the seer, Gāyatrī is the meter, and Indra is the deity. Regarding these two, there are the two Sāmans named Śukra and Candra, [introduced by] "niyutvat" and "kaccandramātra. For those two, Śukra and Candra, Prajāpati is the seer; the Ṛg-verses, the meters, and the deities are as before. (95–6+1)
Thus ends the sixth section in the Dvandva-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna.
The Seventh Section:

The verses from the *Āraṇyaka* beginning with "When you were born, O unprecedented one" (*yaj jāyathā apūrvya*) have Nṛmedha and Purumedha as their seers (*ṛṣi*). The metre (*chandas*) is Anuṣṭubh; the deity (*devatā*) is Indra Maghavān. In that context, there are five Sāman melodies with the following vowels: *eyañjāyathāḥ*, *ehāu yajjāyathāḥ*, *ehāu auho yajjāyathāḥ*, and *havauho iyañjāyathāḥ*. For these, Vāyu is the seer; the Ṛk, the metre, and the deity are as before. 97+1.

Regarding the verse beginning with "yo rayiṃ vo rayintama," the seer is Śaṃyu Bārhaspatya; the metre is Anuṣṭubh; and Indra is the deity. In that [hymn], the sixth Svarasāman is "yorayiṃvorāyintamā. Its seer is the same, and its metre and deity are as stated for the verse. ||98+1||

Now follows the *pañcānugāna* of Viṣṇu, which is the *svarīya-sāman*. In this regard, there are four *staubhika* *sāmans*: *hāuhohāi yajñaḥ*, *pṛthivī divo mūrdhānam*, and *iḍāṃ yaccha*. Then, upon the ṛc verse *punar yajñāyathāḥ*, the fifth *svarīya-sāman* is performed preceded by the *stobha* "hāuhohāi. Thus, the single *sāman* named *pañcānugāna* is completed. Furthermore, there is one *anugāna* based on the *staubhika* [verse] beginning with "hāuhohāu indro dhenuḥ," and the second begins with "eyañjāyathā."

Thus, there are three *svarīya* Sāmans: the *dvayanugāna*, the *hāūvāk* preceded by the *stobha* "tokmayansaśiṅte yebhir vyāyañjāyatha" which has four *anugānas*, and the *pañcānugāna*. These three *svarīya* Sāmans have Viṣṇu as their seer (*ṛṣi*), and the *Ṛg* verses as their meters and deities. 99–101+1.
Thus ends the seventh section in the Dvandvaparvan of the Āraṇyakagāna.
Thus ends the second anuvāka in the Āraṇyaka chapters.
The Dvanda-parvan is completed.

In the first section of the Vrataparvan, there are two Sāmans belonging to the Vākovākya (the Dialogue) in the Staubhika [section], namely *huvevācāma* and *hu-vāivācām*. Vāc is the Ṛṣi of these two; their deity is also Vāc. || 101+11 ||

"Come hither to us, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra"—this verse has Vāmadeva as its seer (*ṛṣi*), the Gāyatrī as its meter (*chandas*), and Indra as its deity (*devatā*). In that regard, the *vrata-sāman* is that of Karṣūśaya. In that case, Karṣūśaya is the seer; the Ṛg-verse, the meter, and the deity are as before. 102+12.

*Imamūṣu tvamasmākam* is a single *sāman* named *Pratiṣṭhāna*, belonging to Prajāpati. Śunaḥśepa is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc*; the *gāyatrī* is the meter; Agni is the deity. For the *sāman*, Prajāpati is the seer; the *ṛc* itself is the meter and the deity. (103+12)
Then follows "Kaivāhiye," a single *sāman* belonging to the *staubhika* class, named after the *vyāhṛti*s of Prajāpati; its seer (*ṛṣi*) is Prajāpati. ||103+13||

Regarding the verse *kānāmayivarcaḥ*, the *Āraṇyaka-ṛc* reads *mayi varcaḥ*. This is one *sāman* belonging to Parameṣṭhin, the son of Prajāpati. Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc*; the metre (*chandas*) is *anuṣṭubh*; the deity (*devatā*) is Prajāpati. For the *sāman*, Prajāpati is the seer; the metre and deity are as those of the *ṛc*. ||104+13||
"Soma-soma" is the vow of Kṛṣṇa Āṅgirasa; it consists of single Sāmans for each [verse]. Its seer is Kṛṣṇa Āṅgirasa. 104+14.

"Saṃ te payāṃsi": Gautama is the seer (ṛṣi); Triṣṭubh is the metre (chandaḥ); Soma is the deity (devatā). Therein, "ovāsaṃ te yā payāṃsi" is one *sāman* belonging to the Soma-vow (*somavrata*). Of that, Soma is the seer; the Ṛg-verse, the metre, and the deity are as [previously] stated. 105+14.

Regarding that [verse], "tatra tvam imā oṣadhīḥ" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.2.9.2), the ṛc is "tvaṃ imāḥ"; the Sāman is the *somavrata*. Gautama is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the ṛc; the metre (*chandas*) is Triṣṭubh; the deity (*devatā*) is Soma. For the Sāman as well, Soma alone is the seer and the deity. 106+14.
Thus ends the first section in the Vrata-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna. ||1||

The second section: "Indro rājā" (Indra is King) is the Ṛk; "Kavāg dadendra" (Where has Indra gone? belongs to Bharadvāja; there is one Sāman. Vasiṣṭha is the seer of the Ṛk; Triṣṭubh is the metre; Indra is the deity. For the Bhāradvāja-vrata Sāman, Bharadvāja is the seer; the Ṛk, the metre, and the deity are as stated above. 107+14.

"Abhī navante adruhaḥ"—in this *ṛc*, "abhīnavante" is the *kavāja*; "abhīnavante" is the single *vrata-sāman* of the Bharadvājins. Rebhasūnu Kāśyapa and Ambarīṣa are the *ṛṣis*. For the *sāman* of the Bharadvājins' *vrata*, Bharadvāja is the *ṛṣi*. The metre is *anuṣṭubh*. Soma is the deity. 108+14.

The *Āraṇyaka* verse beginning with "I praise Agni, the domestic priest" (*agnim īḷe purohitam*) has Madhucchandas as its seer (*ṛṣi*), the Gāyatrī as its meter (*chandaḥ*), and Agni as its deity (*devatā*). In that regard, the *Sāman* "Hāvam" based on the mantra "I praise Agni" (*agnim īḷe*) constitutes one *Yamavrata*. ||109+14||

"Indraṃ naro na" is the *ṛc*; "kahā indrannaraḥ" is the *sāman* which has a single *yama-vrata*. Vasiṣṭha is the seer of the *ṛc*; Indra is the deity; Triṣṭubh is the meter. For the *sāman*, Yama is the seer. ||110+14||

Then follow these verses beginning with "imā u vām diviṣṭayaḥ"; Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Triṣṭubh is the meter (*chandas*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). Therein, in the two *sāmans* belonging to the vow (*vrata*) of the Aśvins, which begin with "hoihā hoihā," the Aśvins are the seers; the verse, the meter, and the deity are as previously stated. (111.14)

They conceived the first name of the cows in these two verses: "I praise Agni, the domestic priest" (*agnim īḷe purohitam*). In which [verse] did they conceive? In the verse beginning with "I praise Agni" (*agnim īḷe*). There are two *sāmans* in the ritual of the cows (*gavāṃ vrata*). Regarding the verse "They conceived" (*te manvata*), Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*); the *triṣṭubh* is the meter. Regarding the verse "I praise Agni" (*agnim īḷe*), Madhucchandas is the seer; the *gāyatrī* is the meter. In both cases, Agni is the deity. For the two *sāmans* of the cow-ritual, the cows are the seers; the meters and deities are those of the respective verses. (112–3 + 14)

Of Kaśyapa Svarvid, [the verses] beginning with "itayṛcaḥ" and "kapsubantarā-kaū kaśyapa" are two *sāmans* belonging to the Kaśyapa lineage. Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc*s; for the two *sāmans*, the meter (*chandas*) is *anuṣṭubh*; Indra is the deity (*devatā*). ||114+14||
Thus ends the second section in the Vrata-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna. ||2||

The Third Section. The two Sāmans *Kaindrāmaka* and *Havabhitvā* belong to the ritual observance (*vrata*) of the Aṅgirases. They are based on the two verses beginning with *indraṃ naro nemadhitā havante* and *abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ*. Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*) for both the verse *indraṃ naro na* and the verse *abhi tvā śūra*. For *indraṃ naro na*, the metre (*chandas*) is Triṣṭubh; for *abhi tvā śūra*, the metre is Bṛhatī. Indra is the deity (*devatā*) of both. The seers of the two Sāmans are the Aṅgirases. The metres and deities are those of the respective verses. 115–6+14.

"Samanyā yanti" is the ṛc; "Kaairaya-kaairayan" refers to two Sāmans belonging to the domain of the waters (apāṃ-vrate). The Ṛṣi of the Āraṇyaka-ṛcs is Gṛtsamada. The metre is Triṣṭubh. The deity is Apāṃnapāt Agni. For the two Sāmans, the Ṛṣis are the Āyas. The ṛc, the metre, and the deity are as previously stated. ||117+14||
For the verse beginning "udu tyam jātavedasam," Kaṇva is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), and Sūrya is the deity (devatā).
Therein, for the verses from "ā prāgāt" to "bhadrā," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ), and Night is the deity (devatā).

For those two verses, there are two Sāmans for the vows of day and night, beginning with *khaprāganyatudutyam* and *hoiāprāgāt*. For these two, Day and Night are the seers (*ṛṣi*). The meters and deities are as stated in the verses. (118–9+14)

For the verse beginning with *pra kṣasya vṛṣṇaḥ*, Bharadvāja is the seer (*ṛṣi*); Jagatī is the metre (*chanda*); Vaiśvānara is the deity (*devatā*). Regarding that, *kaūprakṣasya* is one *sāman* belonging to Viṣṇu’s vow (*vrata*). For that, Viṣṇu is the seer; the Ṛg-verse, the metre, and the deity are as [previously] stated. 120+14.

"May the Viśvedevas hear me"—this is the Ṛk. Bharadvāja and Ṛjiśvan are the seers (ṛṣis). Triṣṭubh is the meter (chandas). The Viśvedevas are the deity (devatā). Regarding that, who are the Viśvedevas? The single Sāman is the vow (vrata) of all the gods; its seers are the Viśvedevas themselves, and the Ṛk, the meter, and the deity are identical.

The *ṛc* "udu brahmaṇyāirata śravasyavaḥ" has Vasiṣṭha as its seer (*ṛṣi*), Triṣṭubh as its meter (*chandas*), and Indra as its deity (*devatā*). Regarding the two *sāmans* beginning with "ka udbrahmā," they belong to the Vasiṣṭha-vrata; for these two, Vasiṣṭha is the seer, Triṣṭubh is the meter, and Indra is the deity. ||122+14||
Thus ends the third section in the Vrata-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna. ||3||
