The fourth section: The hymn beginning with *indraṃ naro na* has the *kaviśvādhanendraṃ naraḥ* [verse] as its *indra-saṃjaya*; there is one *sāman*. Vasiṣṭha is the *ṛṣi* of the *ṛc*. The *triṣṭubh* is the *chandas*. Indra is the deity (*devatā*) of the *ṛc*. Indra is the *ṛṣi* of the *sāman*. The *ṛc*, the *chandas*, and the deity are identical for both. 123+14.

"May glory [attend] Heaven and Earth"—this is a verse from the Āraṇyaka; "How shall we praise?"—this is the *Yama* hymn of Agastya, consisting of a single *Sāman*. The seer (*ṛṣi*) of the verses is Vāmadeva; the meter (*chandas*) is Mahāpaṅkti; and the deities (*devatā*) are Heaven and Earth, Indra and Bṛhaspati, and Bhaga. For the *Sāman*, the seer is Agastya; the meter and the deity are the same as those of the verse. 124+14.

In this *ṛc*, "pra vo mahe mahe vṛdhe bharadhvam," there is one *sāman* consisting of thirty [syllables] measured by the single sound 'e' (ekāra) of Prajāpati. Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc*; Triṣṭubh is the meter; Indra is the deity. For the *sāman*, Prajāpati is the seer; the *ṛc*'s own meter and deity are as stated. ||125+14||

In this verse, *indraṃ naro na*, there is one *sāman* consisting of thirty-four syllables, beginning with *indrannaro* by means of the single letter *e*. Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc*; the meter (*chandas*) is *triṣṭubh*; Indra is the deity (*devatā*). For the *sāman*, Prajāpati is the seer; the meter, recitation, and deity are the same as those of the *ṛc*. (126+14)

In this *ṛc*, "abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ," there is one *sāman* belonging to Jamadagni, beginning with "ka hahāvabhitve. Vasiṣṭha is the *ṛṣi* of the *ṛc*; the metre is *triṣṭubh*; Indra is the deity. For the *sāman*, Jamadagni is the *ṛṣi*; the metre and deity are those of the *ṛc*. (127+14)

In this verse, "indraṃ naro na" (Indra, as men [invoke]), who is Indra? "Naraḥ" (men). "Yugyaṃ ca daśastobham" (the yoke-fellow with ten chants)—this is one *sāman*. For the *ṛc*, Vasiṣṭha is the *ṛṣi*; *triṣṭubh* is the meter; Indra is the deity. For the *sāman*, Jamadagni is the *ṛṣi*. The meter and deity are those of the *ṛk* verse. ||128+14||

"Indrasya nu vīryāṇi" is a verse from the Āraṇyaka concerning the slaying of Vṛtra. "Indrasya nu" is a single *sāman* dedicated to the slaying of Vṛtra by Indra. The seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc* is Hiraṇyastūpa; the meter (*chandas*) is *triṣṭubh*; the deity (*devatā*) is Indra. For the *sāman*, the seer is Indra; the meter and deity are those of the *ṛc*. 129+14.

In this *ṛc*, "indram naro na... [RV 8.97.1], there are two *sāmans* for King Rauhiṇa: "himkāihīndranaro" and "naro". Vasiṣṭha is the *ṛṣi* of the *ṛc*; *triṣṭubh* is the meter; Indra is the deity. For the two *sāmans*, Indra is the *ṛṣi*. The meter and deity are those of the *ṛc*. ||131+14||
Thus ends the fourth section in the Vrata-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna.

The fifth section (*khaṇḍa*): In these four *ṛks*—"Agni am I by birth," "Agni protects the tip of the inspired singer," "The men [invoke] Indra," and "O Agni, they shine"—there is one *sāman* called *ilānda* (consisting of five *anugānas*): *kaūkhā*, *agnirasmi*, *kapātyagniḥ*, *iyāindrannaro*, and *bhrājā auho*. The first is the *staubhika* *anugāna*; there are four *anugānas* in the *ṛks*. For the first and second *ṛks*, Viśvāmitra is the seer (*ṛṣi*). The meter (*chandas*) is *triṣṭup*. The deity (*devatā*) of the former is the Universal Self, the Supreme Self.

Agni is the deity of the second [verse]. Triṣṭubh is the metre of the third. For the verse beginning with "bhrājantyagne," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi); Paṅkti is the metre; Agni alone is the deity. For the Sāman known as Ilānda, Agni is the seer; the Ṛg-verses are the metre and the deity. ||132-5+14||

Then, preceded by *stobha*, there are three *devavrata* *sāmans* belonging to the *staubhika* class, beginning with "manyunā," "namauktibhiḥ," and "namonāya. The first two belong to Rudra, and the third belongs to the Viśvedevas; or alternatively, the first two belong to the Viśvedevas and the third to Rudra—so say the seers (*ṛṣis*). Due to the absence of *ṛc* verses, there is no meter (*chandas*) for these. Rudra is the deity (*devatā*) of all three. (135+16-8)

In this verse, "vasanta innu rantyaḥ," there is the single *sāman* called *yajñāyajñīya*, belonging to the spring season (*vāsanta*). Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc*; the metre (*chandas*) is *paṅkti*; the deities (*devatā*) are the seasons (*ṛtavaḥ*). Prajāpati is the seer of the *sāman*; the metre and deity of the *ṛc* are as stated above. (136+18)

In this verse, "abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ," there is one *sāman* named *ajita-jiti* (the victory of the unconquered), beginning with "abhitvā. Vasiṣṭha is the *ṛṣi* of the *ṛc*; *bṛhatī* is the meter; Indra is the deity. Prajāpati is the *ṛṣi* of the *sāman*. The *ṛc*, the meter, and the deity are as stated. ||137+18||

Upon the verse beginning with *saṃ te payāṃsi*, there is one Sāman called the *somavrata*, namely *īsantepayāḥ*. Gautama is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc*; the metre (*chandas*) is *triṣṭubh*; the deity (*devatā*) is Soma. For the Sāman, Soma is the seer; the metre and deity are as those of the *ṛc*. ||138+18||

Then, upon this verse beginning with "The ocean leaped" (*akrāntsamudraḥ*), there is one *sāman* belonging to Dīrghatamas, beginning with "He has leaped" (*āyāu akrān*). The seer (*ṛṣi*) of the verse is Parāśara; the meter (*chandaḥ*) is *triṣṭubh*; the deity (*devatā*) is Soma. For the *sāman*, the seer is Dīrghatamas; the meter and deity are those of the verse. ||139+18||
Thus ends the fifth section in the Vrata-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna. ||5||

The Sixth Section: Then follows the *Puruṣasūkta*: "The Puruṣa has a thousand heads... three-quarters of him rose upward; the Puruṣa alone is all this... such is his greatness; from him Virāj was born. Over these six verses beginning with "With what [splendor] shall he come to us? (*kayā naścitra ā bhuvat*), there is one *Sāman* called the *Puruṣavrata*, consisting of five *anugānas*: *sahasra-ūhā-u*, *tri-pād-iya-u*, *ho-puruṣa-katā-vān-asya-kha-tat-o-virāḍ*. The seer (*ṛṣi*) of these five verses is Sādhya Nārāyaṇa; the meter (*chandaḥ*) is *anuṣṭubh*; the deity (*devatā*) is Puruṣa, the Supreme Puruṣa.
The Seer of the Sāman is Puruṣa himself; its metre and deity are the Ṛc. 140-5+18.

On the verse "kayā naś citra ā bhuvat," the *anugāna* (repeated chant) is "kayā na. The *puruṣavrata* is a single *sāman* known as *ekatā*. Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc*; the *gāyatrī* is the meter; the Viśvedevas are the deity. For the *puruṣavrata* *sāman*, Puruṣa is the seer; the meter and deity are those of the *ṛc*. 146+18.

The three Sāmans known as *manyevām*, *kayā naścitra ā bhuvat*, and *punaḥ manye vām*—specifically *huvāimanye*, *vāk-kayānaḥ*, and *pratiṣṭhā-simanya*—are the vows (*vratāni*) of the three worlds. For the verses beginning with *manyevām* and *kayā naścitra ā bhuvat*, Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*). Their meters (*chandas*) are Triṣṭubh and Gāyatrī respectively. The deities (*devatā*) are Heaven and Earth (*dyāvāpṛthivī*).
Regarding these Sāmans, the seers are, in order: Heaven, the Intermediate Space, and Earth; while the meters and deities are those of the respective verses. 147+18.

In this verse, "harī ta indra śmaśrūṇi," there is one Sāman named after the Ṛṣi, namely the Ṛśya Sāman. Vāmadeva is the Seer (Ṛṣi) of the verse; Anuṣṭubh is the metre; Indra is the deity. For the Sāman, Ṛśya is the Seer; the metre and the deity are the same as those of the verse. ||150+18||
These two verses they call "aṃhomuc" (the deliverers from distress).
Thus ends the sixth section in the Vrata-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna. ||6||

The seventh section: Regarding the verse beginning with *yad varco hiraṇyasya*, there is a ten-fold chanting (*daśānugānam*) consisting of the single Sāman known as *Diśāṃvratam*. The verses are: *kāham annam*, *kāhaṃ sahaḥ*, *kāhaṃ varcaḥ*, *kāhaṃ tejaḥ*, *kāhaṃ diśaḥ*, *kāhaṃ manaḥ*, *kā vayaḥ*, *kāhaṃ hiyā*, *kāhaṃ ugraḥ*, and *kāhaṃ prathe*. Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*). The metre (*chandas*) is Anuṣṭubh. The deity (*devatā*) is the Self (*ātman*). For the Sāman and the ten-fold chantings, the quarters (*diśaḥ*) are the seers; the metres and deities are those of the verses. 151+18.
Thus ends the seventh section in the Vrata-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna.
The eighth section:
Then there is the Sāman named Kaśyapavrata, which consists of ten verses. Kaśyapa is the seer (ṛṣi) of those ten verses; such is one view.

Alternatively, there is the first *anugāna* (supplementary chant) beginning with "ka hāiū yasyedaṃ. This [sāman] originates from the *ṛc* verse "yasyedaṃ āraḥ ojaḥ," and is a single *sāman* belonging to the vow of Kaśyapa (*kaśyapavrata*). Vāmadeva is its seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Indra is the deity (*devatā*). For the *sāman*, Kaśyapa is the seer; the meter and deity are those of the *ṛc* verse. ||152+18||
*Kāho* is the second *anugāna*, known as *staubhika-kaśyapagrīva*. Its seer (*ṛṣi*) is Kaśyapa. ||152 + 19||

Regarding the verse "kaphālindrannaraḥ" (kaphālindrannara iti), the third *anugāna* based on this *ṛc*, "indrannaro na," is the *kaśyapavrata*. For that as well, Kaśyapa is the *ṛṣi*. For the *ṛc*, Vasiṣṭha is the *ṛṣi*; Indra is the deity. For the *sāman*, Kaśyapa is the *ṛṣi*; the *ṛc* and the *chandas* are the deities. ||153+19||

Then, regarding the verse beginning with "yo no vanuṣyan," the fourth *anugāna* is "kahāuhau hau hau hau hau yonovanuṣyan," known as the *kaśyavratam*. Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc*; *triṣṭubh* is the meter; Indra is the deity. For the *sāman*, Kaśyapa is the seer; the meter and deity are those of the *ṛc*. ||154+19||

"Kemāḥ" is the heart of Prajāpati; it is the fifth *staubhika* *anugāna*, the *kaśyapavrata*. Kaśyapa is its seer (*ṛṣi*). Prajāpati is the deity (*devatā*). Its meter (*chandas*) is *ṛgbhavān*. 154+20.
Then follows the sixth *staubhika* *anugāna*, called *keḍā*, which is named after the *saṃkṣāra* of the *iḍās*. Prajāpati is its seer (ṛṣi). ||154+21||
For the Kaśyapavrata, the seer is Kaśyapa; the meters and deities are those of the Ṛgveda. ||155+21||

Then, regarding the verses beginning with *tataḥ katemanvakhasaharṣabhā* and *gavāṃ vrata dve anugāne te manvate*: Vāmadeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Triṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Agni is the deity (*devatā*).
Regarding the verses beginning with "saharṣabhāḥ," Vāmadeva is the seer (ṛṣi), the Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ), and the cows are the deity (devatā).

In the case of the *sāman* and the *gavām vrata*, the cow itself is the seer (*ṛṣi*), and it is also the deity (*devatā*). For the *ṛk*, the meter (*chandas*) and the deity are the same as those of the *sāman*. 156–7 + 21.

Then follows the tenth *anugāna*, named "The Tail of Kaśyapa," based on the *ṛc* beginning with "Agnir asmi janmanā jātavedāḥ. Viśvāmitra is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc*; the metre (*chandas*) is *triṣṭubh*; Agni is the deity (*devatā*). For the *sāman*, Kaśyapa is the seer; the metre and deity are the same as those of the *ṛc*. ||158+21||

Then, [the verses] "iti" and "svayaṃskunvāi" are the two names for the concealment (*nihnava*) and non-concealment (*abhinihnava*) in the *staubhika* *anugāna*; or they are the two names for the ox-cart (*anaḍudrata*) in the *staubhika* *anugāna*. Prajāpati is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of these two; because of the absence of *ṛc* verses, there is no meter (*chandas*). || 158+22-3 ||
Thus ends the eighth section in the Vrata-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna. ||8||
The Vrataparvan is completed.
Now begins the Śukriya section, the first chapter.

Therein, for the verse beginning with *agnirmūrdhā*, the first Sāman of Agni’s vow is the *kabhrājā* [tune] on the words *agnermūrdhā*. The seer (*ṛṣi*) of the verse is Virūpa; the meter (*chandas*) is Gāyatrī; the deity (*devatā*) is Agni. For the Sāman, the seer is Agni; the verse, the meter, and the deity are as stated above. 159+23.

Then, upon this verse beginning with "ayā rucā hariṇyā," the second *sāman* is "Bhrāja ayā rucā," which is the vow (*vrata*) of Vāyu. Parucchepa is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the verse; *Atyaṣṭi* is the meter (*chandaḥ*); Pavamāna Soma is the deity (*devatā*). For the *sāman*, Vāyu is the seer; the meter and deity are those of the verse. ||160+23||

On the verse beginning with *prakṣasya vṛṣṇo*, there is the *kau hā vayoho* chant; the *sāman* is the *mahāvaiśvānaravrata*. The seer (*ṛṣi*) of the verse is Bhāradvāja; the meter (*chandas*) is Jagatī; the deity (*devatā*) is Vaiśvānara. For the *sāman*, the seer is Vaiśvānara; the verse, meter, and deity are as stated above. ||162+23||

Now, regarding the verse "kāyamāno vanā tvam" (VS 15.40), the Sāman is the Mahāvaiśvānara-vrata, beginning with "om kāyamānaḥ. Viśvāmitra is the seer of the verse; Bṛhatī is the meter; Vaidyuta Agni is the deity. Vaiśvānara is the seer of the Sāman; the deities of the verse and the Sāman are identical. 162+23.

In the verse "agna āyūṃṣi," the *sāman* is the radiance of the sun. The seers are the hundred Vaikhānasas; the meter is *gāyatrī*; the deity is Agni Pavamāna. For the *sāman*, the seer is Sūrya; the meter and deity are as stated for the verse. 163+23.

In the verse "Agnirmūrdhā," the *sāman* is *abhrāja*, the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛc* is Virūpa, the meter (*chandas*) is Gāyatrī, and the deity (*devatā*) is Agni; for the *sāman*, the seer is Sūrya, while the meter and deity are the same as those of the *ṛc*. ||164+23||

The two Sāmans, *Vikarṇa* and *Bhāsa*, are based on the two Ṛks: "vibhrāḍ bṛhat pibatu somyam" and "prakṣasya vṛṣṇo. In the Ṛk beginning with "vibhrāḍ," Sūrya is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Jagatī is the meter (*chandas*), and Sūrya is the deity (*devatā*). In the Ṛk beginning with "prakṣasya vṛṣṇo," Bharadvāja is the seer, Jagatī is the meter, and Vaiśvānara is the deity. For the two Sāmans, *Vikarṇa* and *Bhāsa*, Vāyu or Mṛtyu is the seer; the meters and deities are those of the respective Ṛks. 165–6+23.

Then follows the single *mahādivākīrtya* Sāman on the verse beginning with "vibhrāḍ bṛhat. It has ten *anugānas*. The first six *anugānas* are *staubhika*: *kāyuḥ*, *evāhi*, *vayomanas*, *vayaḥprāṇāḥ*, *vayomanāḥ*, and *hoihauveti ūrdharmavidharmaḥ*. These six *staubhika* *anugānas* correspond to the head, neck, shoulders, bones, excrement, and wings. The verse beginning with "vibhrāḍ" belongs to Sūrya as the *ṛṣi*; its metre is *jagatī*; the deity is Sūrya. For the *mahādivākīrtya* Sāman, Indra is the *ṛṣi*; the metre is *jagatī*; the deity is Sūrya. ||167+24-9||

The *upari-bhūmi*, the *dyauḥ-kajyotis*—these three are the *anugānas*; those designated as the two thighs and the tail are the *staubhikas*. Thus, the *mahādivākīrtya* consists of ten *anugānas*. This, indeed, they call the "Suparṇa. ||167+30-31|||

Now follows the Sāman named Ādityahṛdaya. It is a single Sāman called Ādityavrata, consisting of twenty-one or twenty-two *anugānas*, performed upon the eleven verses beginning with "citraṃ devānām. Together with the *staubhika-anugānas*, the collective name for the twenty-one *anugānas* is Ādityavrata. Among these, the specific name for the first *staubhika-anugāna*, "santvā bhūtāny airayan," is "vaiśvadevāḥ samairayaḥ saṃśanāni bhūtavat. (167+33)

Then follows the second *anugāna*, consisting of two verses beginning with "The wondrous one moves within the gods" (*citraṃ devānām antaścarati*). For the verse "The wondrous one among the gods" (*citraṃ devānām*), Kutsa is the seer (*ṛṣi*), *triṣṭubh* is the meter, and Sūrya is the deity. For the verse "He moves within the luminous realms" (*antaścarati rocanā*), the Sarparājñas are the seers, *gāyatrī* is the meter, and Sūrya is the deity. These two verses constitute the second *anugāna* known as the *ādityavrata*. Āditya is the seer of this *sāman*; the *ṛc*, the meter, and the deity are as stated above. (169–70 + 32)
Thus ends the first section in the Śukriya-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna.
The second section:

Regarding the verse of the Sarparājñī, "āyaṃ gauḥ pṛśnirakramīt," there are two Sāmans—the *Āyaṅgauḥ* and the *Gandharvāpsarasāmānandapratinandau*—which serve as the third and fourth *anugāna*s. The seers (*ṛṣi*) of the verse are the Sarparājñas; the meter (*chandas*) is Gāyatrī; the deity (*devatā*) is Sūrya. For the Sāman, Sūrya alone is the seer, and he is also the deity; the meter is the same as that of the verse. 171+32.

The fifth *anugāna*, named *sūryātiṣaṅga*, consists of these two verses: "ud u tyam" and "citram". For the verse "ud u tyam", the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Praskaṇva; for the verse "citram devānām", the seer is Kutsa. The meter (*chandas*) of "ud u tyam" is *gāyatrī*; the meter of "citram devānām" is *triṣṭubh*. The deity (*devatā*) of both is Sūrya. Sūrya is the seer of the *sāman*; the meters and deities are those of the respective *ṛc*s. ||172-3+32||

"kasā u bhrājate" is the sixth *anugāna* of the *staubhika* class, named after the dwelling-place (*sadhastha*) of Indra. Its seer (*ṛṣi*) is Indra. Due to the absence of *ṛc* verses, it has no meter (*chandas*). The deity (*devatā*) is Sūrya. ||173+33||

In this verse, "antaścarati rocanā," there is the seventh *anugāna* named Bhūtika, with the refrain "auho auho vā antar. The verse "antaścarati rocanā" is by Sarparājñī; for the *sāman* Bhūti of the Maruts, the Maruts themselves are the seers.
On this verse, "āyaṃ gauḥ," there is the eighth *anugāna* chant, the *sāman* called *khendurāyaṅgauḥ*.
"In the phrase 'antaścarati rocanā,' the word 'antar' (within) refers to the sky; this is one *sāman*, the ninth *anugāna*."
Regarding the verse "triṃśaddhām virājati," the tenth Anugāna is the single Sāman known as Khāyastriṃśaddhāma.

The seers of the three *ṛc*s are the Serpent Kings (*sarparājānaḥ*). Of the three *sāman*s, the seers are the Serpent Kings, or the serpent named Arbuda. The meter of the *ṛc*s is *gāyatrī*; the deity is Sūrya. For the *sāman*s, the meters and deities are those of the *ṛc*s. (175–7 + 33)

Then follows the eleventh *anugāna*, the *staubhika* named "Dharmarocana," beginning with the words "tata udyamllokānarocayaḥ. Its seer (*ṛṣi*) is Dharma; its deity (*devatā*) is Sūrya. Since there is no *ṛc* verse, there is no meter (*chandas*); however, some say the meter is *anuṣṭubh*. ||179+34||

There are six *paridhi* chants belonging to Indra. Two are *ka bhrājā ud u tyam* and *ka śukrā ud u tyam*. In the three verses beginning with *ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam* and *apatye tāyavo yathā adṛśyann asya ketavaḥ*, there are two *sāmans* named *paridhi* in the twelfth and thirteenth *anugānas*. For the verse *ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam*, Praskaṇva is the seer (*ṛṣi*). For the two verses beginning with *apatye tāyavo yathā adṛśyann asya*, Praskaṇva is the seer. The meter (*chandas*) for all three is *gāyatrī*. The deity (*devatā*) is Sūrya. For the two *sāmans*, Indra is the seer. The meter and deity are those of the *ṛc* verses themselves. (178–80 + 34)

Then, regarding the three verses beginning with *taraṇir viśvadarśato 'tyaṅga devānāmiyenā pāvakacakṣasā*: in these three ṛks, there are two *paridhisāmans* (boundary-chant melodies), namely *kabhūtātaraṇiḥ* and *katejātaraṇiḥ*, which are sung as the fourteenth and fifteenth [stotras] in the *anugāna*. For the three ṛcs, Praskaṇva is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), and Sūrya is the deity (*devatā*). For the two *sāmans*, Indra is the seer; for the ṛg-verses, the meter and the deity are as stated above. (181–3 + 34)

In the three *ṛks* beginning with "Uddyāmeṣi rajaḥ," "Ayukta sapta śundhyuvaḥ," and "Sapta tvā harito rathe," there are two *paridhisāmans*, namely "Kasatyā uddyāmeṣi" and "Kaṛtā uddyāmeṣi," which are sung as the sixteenth and seventeenth [stotras] in the *anugāna*. Praskaṇva is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of the *ṛcs*; the *gāyatrī* is the meter; Sūrya is the deity. For the two *sāmans*, Indra is the seer; the *ṛk* itself is the meter and the deity. (184–6 + 34)
Then follows the eighteen-fold *ekānugāna* beginning with "vāṅ manaḥ prāṇa" and ending with "staubhikaṃ pitryam"; its seers are the Seasons (*ṛtavaḥ*), and its deity is Sūrya. ||186+35||

Then, upon this verse, "He moves within the luminous realm" (*antaścarati rocanā*), there is the nineteenth *anugāna*, preceded by the *stobha*: "He shines among the gods" (*antardeveṣu rocase*). The verse "He moves within the luminous realm" belongs to Sarparājñī; the seers of the verse are the Serpent Kings (*sarparājānaḥ*); the seers of the *sāman* are the Fathers (*pitaraḥ*); the meter is *gāyatrī*; and the deity is as in the verse. || 187 + 35 ||

Beginning with "Speech and Mind" and ending with "The Light of the Gods and so forth," this constitutes one *sāman*. According to the school of Śāṇḍilīputra, this is the twenty-first *anugāna*; according to the school of Vārṣāyaṇīputra, it is the nineteenth *anugāna*. However, according to the latter school, there are two *anugānas*: the eighteenth and the nineteenth.

Then, from these two verses, *ud u tyam* and *citram*, there is a single twenty-one-fold *anugāna*: *kabhrājā ud u tyam jā citram*. The second *atiṣaṅga* is *hāu hāu hāu bhrājā bhrājā*; this they call "the hearing of Mitra and Varuṇa. (The seer of the verse *ud u tyam* is Praskaṇva; the metre is *gāyatrī*; the deity is Agni. The seer of the verse *citram* is Kutsa Āṅgirasa; the metre is *triṣṭubh*; the deity is Sūrya. The seers of the *sāman* are Mitra and Varuṇa.)

The *Ṛk* is "ud u tyam" and the *Chandas* is *Devatā*. Then, from these two *ṛcs*, "ud u tyam" and "indraṃ naro," the third *atīṣaṅga* is "kabhrājā ud u tyam jā indraṃ naro"; this is the twenty-second *anugāna*. That is called "the head of Indra. For the *ṛc* "ud u tyam," Praskaṇva Kāṇva is the *ṛṣi*; *Gāyatrī* is the *chandas*; Indra is the *devatā*. For the *ṛc* "indraṃ naro," Vasiṣṭha is the *ṛṣi*; *Triṣṭubh* is the *chandas*; Indra is the *devatā*. For the *Sāman*, Indra is the *ṛṣi*; Sūrya is the *devatā*. || 188–9 + 35 ||

Then there is one *augāna* chant called *unnayāmi*, which belongs to the *staubhika* class. It is the rising (*unnaya*) of the Sun; therefore, they call it "the Solar" (*āditya*). The Sun is both the seer (*ṛṣi*) and the deity (*devatā*) of this *sāman*. ||189+36||
Thus ends the third section in the Śukriya-parvan of the Āraṇyaka-gāna. ||3||
The Śukriya section is completed.

Now follows the section called Śakvarī (as a supplement): *vidā maghavan* is one *sāman*. *vidā maghavan vidā* is one *ṛc*; *vidā rāye suvīryam* is the next; *indraṃ dhanasya sātaye* is the last. Upon these [verses], *evidāmaghavan-evidārāye—(e)indraṃdhanasya* is one *sāman*. These very ones are designated as the *simāḥ*, the *śakkarī*s, and the *maḍḍiṇyāḥ mahānāmnyaḥ*. Regarding the *ṛc*s, Indra, Prajāpati, Viṣṇu, or Viśvāmitra is the *ṛṣi*. The *śakkarī* is the meter (*chandas*). Indra is the deity (*devatā*).

These Śakvarī verses are interwoven with both Śākvara and non-Śākvara feet, and they are joined with five *purīṣa* feet. Indra is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of these Sāmans; their meters and deities are the same as those of the *ṛc*s. All the *purīṣa* feet belong exclusively to Indra. Thus, Indra is addressed as the controller of all those [feet] and as the embodiment of the strength of all the gods.
The section known as the Śakvarī is completed.
Thus ends the *Sāmavedārṣeyadīpa*, composed by the illustrious Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara, the preeminent among sacrificial priests.
